questions.prompt: To obtain an easement by prescription, one must:
questions.explanation: Prescriptive easements are obtainable after using the property for five years. One does not need to occupy the property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the largest parcel of land?
questions.explanation:
Choice (A): 10% of a township = 3.6 sections or 3.6 square miles

Choice (B): 2 sections = 2 square miles or 55,756,800 sq. ft.

Choice (D): 5,280' x 10,560' also equals 55,756,800 sq. ft.

Choice (C): 4 square miles is the largest parcel of land.

questions.prompt: A power granted by an enabling act refers to:
questions.explanation: Zoning is the regulation of structures and uses of property within designated districts or zones. Zoning regulates and affects such things as use of the land, lot sizes, types of structure permitted, building heights, setbacks and density. Counties and/or municipalities generally enact their own zoning ordinances pursuant to an enabling act of the state.

questions.prompt: Prescription most nearly pertains to:
questions.explanation: Prescription is a term usually applied to easements. We refer to easements by prescription.

questions.prompt: A lien imposed by court action would be:
questions.explanation: A lien imposed by court action is considered a judgment. Once it is recorded, it creates a general lien on all property of the debtor in the county in which it was recorded.

questions.prompt: The most important test of a fixture is:
questions.explanation: The intention of the parties, particularly the intention of the person attaching it usually governs.

questions.prompt: Tenants in common have equal right of:
questions.explanation: Tenancy in common is a form of concurrent ownership where two or more persons hold separate legal title in the same property through the unity of possession. This means that each co-owner has an undivided fractional interest in the land and a right to use the whole property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of involuntary alienation?
questions.explanation: Involuntary alienation takes place when property is sold against the owner's will.

questions.prompt: Archer, Baker and Charles hold title to real property in joint tenancy. If Archer were to die:
choices: Baker and Charles remain joint tenants.
Baker and Charles become tenants in common.
Baker and Charles acquire Archer's interest by succession.
Baker and Charles become tenants in common with Archer's wife.
questions.explanation: Upon the death of Archer, Archer's 1/3 interest passes to Baker and Charles, who are still joint tenants with each holding a 1/2 interest.

questions.prompt: Smith and Jones own property as joint tenants. Jones, without Smith's knowledge or consent, encumbers his interest by borrowing $10,000. Before making any payments on the loan, Jones dies. Smith now owns the property:
choices: totally, but subject to the $10,000 loan.
with the mortgagee as joint tenants.
in severalty and without liability for the mortgage.
with the mortgagee as tenants in common.
questions.explanation: If one joint tenant dies, the surviving joint tenant becomes the sole owner of the property and is not liable to the creditors of the deceased who hold unforeclosed liens on the joint tenant's interest in the property.

questions.prompt: A township contains:
questions.explanation: A township is 6 miles square and contains 36 sections.

questions.prompt: Deed restrictions based on race are:
questions.explanation: Deed restrictions based on race have no effect, whatsoever.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT appurtenant to real estate?
questions.explanation: Appurtenant means belonging to, adjunctive, appended or annexed to. For example, the garage is appurtenant to the house, and the common interest in the common elements of a condominium is appurtenant to each apartment. Appurtenant items "run with the land" when the property is transferred. Trade fixtures do not transfer with the property.

questions.prompt: Mark gives a life estate to Charlie. Mark's interest is:
questions.explanation: Mark's interest reverts back to him after the death of Charlie.

questions.prompt: An "S" corporation:
choices: passes tax liability through to shareholders.
questions.explanation: With an "S" corporation, taxable income and net losses are passed through to the corporation's shareholders. Double taxation at the corporate level is thus avoided.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT necessary to establish title by adverse possession?
choices: Possession open and notorious for five years
Against the true wishes of the owner
questions.explanation:
There are five requirements to acquire title by adverse possession:

The possession must be by actual occupation and be open and notoroius.

It must be hostile to the true owner's title.

It must be under claim of right or color of title.

Possession must be continuous and uninterrupted for a period of five years.

Claimant must have paid all real property taxes levied and assessed for a period of five years continuously.

questions.prompt: The Section East of Section 36 is:
questions.explanation: Section 31 of the adjoining Township is East of Section 36.

questions.prompt: Among the principles involved in the "Bundle of Rights" is the right to:
questions.explanation: The Bundle of Rights theory claims that ownership of a parcel of real estate embraces a great many rights, such as the right to Possess, Encumber, Will and Sell. Study aid: PEWS

questions.prompt: An interest in real property acquired by prescription is:
choices: the right to use another's land.
questions.explanation: Adverse possession refers to land while prescription is a term usually applied to easements. We speak of title by adverse possession and easements by prescription. An easement by prescription creates a right to use someone else's land.

questions.prompt: Rights of ownership include everything EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The rights of ownership include the exclusive right to possess, encumber, will and sell. Also included is the right to give the property away (gift). Not the right of eminent domain.

questions.prompt: A group of neighbors had pleaded with their neighbor Mr. Brown to stop burning garbage on his property. They finally obtained a court order to stop him from continuing to do so. This court order would be known as a(n):
questions.explanation: An injunction is a legal action whereby a court issues a writ that forbids a party defendant from doing some act or compels the defendant to perform an act. An injunction requires the person to whom it is directed to refrain from doing a particular thing, such as violating deed restrictions or house rules prohibiting pets.

questions.prompt: A court order prohibiting an act from being done is a(n):
questions.explanation: An injunction is an order or decree of a court of equity prohibiting some act or compelling an act to be done.

questions.prompt: The insects that are considered to be the most destructive to wood are:
questions.explanation: One of the most damaging types of termites is the dry-wood termite. Also look for subterranean termite as a possible answer on the state exam.

questions.prompt: Personal property can never:
questions.explanation: Personal property sometimes becomes real property when it is affixed to real property. It can be hypothecated, as when a person borrows on a car and hypothecates the title. It can be alienated or conveyed to someone else.

questions.prompt: To determine ownership, what is the court action taken?
questions.explanation: Quiet title action is a court action intended to establish or settle the title to a particular property, especially where there is a cloud on the title. All parties with a possible claim or interest in the property must be joined in the action. A quiet title action is frequently used by an adverse possessor to substantiate the title, because having official record title makes it easier to market the property. Once the judgment or decree of the court has been recorded, proper record notice of the claimant's right and interest in the property is established.

questions.prompt: Freehold estate includes:
questions.explanation:
The distinctive characteristic of the freehold estate is that they endure for an interminable duration. Thus, freehold estates consist of:

(1) Estates in fee:
     a. Absolute
     b. Qualified-by condition or limitation

(2) Life Estates

questions.prompt: Mr. Friedman purchased real property on which there was an old home. He removed the run down home and had the lot graded. He immediately obtained a construction loan secured by a deed of trust. During the construction period, a painter who had not been paid filed a mechanic's lien. Which of the following is correct?
choices: The mechanic's lien takes priority over the trust deed because the priority dates back to when the construction actually began.
The trust deed takes priority because it was recorded before completion of construction.
The trust deed takes priority because it was recorded prior to the mechanic's lien.
Mechanic's liens always take priority over trust deeds.
questions.explanation: Since the improvements began prior to recordation of the trust deed, all materials and labor contributors have priority over the trust deed.

questions.prompt: A mechanic's lien has advantages over the other types of liens in that:
choices: it has priority over recorded trust deeds.
it has priority over certain other types of liens.
its effective date is the date work commenced.
its effective date would normally be prior to the recording date.
questions.explanation: The effective date of a mechanic's lien is the date of commencement of work rather than the filing date. This would give them priority over subsequently recorded liens.

questions.prompt: Taylor was injured while swimming in Smith's new pool. Taylor obtained a $2,500 judgment against Smith and recorded an abstract of judgment with the county recorder. The type of lien imposed was:
questions.explanation: A judgment lien is a general lien.

questions.prompt: The vertical structural support members are attached to the:
questions.explanation: The vertical structural support members (studs) are nailed to the horizontal plate (sole plate) which is attached to the subfloor.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements regarding deed restrictions is TRUE?
choices: A covenant is generally more severe than a condition.
To be legally enforced, a private restriction must promote public health, safety, and welfare.
The term "covenant" is an all-inclusive word embracing both restrictions and conditions.
A violation of a condition is more severe than a covenant and might result in the loss of title.
questions.explanation: Violation of a covenant may result in an injunction (court order to stop doing something) and monetary damages. Violation of a condition may result in loss of title which is more severe than an injunction.

questions.prompt: A, B, and C are co-owners of real property in joint tenancy. C sells his interest to D and shortly thereafter, dies. If C had also executed a will, leaving all of his property to his sole heir (whom we shall call E), title to the property would vest as:
choices: A and B as joint tenants, together with D a tenant in common.
A and B as joint tenants, together with E a tenant in common.
A, B, and D as tenants in common.
A and B as joint tenants.
questions.explanation: It is the right of any joint tenant to sell his share during ownership. In the example, the sale created a tenancy in common between D and the other joint tenants. The death of C had no effect as he died after the transfer.

questions.prompt: The rights of a landowner whose property line touches on a non-navigable river or flowing stream are called:
questions.explanation: Riparian rights are the rights of an abutting owner to his/her fair share of water flowing past the land.

questions.prompt: If a client asks how they should take title, the broker should say:
questions.explanation: The question of how to take title should be referred to an attorney.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes an estate of inheritance?
questions.explanation: An estate of inheritance is a fee simple estate handed down by will.

questions.prompt: Partition action refers to:
choices: court action to break up joint tenants.
questions.explanation: Partition action refers to a court proceeding to divide the interests of co-tenants.

questions.prompt: An agreement to sell community real property, signed by one spouse only is:
questions.explanation: Neither spouse alone can sell community real property.

questions.prompt: In real estate, the word "tenancy" means:
choices: two or more people joined in an enterprise.
a mode or method of holding title to real property.
questions.explanation: Tenancy means a method, mode or means of holding title by a lessee or owner.

questions.prompt: The act of joining or uniting one thing to another, as in attaching personal property to real property thereby creating a fixture is called:
questions.explanation: Annexation is an addition to property by the act of joining or uniting one thing to another, as in attaching personal property to real property thereby creating a fixture. For Example, a sink becomes a fixture when it is annexed to the plumbing outlet.

questions.prompt: Which of the following DOES NOT "go with the land?"
questions.explanation: An easement in gross attaches personally to the owner, not to the land.

questions.prompt: The difference between a judgment lien and a mechanic's lien is:
choices: mechanic's liens may take priority earlier than the date they are recorded.
judgment liens are not enforceable until recorded.
mechanic's liens are created by statute.
questions.explanation: The effective date of a mechanic's lien is the date the work began on the property. A judgment becomes effective and takes priority when it is recorded.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is neither a lien nor an encumbrance?
questions.explanation: An encumbrance is an interest or right in real property which diminishes the value of the fee, but does not prevent conveyance by the owner. A lien is a type of encumbrance that creates a charge against property, whereby the property is used as security for the payment of a debt, referred to as attachment liens (e.g.; trust deeds, taxes, judgments, etc.) Restrictions, easements, and reservations are encumbrances but not liens. Remember, all liens are encumbrances, but not all encumbrances are liens.

questions.prompt: Adams has an easement over Baker's property. Adams leaves town for 21 years. When he returns, does he still have an easement over Baker's land?
choices: No, because he was gone 20 years.
Yes, he still has the easement right, since he was not gone over 30 years.
Yes, Adams still has the easement.
No, because Adams abandoned the easement.
questions.explanation: A granted easement does not "expire" through nonuse, only a prescriptive easement can be lost through nonuse.

questions.prompt: An easement by prescription may be lost by:
choices: merger of ownership between the dominant and servient tenements.
express release by the holder of the dominant tenement.
questions.explanation: A prescriptive easement may be lost by nonuse for five years, or from express release by a quitclaim deed signed by the holder of the dominant tenement, or by mutual agreement of the parties.

questions.prompt: A roof which slopes upward from all four sides and joins at the ridge is called a:
questions.explanation: See diagrams.

questions.prompt: The eave of your neighbor's new house hangs six inches over your land. This describes a(n):
questions.explanation: An encroachment is an unauthorized invasion or intrusion of an improvement or other real property onto another's property.

questions.prompt: Ingress and egress apply to:
questions.explanation: The term ingress and egress are associated with the word access. To ingress means to go upon the land and to egress means to exit or leave the land.

questions.prompt: Insulation materials are rated by their effectiveness according to their "R-value." The rating system is used to rate the material's:
questions.explanation: The R-value rating system is used to measure a material's resistance to the flow of heat.

questions.prompt: CC&R's are found in:
questions.explanation: CC&R's are found in deeds.

questions.prompt: All of the following are factors considered when determining whether an item of personal property has become real property, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fixtures are items of personal property which have become attached to real property, thus becoming real property. The five tests of a fixture are: Method of attachment, Agreement of the parties, Relationship of the parties, Intention of the person attaching it, Adaptability of the item. Study aid: "MARIA"

questions.prompt: Emblements refer to:
questions.explanation: Vegetable chattels called "emblements" are the crops of the earth produced annually, not spontaneously, by labor and industry.

questions.prompt: A person who held a life estate leased the property for five years and then died. The new owners ordered the lessee to move out. The lease was:
choices: invalid unless the deceased's executor confirmed it.
questions.explanation: The holder of the life estate could only lease what he had which was the use of the property until he died.

questions.prompt: Conditions differ from covenants in which of the following ways?
choices: Covenants cannot be created by grant.
Conditions can only be created by grant.
Only covenants restrict the use of the land.
questions.explanation: A condition is a qualification of a grant of estate and can only be imposed at the time of the grant. A covenant, however, can be imposed at another time by mutual agreement. Both conditions and covenants can "run with the land."

questions.prompt: One man transferred title to a house with a condition that no alcoholic beverages would be sold on the premises. The estate created is known as a(n):
questions.explanation: A fee simple defeasible estate is created to exist only until the occurrence or non-occurrence of a particular event. This question describes a defeasible estate with a condition subsequent. If the condition is breached, the estate can revert to the grantor either automatically or by court action.

questions.prompt: A brother and sister CANNOT hold property as:
questions.explanation: Community property ownership requires marriage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT considered dry-wall construction?
questions.explanation: Dry wall construction is any type of masonry work laid up without the use of mortar. It is the type of interior wall construction where finished material is used (other than plaster), such as wood paneling, plywood, plasterboard, or other types of wall board.

questions.prompt: In what year did the requirement for disclosure of lead based paint in dwelling units become effective?
questions.explanation: Lead based paint laws went into effect in 1996. The law applies to owners, lessors, and real estate licensees. This law requires the owner or lessor of dwelling units built before 1978 to provide the buyer or lessee with the federal booklet entitled "Protect Your Family from Lead in Your Home."

questions.prompt: Potable means:
questions.explanation: Potable means drinkable (safely and agreeably used for drinking).

questions.prompt: As spelled out in her deceased husband's will, Colleen can collect the rents from an apartment building for her lifetime, after which the apartment building goes to their church. Colleen holds a:
questions.explanation: Colleen has a life estate with the remainder interest held by the church.

questions.prompt: Which of the following "runs with the land?"
questions.explanation: The key to this question is the word "appurtenant" which means belonging to; attached; appended; or annexed to. An appurtenant easement is a right to use adjoining property that transfers with the land. It is attached to and belongs with this superior right of possession of the dominant estate, passing as incident to it and incapable of existence separate and apart from such possession. Appurtenant items "run with the land" when the property is transferred.

questions.prompt: A property is owned by two persons in joint tenancy. Which of the following actions could destroy the joint tenancy?
choices: Foreclosure against one of the parties to the joint tenancy.
One of the joint tenants places a deed of trust against his/her interest.
One joint tenant wills his/her interest to another.
Judgment and writ of execution are awarded.
questions.explanation:
There are four unities to a joint tenancy.

Study aid: "TTIP"
TIME: That the co-owners became such at the same time.
TITLE: Created by a single will or transfer.
INTEREST: Equal shares.
POSSESSION: A right to use the whole and share in the profits and costs. Foreclosure breaks two of the unities: Time and Title.

questions.prompt: All of the following are considered less-than-freehold estates EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A life estate is considered a freehold estate.

questions.prompt: The building up of new soil adjacent to a river is called:
questions.explanation: Accretion is the process by which fine material, such as sand or mud, is carried by water and deposited on land. Accretion is the process - alluvium is the material that builds up.

questions.prompt: A builder was going to build a home on a 75' x 125' lot, and wanted it to fit in relation to its surroundings. This placement would be known as:
questions.explanation: Orientation is the placing or positioning of a structure on its lot with regard to exposure to the sun, prevailing winds, privacy, and protection from noise.

questions.prompt: The holder of a life estate can do all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A life estate only exists for the life of its owner or the life of some other designated person.

questions.prompt: What may the tenant do with fixtures in an industrial property?
choices: remove or leave at the choice of the lessor
questions.explanation: Trade fixtures are pieces of property that a tenant affixes to a leased building or land for the purpose of conducting business. Trade fixtures differ from other fixtures in that they may be removed from the real estate (even if attached) at the end of the tenancy of the business, while ordinary fixtures attached to the real estate become part of the real estate. The business tenant must compensate the owner for any damages due to removal of trade fixtures or repair such damage. Remember, the lessee (tenant) pays rent to the lessor (landlord).

questions.prompt: The liability of a limited partner for business debts is limited to:
choices: the same as the general partners.
any amount agreed to in the partnership agreement.
the amount of the debts equally divided among all the partners.
questions.explanation: Limited partners are not responsible for the firm's debts beyond their investment. At least one partner in such a firm must be a general partner with unlimited liability.

questions.prompt: Where there is a conflict between local building codes and the State Housing Act, which will prevail?
choices: Local building codes in unincorporated areas
Local building codes, since they are more specific than the State Housing Act
The one with the highest safety standards
questions.explanation: Usually when there is a conflict, you must follow the most restrictive. Since you cannot tell which is more restrictive, you must follow the law with highest safety standards.

questions.prompt: An attachment is:
questions.explanation: An attachment is classified as a lien.

questions.prompt: What kind of architectural style has lots of large windows, an open plan, easy access to outside, simplicity?
questions.explanation: Contemporary architectural design is generally one story; usually plat or low pitched roof; often on concrete slab; large amount of glass; and indoor/outdoor living.

questions.prompt: A general contractor hired a subcontractor to install the hardwood floors in a home under construction. If the subcontractor had to file a mechanic's lien in order to get paid, the mechanic's lien would date back to the date:
choices: work began on the hardwood floors.
work was completed on the hardwood floors.
questions.explanation: A mechanics' lien dates back in priority to the beginning of any work on the project, not the date the individual mechanic performs his labor.

questions.prompt: Soil pipe is usually used for:
questions.explanation: Soil pipe is the pipe that carries waste from the house to the sewer in the street.

questions.prompt: Subdivisions are controlled by:
choices: the city in which the subdivision is located.
the Department of Housing and Urban Development.
the California Department of Business Oversight.
questions.explanation: One of the two major laws that regulate subdivisions in California is the Subdivision Map Act. The purpose of this act is to develop a subdivision filing procedure to be followed at the city or county level and to make sure that subdividers comply with a city's or county's master plan. Cities and counties have the legal authority to enact subdivision ordinances. This gives them control over what type and size subdivisions may be built and the physical aspects of the subdivisions such as the streets, sidewalks, sewers, recreational areas, and flood control.

questions.prompt: Which of the following liens covers all the property of a person?
questions.explanation: General liens apply to all the licenee's real and personal property.

questions.prompt: The word "percolation" refers to:
questions.explanation: Percolation refers to the returning of water to the land. It results in the recharging of the underground water system called the "water table."

questions.prompt: When subdividers evaluate the topography of land,
choices: hillside topography property is less desirable than flat mainstream property.
questions.explanation: Topography is a graphic representation of the surface features or contour of a place or region on a map, indicating their relative positions and elevations. Flat land is cheaper and easier to build on. The subdivider can build more homes on flat land compared to hillside land.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements concerning deed restrictions is correct?
choices: A covenant includes conditions and equitable servitudes.
A violation of a condition can result in forfeiture of title to real property.
Private restricitons must be for public health, safety, and general welfare.
Covenants are more restrictive and costly for the owner than conditions.
questions.explanation: A condition is any fact or event which, if it occurs or fails to occur, automatically creates or extinguishes a legal obligation. If a condition is violated, the owner may be forced to forfeit the title. A covenant is only a promise. If a person fails to adhere to a covenant, it will result in a cause of action for damages, but will not automatically extinguish the owner's title.

questions.prompt: A grant deed that conveys title to real property without limitation is called a:
questions.explanation: A fee simple estate is the maximum possible estate one can possess in real property. It is the least limited interest and the most complete and absolute ownership.

questions.prompt: What is considered real property?
choices: stock in a mutual water company
questions.explanation: Stock in a mutual water company is appurtenant to the land, therefore it is considered part of the real property and would transfer when the property is sold. Crops growing in the ground are always considered real property while in the ground. Ownership of the crops could be in question, but not the fact that they are real property while still growing.

questions.prompt: To hold real property as tenants in common, the individuals must:
questions.explanation: Whenever two or more people hold title to property together, they must hold an undivided interest. If you own 1/3 of the property, you CANNOT designate which 1/3.

questions.prompt: Easements are:
questions.explanation: An easement is not a lien but would always be considered an encumbrance.

questions.prompt: "A" sells a farm to "B". Crops are growing on the farm. "A" wants to harvest the crops. Who owns the crops?
questions.explanation: Emblements are regarded as personal property even before harvest; thus, a seller or tenant has the right to take the annual crop resulting from his/her labor, even if the harvest does not occur until after the sale or tenancy. Therefore, "A" has the right to re-enter the land to harvest any crops he/she had grown.

questions.prompt: When the local building authority permits an inconsistency to the construction, systems, or standards within applicable building codes, it is referred to as a(n):
questions.explanation: A variance is an exception to the zoning law.

questions.prompt: Concerning deed restrictions, which of the following is TRUE?
choices: Deed restrictions may be creatd by developers.
questions.explanation: All of these are true with regard to restrictions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a fixture?
questions.explanation: Fixtures are items of personal property which have become attached to real property, thus becoming real property. Of these choices the only one which is permanently fixed to the land (incorporated into the land) are the new ceiling fans.

questions.prompt: A property owner intends to build an addition onto the back of his house. He should check:
questions.explanation: A property owner should check all of these.

questions.prompt: After paying his general contractor in full, a property owner files a notice of completion. Which of the following is correct?
choices: Mechanic's liens may not be filed.
A notice of nonresponsibility must be filed to protect the owner.
As long as work has not stopped, workers may file mechanic's liens.
Unpaid workers can file mechanic's liens up to 30 days after the owner files a notice of completion.
questions.explanation: A notice of completion is filed to give public notice that a construction job has been completed and that mechanic's liens must be filed within 30 days. California's deadline to file a mechanics lien is 90 days after the completion of the project. However, the owner can SHORTEN the deadline by filing a if a notice of completion within 30 days of the completion of the project. When such a notice is filed, the deadline to file a mechanic's lien is shortened to 30 days from the date the notice was filed.

questions.prompt: The technical definition of real property includes:
choices: the right to possess and use to the exclusion of others.
questions.explanation: In the strict legal sense, real property includes land, appurtenances, that which is affixed to the land, and that which by law is immovable.

questions.prompt: What is dispossession?
questions.explanation: Dispossession is the eviction of someone (such as a tenant) from the possession of land by process of law. A landlord seeking to evict a tenant can file suit for dispossession.

questions.prompt: A contract for the sale of rural property requires a:
questions.explanation: Some property, such as rural, undeveloped land cannot be identified by a street address. The best practice is to use a complete legal description. Most parcels of land are defined by one of three methods of legal description: lot and block, rectangular survey system, and metes and bounds.

questions.prompt: When a governmental body takes private land for public use, it is accomplished through the right of:
questions.explanation: Eminent domain is the right of the government (such as a city or county), to take private property for necessary public use with just compensation paid to the owner.

questions.prompt: A form of business organization in which the co-owners are fully liable for the company's debts is:
questions.explanation: All the owners are general partners and share a full liability for the debts and obligations of the partnership.

questions.prompt: Artificial monuments are:
questions.explanation: A monument is a visible marker, either a natural or artifical object set by the government or surveyors, used to establish the lines and boundaries of a survey. Streets and canals are both manmade.

questions.prompt: Which of the following most accurately describes a joint tenancy estate?
questions.explanation: A joint tenancy estate requires two or more people; and therefore, could not be in severalty.

questions.prompt: A flood hazard exists when an area floods:
choices: more than twice in ten years.
questions.explanation: A flood hazard is an area which floods more than twice in ten years.

questions.prompt: Who of the following may file a valid mechanic's lien?
questions.explanation: A mechanic's lien exists in favor of every person who contributes to the work of improvement. The Civil Code covers all mechanics (skilled workers), materialmen, contractors, subcontractors, lessors of equipment, artisans, architects, registered engineers, licensed land surveyors, machinists, builders, teamsters, and truck drivers.

questions.prompt: When referring to his development, a contractor mentions his elevation sheet. He is referring to:
choices: reinforcing steel rods in the side walls of the building.
the inside dimensions of each room.
the building and site relative to other sites.
questions.explanation: Elevations show the exterior sides of a building as it appears after all structural work has been completed. Views are often identified as front, rear, left, and right elevation. Symbols on elevation drawings indicate the kind of exterior materials, their placement and the height of their construction.

questions.prompt: Deed restrictions are created by:
questions.explanation: Deed restrictions (CC&R's) are created by grantors in their deeds.

questions.prompt: What is the unutilized space between the floor and ground of a structure called?
questions.explanation: The minimum required crawl space is 18". This is measured from the ground level to the bottom of the floor joists. (See construction terms)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true regarding the separate rights of tenants in common?
choices: Each owner has the right to possession of the entire property.
One owner cannot institute an action in court to divide the property.
One owner cannot convey his/her interest without the consent of the others.
One owner can exclude the other owners from possessing any of the property.
questions.explanation: Each owner in a tenancy in common has the right to possession of the entire property. Choice (D) is incorrect for this reason: Each of the owners can sell their interest without the consent of the others and anyone can sue for partition action.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are ways in which the government has control over real property?
questions.explanation: There are many government controls (i.e., building codes, zoning, Subdivision Map Act). The VA and FHA exert control by requiring minimum property requirements before guaranteeing or insuring loans. The real estate commissioner has the authority to approve new subdivisions.

questions.prompt: The framing members over windows and doors are called:
questions.explanation: A header is a framing member over an opening in a wall. The most common are those over windows and doorways which serve to transfer the load. (See construction terms)

questions.prompt: The term "walk-up" refers to a(n):
questions.explanation: The term "walk-up" usually refers to three or more story apartment buildings with no elevation.

questions.prompt: The seizure of property prior to a judgment is known as:
questions.explanation: An attachment is the process by which real or personal property of a defendant in a lawsuit is seized and retained in the custody of the law for satisfaction of the judgment.

questions.prompt: If a corporation buys property and takes title in its corporate name, it may hold title:
questions.explanation: If a corporation takes title in its name only, no co-owners may exist (in severalty).

questions.prompt: Joint tenancy and tenancy in common both share the unity of:
choices: the right to pass title by will.
questions.explanation: Both tenants in common and joint tenants hold an undivided interest in real property through the unity of possession.

questions.prompt: A limited partner may:
choices: use his or her name in the partnership.
request an accounting from the partnership.
act as CEO of the partnership.
questions.explanation: Limited partners are usually passive investors that share in the profits, but do not actively participate in its management or operation.

questions.prompt: Identifying property as "personal" or "real" can be difficult because personal property can:
questions.explanation: Identifying property as "personal" or "real" is complicated by the fact that personal property can become real property. The emphasis of this question is why it can be difficult to identify property as real or personal so (c) is the correct answer, not (d).

questions.prompt: A completion bond would be for the protection of the:
questions.explanation: Some lenders require an owner to provide a completion bond assuring the lender that the development will be completed whether or not the owner pays the contractor.

questions.prompt: A beam placed across openings for doors, windows to support the load from the structure above is called a:
questions.explanation: A lintel is a horizontal support of timber, stone, concrete, or steel across the top of a door or window to support the load from the structure above.

questions.prompt: A property owner, whose house is located next to the landing strip of a small airport, successfully sued and received judgment against the airport, forcing them to buy his house. This is known as:
questions.explanation: Inverse condemnation is an action brought by a person whose property has been effectively taken, substantially interfered with, or taken without just compensation.

questions.prompt: The designation "M" on a zoning map would stand for:
questions.explanation: The zoning designation "M" generally stands for manufacturing.

questions.prompt: The best way to test for radon gas in a building is with a:
questions.explanation: A spectrometer is a scientific device that detects alpha particles that are emitted by radon gas and is considered to be highly reliable.

questions.prompt: Acquisition of property by its incorporation with other property is known as:
questions.explanation: Accession is the acquisition of title to additional land or to improvements as a result of the annexation of fixtures or as a result of alluvial deposits along the banks of streams by accretion.

questions.prompt: The person most likely to use a "bench mark" in his/her profession would be a:
questions.explanation: A bench mark is an identification symbol on stone, metal, or other durable matter permanently fixed to the ground from which differences of elevation are measured, such as tidal observations or topographical surveys.

questions.prompt: All of the following are ways government controls the use of land EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A number of restrictions on land are a result of actions by the government. Many restrictions, however, are created by land developers. Such devices take several forms and can be either positive or negative in nature. They include defeasible fees, easements, equitable servitudes, and restrictive covenants.

questions.prompt: Under a lease, the leasehold interest lies in the:
questions.explanation: A leasehold interest is the right to exclusive possession and use of real property for a fixed period of time held by the lessee (tenant).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a "less than freehold estate?"
questions.explanation: A less than freehold estate is an estate in possession generally referred to as a leasehold. Such interests exist for a definite period of time or successive periods of time until termination by notice.

questions.prompt: A mechanic's lien filed today would undoubtedly take precedence over:
choices: an unrecorded deed delivered last week.
a tax lien to be filed tomorrow.
questions.explanation: A mechanic's lien dates back to the commencement of work. It does have precedence over deeds whether they are delivered or recorded.

questions.prompt: An acre is:
questions.explanation: One acre contains 43,560 square feet. All equal one acre.

questions.prompt: Who of the following generally installs conduit?
questions.explanation: Conduit is usually a metal pipe in which electrical wiring is installed.

questions.prompt: A negative declaration would indicate:
choices: a negative influence of the development on the environment.
no significant influence of the development on the environment.
a developer's poor financial status to protect purchasers.
questions.explanation: Environmental Impact Reports (EIR) may be required by local government prior to approval of the map for a subdivision. If it is determined that the proposal will NOT have a potentially significant adverse affect, the city or county prepares a negative declaration prior to making a decision on the development.

questions.prompt: Joan Black owned property in severalty as a single woman. She later married and owned the property under her married name, Joan Redding. This may be confusing in the future because:
choices: it will create a cloud on the title.
it may cause the property to automatically become community property.
it automatically creates a joint tenancy.
it may jeopardize her ownership rights.
questions.explanation: This creates a cloud on the title. It can be cleared by Joan producing her marriage certificate or other proof that she is the same person.

questions.prompt: Riparian rights are best described as:
questions.explanation: Riparian rights are the rights held in common with other riparian owners to make reasonable use of the waters that flow on, under or adjacent to a property, provided such use does not alter the flow of water or contaminate the water.

questions.prompt: Corn crops are harvested once-a-year. Which theory applies?
questions.explanation: The "doctrine of constructive severance" states that when growing crops (emblements) are sold or mortgaged, they are considered separated from the land (severed), even though they have not been severed from the land. If constructively severed, they would not transfer with the sale of the land.

questions.prompt: If three different buyers take title to real property as joint tenants, there would be:
questions.explanation: With a joint tenancy ownership, only one title exists.

questions.prompt: Local governments are authorized to create Community Redevelopment Agencies (CRA's) for the purpose of correcting blighted conditions and to expand the supply of low and moderate income housing within their jurisdiction. By law, CRA's must set aside a portion of the tax revenue increases generated by the higher valuation created by their development projects in a special fund. The name of this fund is the:
choices: Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund.
questions.explanation: The bonds issued by a redevelopment agency are secured by future, anticipated property tax revenues. This procedure which is called tax incremental financing, allows the CRA to receive any increases in project area property taxes that are a direct result of the CRA's development activities. The monies that must be set aside, however to retire these bonds must be placed in a legally required Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund.

questions.prompt: Which of the following zoning classifications would permit the construction of a tri-plex (multi-family residential dwelling)?
questions.explanation: Multi-family residential (tri-plex) would be R-3. "A" designates agricultural zoning.

questions.prompt: The parallel framing members under the flooring boards and in the ceiling are called:
questions.explanation: A joist is a heavy piece of horizontal timber to which the boards of a floor or the lath of a ceiling are nailed. Joists are laid edgewise to form the floor support. (See construction terms)

questions.prompt: By conveying less than his fee estate, the grantor retains a:
questions.explanation: Reversion is the estate remaining in the grantor who has conveyed a lesser estate from the original.

questions.prompt: What is the closest measurement in linear feet of the sides of a square, one acre parcel of land?
questions.explanation: One acre = 43,560 square feet. Using the Length x Width = Area formula, the closest answer is 208 linear feet. 208 x 208 = 43,264 sq. ft. (closest to 43,560).

questions.prompt: A parcel of land known as the servient tenement:
choices: is the property benefited by the easement.
has an easement appurtenant attached thereto.
loses its status upon transfer of title.
is the property burdened by the easement.
questions.explanation: The servient tenement is the property burdened by the easement.

questions.prompt: Who develops deed restrictions?
questions.explanation: CC&R's are commonly found in the Declaration of Restrictions filed by the developer in a subdivision plan.

questions.prompt: The metal used by builders to prevent the seepage of water at certain joints in buildings is known as:
questions.explanation: Flashing serves as protection against water entering the building framework at valleys in the roof and at other critical joints between the roof and wall sections. Flashing is usually made of galvanized steel. (See construction terms)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is false regarding a "fee estate?"
questions.explanation: Fee estates are of indefinite duration.

questions.prompt: Because of roofing regulations regarding load factor:
choices: builders are spacing roofing rafters closer together.
questions.explanation: Placing rafters closer together strengthens a roof.

questions.prompt: When water is returned to the water table by the process known as "percolation," the water belongs to:
questions.explanation: In California, the landowner has only a right in common with other owners to take his/her share of the water for beneficial use.

questions.prompt: Before damming or diverting water, a landowner must have permission from:
questions.explanation: This is for the protection of the general public.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is always required in joint tenancy ownership of real property?
choices: Equal shares of interest in the property by each of the joint tenants.
questions.explanation: The four unities must be present for the existence of a joint tenancy: Time, Title, Interest, and Possession. TTIP

questions.prompt: All of the following are reasons to conduct a soil study EXCEPT:
choices: See if soil must be exported or imported
questions.explanation: A soil study (survey) is a systematic examination, description, classification, and mapping of soils in an area.

questions.prompt: The term "infill" is most closely defined as:
choices: An old building torn down and rebuilt.
A building renovated for recreational facilities.
A commercial building built on an empty lot in a commercially developed area.
Excavation of property for a new housing development.
questions.explanation: Infill: In housing construction, the process of developing open areas within an established area before developing outside the established area. These areas of vacant land may have been bypassed by earlier waves of development and are now largely surrounded by developed land.

questions.prompt: Steve has an old building where he runs his business. The city has just condemned the property through eminent domain. In this case:
choices: the city pays only just compensation.
the city pays compensation for the property and separate compensation for his stock-in-trade.
the city must pay compensation for the property, stock-in-trade and cost of moving.
the city does not need to pay compensation.
questions.explanation: When a city condemns a property by means of eminent domain, it is required to pay just compensation for the property only. "Just compensation" is usually the fair market value of the property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT automatically included in a sale unless stated?
choices: manufactured home not on a permanent foundation
a watercourse appurtenant to the land
questions.explanation: A manufactured home NOT attached to the land is personal property, not real. It would have to mentioned separately in the deed.

questions.prompt: All of the followings are true about the “frost line” EXCEPT:
choices: The frost line is the deepest point in the ground to which ground water will freeze.
The frost depth depends on the climatic conditions of an area.
Building codes take frost depth into account because of potential damage to building foundations.
Buildings/structure foundations should be built above the frost line to prevent slipping.
questions.explanation: The “frost line” is the depth at which the moisture present in the soil is expected to freeze. Building codes sometimes take frost depth into account because of frost heaving which can damage buildings by moving their foundations. Foundations are normally built below the frost line for this reason. Once your footings are buried below the frost line the ground will act as a barrier to insulate the soil below the footing from freezing in the winter.

questions.prompt: The transfer (sale) of real property would not affect:
questions.explanation: All of these transfer with the land.

questions.prompt: Mechanic's liens are:
questions.explanation: A mechanic's lien only affects the property of the party against whom the lien is filed.

questions.prompt: Community property is property owned by:
questions.explanation: Community property is automatically owned equally by each spouse regardless of whose name record title is held under.

questions.prompt: Property once zoned as commercial is re-zoned as residential. This is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Downzoning is action taken by local government to reduce the allowable density for a parcel of land, e.g., from commercial to residential.

questions.prompt: The listing agent fails to disclose that the property is in a Mello-Roos special tax district when the purchase contract is signed. Realizing his oversight, he delivers the required disclosure to the buyer in person the next day. Which of the following is correct regarding the buyer's rights?
choices: The buyer has a three-day right of rescission after receipt of the disclosure.
The buyer has no right to rescind if they did not specifically ask about the tax.
The listing agent is protected under the doctrine of "buyer beware."
The buyer is protected under the doctrine of "buyer beware."
questions.explanation: Failure to give notice of a Mello-Roos tax before signing of the sales contract permits the buyer or tenant a three-day right of rescission after receipt of the notice.

questions.prompt: The Statute of Limitations on action for removal of an encroachment is:
questions.explanation: The party being encroached upon must bring legal action for removal within three years of the discovery of the encroachment.

questions.prompt: If the interior side of an exterior wall is the same temperature to the touch on a winter day as the interior adjacent wall, this would indicate:
choices: there is plenty of heating duct work in that room.
the home has a good heating system.
questions.explanation: When an exterior wall is adequately insulated, the interior surface will be about the same temperature as the surface of interior walls because warm air will not be seeping through the walls. BE CAREFUL! The state has other versions of this same question, but the concept is the same.

questions.prompt: Zoning that allows residential property to exist on land zoned for industrial use is called:
questions.explanation: Cumulative zoning permits higher uses (e.g., residential) to exist on land zoned for lower uses (industrial), but lower uses cannot occupy higher-zoned land.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum depth of a closet?
questions.explanation: Standard closets are at least 24 inches deep or 2 feet deep in another version of this question.

questions.prompt: A high energy efficiency rating (EER) on an air conditioner would mean:
questions.explanation: Manufacturers are required to provide EER's (energy efficiency ratio). The unit of measure is the British Thermal Unit (BTU). It takes about 12,000 BTU's to melt a ton of ice in one hour. It is also the amount of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 Lb. of water 1 degree Fahrenheit. The higher the EER, the higher the efficiency. The higher the efficiency, the less electricity the unit uses.

questions.prompt: The "classical definition" of property ownership is ownership of:
choices: horizontal and vertical areas above and below the property.
everything below the property in the shape of an inverted pyramid with its apex at the center of the earth and infinite airspace.
questions.explanation: This is the classical definition of ownership of land. Modern day, practical theory prohibits exercising absolute control beyond a reasonable distance above and below the surface of the land.

questions.prompt: If you went to the city/county and wanted to change the electrical requirements specific to the structure from the standard normal requirements, this would be a(n):
questions.explanation: If the city or county allows you to do something on your property which differs from the building codes, it is called a variance.

questions.prompt: A property owner would post a notice of nonresponsibility to:
questions.explanation: A "notice of nonresponsibility" is designed to relieve a property owner from responsibility for the cost of unauthorized work done on his/her property or materials furnished for such a project.

questions.prompt: If you were granted the right to purchase a business with ready product, business plans, development plans, and marketing plans, this would be a(n):
questions.explanation: A franchise agreement is an agreement between a franchisor and franchisee, whereby the franchisee is given the right to distribute goods and services under a marketing plan prescribed by the franchisor.

questions.prompt: By law, all cities must have:
questions.explanation: Every city, by law, must have a planning commission. From this comes a general plan.

questions.prompt: A judgment will be most effective in the county where the:
questions.explanation: A judgment has no legal effect until recorded, and then only to the extent it is recorded in a county in which the defendant owns real property.

questions.prompt: A plot plan drawn by an architect is designed to:
choices: show the side and exterior views of the improvement.
give detailed specifications of the building components.
define the lot and show the location of the improvements on the site.
questions.explanation: A plot plan shows the layout of improvement on a property site. The plot plan usually includes location, dimensions, parking areas, landscaping, and the like.

questions.prompt: B.T.U.'s would indicate:
questions.explanation: B.T.U. stands for British Thermal Unit. One BTU is the amount of heat required to raise one pound of water one degree Fahrenheit in temperature.

questions.prompt: An easement differs from a license in that a license:
choices: must be created by written instrument.
questions.explanation: A license is the personal, revocable, nonassignable permission to do some act on the land of another. An easement cannot be revoked.

questions.prompt: An estate in real property with an individual interest in the unit plus undivided interest in common areas, such as, swimming pools, parking, or shared walkways, describes which of the following?
questions.explanation: Condominium ownership is an estate in real property consisting of an individual interest in an apartment or commercial unit and an undivided common interest in the common areas in the condo project such as the land, parking areas, elevators, stairways, exterior structure, and so on.

questions.prompt: The four unities of joint tenancy are:
questions.explanation: The four unities to a joint tenancy are: Time, Title, Interest and Possession. "TTIP"

questions.prompt: All of the following may use the power of eminent domain EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Eminent domain is the right of government (both state and federal), public corporations (school districts, sanitation districts), public entities, and public service corporations (railroads, power companies) to take private property for a necessary public use. The California Department of Real Estate (DRE) does not have this power.

questions.prompt: Abigail Blake leased an apartment in a recreation area from July 1, 2014 through August 31, 2015. She holds a(n):
questions.explanation: An interest or estate in land for a fixed period of time (a year, month, week) is called an estate for years.

questions.prompt: In order to find the architectural details of the footing, pier blocks, and sub-floor, a contractor or real estate broker would look at a(n):
questions.explanation: A foundation plan provides details concerning size of footings, size and dimensions of piers, and construction measurements with details of sub-floor areas.

questions.prompt: When a government or business gives the right to use its land without any interest in the land it's called a:
questions.explanation: A license is permission or authority to do a particular act on the land or property of another, usually on a nonexclusive basis. A license is a personal, revocable, and nonassignable right, but unlike an easement, it is not considered an interest in the land itself.

questions.prompt: Mark enters into an agreement to lease to Steve for 10 years. Four years later, Mark dies. Steve then discovers that Mark's interest was a life estate. Which of the following is correct?
choices: The ownership remains with Mark's heirs.
The lease is still valid for the full 10 years.
The lease terminates with Mark's death.
questions.explanation: A life tenant (Mark) may not encumber his or her interest beyond the life of its owner or the life of some other designated person.

questions.prompt: What is the length of measurement referred to as a "chain?"
questions.explanation: The total length of a surveyor's chain is 66 feet.

questions.prompt: A non-riparian landowner obtains the right to take water flowing on the public domain for personal use by:
questions.explanation: Appropriative water rights allow a non-riparian owner to divert water flowing on another owner's land or water flowing on the public domain for personal use.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered real property?
choices: Artificial items which are immovable by law
Easements that convey rights-of-way over adjoining land
questions.explanation: Real property includes land, that which is attached to it (physically or legally), and appurtenances (including easements).

questions.prompt: A lessee can remove:
choices: fixtures installed by the tenant for manufacture.
fixtures installed by the tenant for domestic use.
questions.explanation: Most items affixed to the property by the tenant CAN be removed when the lease expires.

questions.prompt: All of the following are considered real property EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A trade fixture is an article of personal property annexed or affixed to leased premises by the tenant as a necessary part of the tenant's trade or business.

questions.prompt: Mr. Coronado has an easement granted by the government to extract minerals on a piece of property. Mr. Smith acquired the adjacent land and put up a fence which blocked Mr. Coronado's access. Regarding Mr. Smith's actions:
choices: Mr. Coronado could sue for damages.
Mr. Smith had the right to put up the fence.
Mr. Smith could have Mr. Coronado arrested for trespassing.
questions.explanation: Mr. Coronado had an implied easement to cross Smith's land to get to his land. This could also be an easement by necessity.

questions.prompt: A husband alone, without his wife's consent, may:
questions.explanation: Any real property purchased by husband or wife separately becomes community property.

questions.prompt: Gregorian owns an easement in Duran's property/land. Gregorian is not a property owner. What kind of easement does Gregorian have?
questions.explanation: An easement in gross is the limited right of one person to use another's land (serviant estate) when such right is not created for the benefit of any land owned by the owner of the easement. In such case, there is no dominant estate, because the easement attaches personally to the owner, not the land.

questions.prompt: A property owner's petition for rezoning is rejected by the city planning commission. He/she:
choices: may appeal to the county planning commission.
may appeal to the municipal court claiming an unjust ruling.
may appeal to the city council.
has no recourse and may not apply again later.
questions.explanation: An appeals process is available through the city council. Legal action would be the next step.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a "fee estate?"
questions.explanation: A fee simple estate is the greatest degree of ownership recognized by law, also referred to as fee simple absolute.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must be recorded to be effective?
questions.explanation: Although a judgment is valid when awarded, it is only effective when properly recorded.

questions.prompt: A court order to ensure the sale of property to pay off judgment is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A writ of execution (also known as an execution) is a court order granted to put in force a judgment of possession obtained by a plaintiff from a court. When issuing a writ of execution, a court typically will order a sheriff or other similar official to take possession of property owned by a judgment debtor.

questions.prompt: The word "fee" as used in connection with real estate means:
questions.explanation: Fee simple title is sometimes referred to as "the fee" or "fee."

questions.prompt: A water company's right to run a water line through private property would most likely be:
questions.explanation: This is an example of a commercial easement in gross.

questions.prompt: The word "percolation" deals with:
questions.explanation: Percolation refers to the returning of water to the land. It is important that a septic tank system has good percolation. Percolation also refers to the recharging of the underground water system (water table).

questions.prompt: Which entity issues a permit for a subdivision in a coastal community?
choices: California Department of Parks and Recreation
questions.explanation: The California Coastal Commission has permit authority over construction of buildings, subdivisions, and activities that change the intensity of use of land or public access to coastal waters. The California Coastal Commission's mission is "To protect, conserve, restore, and enhance the environment of the California coastline"

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a type of soil or a soil condition?
questions.explanation: Deciduous pertains to plants that lose their leaves, not ground. Expansive soil is tightly packed, such as clay or adobe. Alkaline refers to the condition of the soil as to alkali content (salt).

questions.prompt: All of the following describe a fee simple interest EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Fee simple estates are usually encumbered by some kind of voluntary (e.g., mortgage) or involuntary lien (e.g., property tax).

questions.prompt: Brown leases a residence from Baker on a three-month written lease. Upon expiration of the written lease, Brown retains possession of the property without the consent of Baker. Brown now holds a(n):
questions.explanation: An estate at sufferance is defined as one in which a lessee rightfully comes into possession of the land and retains possession after the expiration of the lease.

questions.prompt: If land has a servient tenement, it has a(n):
questions.explanation: A servient estate is land on which an easement or other right exists in favor of an adjacent property (called the dominant tenement). The land subject to the easement (servient tenement) is said to be encumbered.

questions.prompt: If a lien was "lifted" from a property, what would it be called?
questions.explanation: The lien release bond allows for the removal of the lien on the property. The lien is instead attached to a surety bond. The property owner is typically the principal on the bond, the party ultimately responsible for satisfying the lien.

questions.prompt: An attachment lien is good:
choices: for three years from the date of levy.
questions.explanation: An attachment lien is good for three years from the date of levy and may be renewed.

questions.prompt: The best possible estate to have is:
questions.explanation: A fee simple estate is the maximum possible, least limited, and most complete ownership.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true regarding encumbrances?
choices: Even beneficial restrictions can be encumbrances.
questions.explanation: CC&R's are an example of a potentially beneficial encumbrance.

questions.prompt: Which of the following allows a landowner to retain private ownership while also achieving other goals, like protecting a farming or ranching operation, preserving open space or conserving habitat for wildlife?
questions.explanation: Conservation easements are based on the idea that when people own land, they own rights that go with the property – such as the right to graze cattle, hunt, build a home, subdivide or extract minerals. By voluntarily limiting some of these activities, a conservation easement allows a landowner to retain private ownership while also achieving other goals, like protecting a farming or ranching operation, preserving open space or conserving habitat for wildlife. Typically, a conservation easement limits subdivision and non-agricultural, commercial uses.

questions.prompt: What is bifurcation?
choices: Dividing a market of potential customers into groups, or segments, based on different characteristics.
Dividing the housing market into different segments, such as the difference between traditional sales and short sales.
The illegal practice of categorizing different minority groups within a specific residential area.
The process of renovating and improving a house or district so that it conforms to middle-class taste.
questions.explanation: Bifurcation is a word to indicate something is split into parts. When it comes to the housing market, we'd say the market is bifurcated because there are different segments of the market. We see this clearly when there is a price difference between traditional sales, short sales and foreclosures.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered personal property?
questions.explanation: A mortgage or trust deed is personal property (lien).

questions.prompt: Studding in a single-family dwelling is usually:
questions.explanation: The letters O.C. stand for "On Center." Stud spacing is usually 16" O.C. This means that the distance between the center line of adjacent studs is 16" on center. (See construction terms)

questions.prompt: As a general rule which of the following sources would be least satisfactory in providing a legal description for a parcel of real property?
questions.explanation: A legal description is required on all deeds, assignments of lease and mortgages. It is also used in most contracts for deed. The bill for real property tax does not include the legal description. It includes only a parcel number. An owner is taxed according to parcel number.

questions.prompt: An easement may be created for what length of time?
questions.explanation: An easement may be created for any length of time.

questions.prompt: A limited partner is:
choices: limited to a 40 hour work week.
the same in terms of liability as the general partners.
limited as to his/her personal liability.
questions.explanation: Liability is limited to the amount of their investment. (see limited partnership)

questions.prompt: What are the units used to measure the length of a nail?
questions.explanation: The original system was to measure the nail in relation to a silver penny. Thus, a ten-penny nail weighed as much as ten silver pennies.

questions.prompt: Truman deeded his farm to his sons, "A", "B", and "C" as joint tenants. "B" sold his interest to "W". "A" died, but had previously willed his interest to "S" (his heir). "C" retained his inheritance. Ownership of the property would be:
choices: "C" and "W" as tenants in common, with "C" having 2/3 interest and "W" having 1/3 interest.
Undecided until probate of "A's" estate has been completed.
"S", "W", and "C" as tenants in common, each having 1/3 interest.
questions.explanation: When "B" sold his interest to "W", "W" became a tenant in common with BOTH "A" and "C". Because "A" and "B" were joint tenants, "A" could NOT will his interest. It passed to "C" upon "A's" death. This resulted in "C" and "W" becoming tenants in common.

questions.prompt: Mechanic's liens are based on:
questions.explanation: Mechanic's lien law is statutory law contained in the California Civil Code.

questions.prompt: The rededication of land in an urban environment, usually open space, to new construction is referred to as:
questions.explanation: In urban planning, infill is the rededication of land in an urban environment, usually open space, to new construction.

questions.prompt: A bearing wall:
choices: can be built at any angle to the door.
is usually left alone during remodeling.
questions.explanation: A bearing wall is a main or supporting wall referred to as a load-bearing wall, usually supporting a roof above. It usually is of stronger construction than other members and is usually left alone when remodeling. It is possible for a bearing wall to be built in a variety of angles to a door.

questions.prompt: The sudden tearing away or removal of land by water flowing through or over it is called:
questions.explanation: Avulsion is the loss of land as a result of its being washed away by a sudden or violent action of nature.

questions.prompt: A covenant in Johnson's deed states that he may not operate a dog kennel on the property. Johnson proceeds to build a commercial dog kennel. Adjoining land owners would have recourse by:
questions.explanation: An injunction would compel Mr. Johnson to close the kennel.

questions.prompt: A licensee who speaks of a "grandfather clause" is probably referring to:
choices: Inheritance rights of a direct descendant
Public restrictions on the use of a property
questions.explanation: When zoning is changed, the present use becomes a "non-conforming use". Since it was legal when it was put into service, it is "grandfathered" in, and the original use will remain legal.

questions.prompt: The legal seizure of property for sidewalks by the government is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Eminent domain is condemnation by government for public purposes, just compensation must be paid. Condemnation is part of the government's right of eminent domain.

questions.prompt: Deed restrictions are:
questions.explanation: CC&R's are encumbrances but not liens.

questions.prompt: Land subject to an easement is said to be:
questions.explanation: Land subject to an easement is said to be burdened or encumbered.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are known as artificial monuments?
questions.explanation: A monument is an object that marks property lines or the like. Streets may or may not be artificial. Canals are not natural, therefore artificial.

questions.prompt: Ownership of an undivided interest in land with no right of survivorship is found in:
questions.explanation: The words "undivided interest" coupled with "no right of survivorship" refer to tenants in common.

questions.prompt: Documentary Transfer Tax is calculated at a rate of ______ of the price paid for the property (or fraction thereof).
questions.explanation: Documentary Transfer Tax is calculated at a rate of 55 cents for each $500 of the price paid for the property or fraction thereof. A portion of the total price paid for the property may be exempt because a lien remains on the property.

questions.prompt: In new construction financing, when does the lender usually release the final payment to the borrower?
choices: When the owner accepts the property
When the Notice of Completion is recorded
questions.explanation: The lender will not release final payment until the lien period has expired.

questions.prompt: The higher the EER rating:
choices: the more watts needed to run the unit.
questions.explanation: The efficiency rating of an air conditioning unit is called its EER or Energy Efficiency Ratio. A unit’s Energy Efficiency Ratio (EER) is the ratio of cooling energy to the amount of energy (wattage) required to power your unit. The higher the EER rating, the more efficient the unit and the more money saved on cooling bills. With this question, it is correct to say the higher the EER rating, the lower the BTU’s (British Thermal Unit). (British Thermal Unit).

questions.prompt: A lease would be a:
questions.explanation: A chattel is an item of personal property. The word chattel evolved from the word cattle, one of the early important possessions. Chattels real are annexed to real estate, whereas, chattels personal are moveable. A lease is an example of a chattel real.

questions.prompt: Private restriction on the use of land may be created by:
questions.explanation: Private restrictions are created by means of covenants, conditions and restrictions (CC&R's) written into real property instruments such as deeds and leases.

questions.prompt: A judgment that has been recorded would be a(n):
questions.explanation: A judgment lien is an involuntary lien.

questions.prompt: What is a kiosk?
choices: a term for a sunken living room
questions.explanation: A kiosk is a freestanding structure (open sides usually multi-sided) located in a shopping center or mall from which merchandise is sold. Another answer encountered on the state exam may be "a multi-sided structure found in a shopping mall."

questions.prompt: The spread part at the bottom of the exterior of the foundation in a single-family dwelling is a:
questions.explanation: The spread part of the foundation below the ground is referred to as the foundation footing.

questions.prompt: The Williamson Act provides helps owners of farmland and open-space land in the form of:
questions.explanation: The Williamson Act of the US state of California (officially, the California Land Conservation Act of 1965) is a California law that provides relief of property tax to owners of farmland and open-space land in exchange for a minimum 10 year agreement that the land will not be developed or otherwise converted to another use. The motivation for the Williamson Act is to promote voluntary land conservation, particularly farmland conservation.

questions.prompt: How long must land be maintained under a Williamson Act contract?
questions.explanation: The California Land Conservation Act, better known as the Williamson Act, has been the state’s premier agricultural land protection program since its enactment in 1965. The minimum term for a Williamson Act contract is 10 years.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which lists the events in their proper order?
questions.explanation: The plaintiff gets an attachment lien before entry of the judgment, and thus is assured of the availability of the defendant's property for eventual execution in satisifaction of the claim.

questions.prompt: In the event of a conflict between local building codes and the Health and Safety Code, which would prevail?
choices: The more stringent of the two
The one selected after a hearing
questions.explanation: In the event of a conflict between local building codes and the Health and Safety Code, the more stringent typically prevails.

questions.prompt: California's community property laws are a holdover from:
questions.explanation: A holdover from Spanish law is the concept of community property which is property acquired by husband and wife during marriage.

questions.prompt: A developer ordered two truckloads of backfill during the construction of a home. He ordered this for the purpose of:
questions.explanation: Backfill is earth or selected material such as aggregate, usually used to fill in around foundation walls after they are completed.

questions.prompt: Which is the most common type of easement on residential property?
questions.explanation: Normally, the telephone company or electric company has an easement over the back of your property to string wires or place telephone poles. This right is called an easement in gross.

questions.prompt: A person holding title to property in severalty would most likely have:
questions.explanation: Severalty is sole ownership of real property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of police power?
questions.explanation: Police power is the authority of the state to adopt and enforce laws and regulations to promote and support the public's health, safety, morals, and general welfare.

questions.prompt: What is a commercial acre?
choices: An acre minus space for streets and parking.
An acre minus space for warehouse structures.
An acre minus space for all housing accommodations.
An acre minus space for schools and emergency services.
questions.explanation: A commercial acre is that portion of an acre of newly subdivided land remaining after dedication for streets, sidewalks, parks and so on.

questions.prompt: The highest structural point of a wood frame house is the:
questions.explanation: The highest point is the ridge or the ridge board.

questions.prompt: The doctrine of constructive severance applies to:
questions.explanation: The "doctrine of constructive severance" states that when growing crops are sold, they are legally considered severed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be considered real property?
choices: A maturing grape crop which is under a sales contract to be harvested later.
Trade fixtures that a tenant has installed but which are removable without damage.
A built-in refrigerator in a mobile home that is not attached to a permanent foundation.
A bearing wall in a single-family home.
questions.explanation: Since a bearing wall is part of the structure of a house and the house is real property, the bearing wall would also be real property.

questions.prompt: The water department is a:
questions.explanation: A quasi-governmental agency is privately owned and has stock holders but is governmentally regulated.

questions.prompt: Who regulates franchises in California?
questions.explanation: The Department of Business Oversight (DBO) regulates and oversees the enforcement of California's Franchise Investment Law and the registration of Franchise Disclosure Documents (FDDs).

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for disclosure of a Mello-Roos bond against the property?
questions.explanation: Based on passage of the Mello-Roos Community Facilities Act of 1982, certain housing tracts may be within what are called "community facilities districts" where special taxes are assessed to finance designated public facilities and/or services.
