Mello-Roos liens are usually municipal bonds issued to fund streets, sewers, and other infrastructure needs before a housing development is built. The seller of a property consisting of one-to-four dwelling unit or a lease (for more than five years) subject to the lien of a Mello-Roos community facilities district must make a good faith effort to obtain from the district a disclosure notice concerning the special tax and give the notice to the prospective buyer.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements are true about zoning EXCEPT:
choices: Violations of zoning ordinances may render title unmarketable.
Zoning laws are generally enforced through building permits.
Zoning laws are concerned with regulating property values.
questions.explanation: Zoning laws are NOT retroactive.

questions.prompt: A "key lot" is:
choices: the most desirable lot on the block.
the least desirable lot on the block.
the lot which has the best orientation.
questions.explanation: A key lot is abutted by 3 or more parcels and is considered the least desirable because of loss of privacy and noise.

questions.prompt: Property is:
questions.explanation: One of the most basic definitions of real property is: "All property is personal if not real."

questions.prompt: Based on the white paper on smart community planning in California, which of the following is superseded by Form-Based Planning?
questions.explanation: Form-based planning (or code) is a land development regulation that fosters predictable built results and a high-quality public realm by using physical form (rather than separation of uses) as the organizing principle for the code. A form-based code is a regulation, not a mere guideline, adopted into city, town, or county law. A form-based code offers a powerful alternative to traditional planning using zoning regulations.

questions.prompt: Personal property becomes real property when:
questions.explanation: Property, whether real or personal, may undergo a change of class, as when personal property readily movable becomes immovable by becoming permanently affixed to land or improvements.

questions.prompt: Which of the following forms of ownership consists of an undivided interest with right of survivorship?
questions.explanation: The right of of survivorship is the main characteristic of a joint tenancy holding.

questions.prompt: The city's master plan would include:
choices: access to water, drainage and sewage.
questions.explanation: The city's master plan is a comprehensive plan to guide the long-term physical development of a particular area.

questions.prompt: Johnson, a real estate broker, listed a property. Suzie, a salesperson working for broker Sims, received an offer. Donna, a salesperson working for broker Johnson, got the offer accepted. Who earned the commission?
questions.explanation: As the listing broker, Johnson earned the commission under the terms of the listing agreement. A commission split may occur since the offer came in through another broker.

questions.prompt: When acting as agent for seller Jones, real estate broker Smith:
choices: is obligated to render faithful service to Jones.
can modify the terms of any contract that Jones enters into.
can eliminate any offers on Jones' property that Smith believes are not good enough.
questions.explanation: As a fiduciary, the broker (and salesperson) have a duty to be faithful to the principal.

questions.prompt: An agent becomes the agent of the seller when both the seller and the agent sign:
questions.explanation: The Listing Agreement creates the agency relationship between the seller and the listing agent.

questions.prompt: Jackson leased his home to Sullivan with a verbal agreement to sell the property to Sullivan. Jackson knows that Sullivan has been making significant improvements to the property in reliance on that verbal agreement. Jackson now declines to sell the property to Sullivan. Which of the following best describes the rights of the parties?
choices: Jackson must sell because he made an ostensible agreement.
Sullivan has no right to enforce the verbal agreement.
Jackson must sell because the doctrine of estoppel will apply in this case.
Jackson does not have to sell because of the Statute of Frauds.
questions.explanation: The doctrine of estoppel would apply when one person allows another to rely on statements made to the detriment of that person. In this case, Jackson allowed Sullivan to rely on a verbal promise to sell and to make substantial improvements to the property. The court would "stop" Jackson from refusing to sell.

questions.prompt: Commission rate price fixing is a violation of the:
choices: California Fair Employment and Housing Act.
questions.explanation: Price fixing is a violation of the Sherman Anti-trust laws.

questions.prompt: In the case of a sale of property where the deceased died without leaving a will, the commission would be set by:
choices: the California Code of Civil Procedure.
questions.explanation: The court referred to would be the probate court.

questions.prompt: Who is more likely to earn the commission?
choices: The one who communicated the offer to the seller.
The one who communicated the seller's acceptance of the offer to the buyer.
The one who secured the biggest down payment from the buyer.
The one who secured the offer.
questions.explanation: Until the seller's acceptance is communicated to the buyer, there is no contract. Therefore, the one who communicates the seller's acceptance to the buyer is more likely to earn the commission.

questions.prompt: The Real Estate Commissioner may fine a broker which of the following amounts for illegal payment of commission to an unlicensed person:
questions.explanation: The Commissioner does not levy fines. This is done by the court. The Commissioner may temporarily suspend or permanently revoke the license of a real estate licensee for such illegal payment of commission.

questions.prompt: An agency relationship may be terminated by:
questions.explanation: All of the choices are ways to terminate an agency relationship. Look out for a question about what happens to a listing if the property burns down. Destruction of the property prior to the sale also terminates the agency agreement and thus a listing.

questions.prompt: When negotiating a lease on behalf of a commercial real property landlord, the broker would usually calculate his commission as:
choices: a percent of the rent due in the first year of the lease.
a percent of the first and last month's rent.
a percent of the rent due for the entire lease period.
a percent of the rent due for the first six months of the lease.
questions.explanation: The broker's commission is normally calculated as a percent of the total amount of lease payments. This is negotiable, however and not a hard and fast rule of law.

questions.prompt: Under the law of agency, a fiduciary relationship is created between the broker and the seller on execution of the listing agreement. As far as the broker's responsibility to third parties, the broker:
choices: needs to disclose material facts only when asked about them.
should disclose the lowest price the seller is willling to accept.
questions.explanation: In addition to his/her fiduciary obligations to the seller, an agent must be fair and honest to third parties. Because of the close personal relationship between broker (agent) and seller or buyer (principal), the broker often learns certain confidential information about the client and/or financial situation of the principal. This information cannot be disclosed by a broker, even after the transaction is completed and the fiduciary relationship is terminated.

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee offered to rebate part of his commission to the buyer if the buyer would increase his offer to a level that the agent knew would be high enough for the seller to accept. Under these circumstances:
choices: this information must be disclosed to the seller before the offer is accepted by the seller.
this action is a violation of the licensing law and would lead to immediate disciplinary action.
the licensee could be held liable for damages in a civil suit even though this information was given to the seller prior to the seller's acceptance.
questions.explanation: Any information material to the transaction must be disclosed to the seller prior to acceptance of the offer by the seller. This would include any agreement by a licensee to rebate a portion of his/her commission to the buyer.

questions.prompt: Real estate commissions may be paid the form of:
questions.explanation: Although it is true that most real estate commissions are paid in the form of cash (check), it can be "anything of value" so long as that value is defined and agreed upon by all parties to the transaction.

questions.prompt: A real estate broker should regard himself/herself as a:
questions.explanation: The broker acts as a fiduciary in the transaction.

questions.prompt: As the agent for the seller, a real estate broker negotiated a sale. By agreement, the licensee can be paid his commission in the form of:
questions.explanation: All of the choices may be the commission if agreed upon in advance.

questions.prompt: Typically when leasing real property, the commission of the leasing agent is based on a percentage of:
choices: total rents collected during the term of the lease.
questions.explanation: Usually, the commission of a leasing agent is figured on the total rent to be collected over the term of the lease. The commission can be any amount negotiated and specified in the employment contract.

questions.prompt: An agency relationship may be created by all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Subornation (suborn) means to bribe or induce someone to unlawfully (or secretly) perform some misdeed or to commit a crime. (Don't confuse this with subordination.) The other answers are methods by which agencies may be created.

questions.prompt: Which of the following types of sales requires a disclosure that the sales commission is negotiable?
questions.explanation:
B & P Code § Section 10147.5 is now operative. It reads: 10147.5(a)-Any printed or form agreement which initially establishes or is intended to establish or alters the terms of any agreement which previously established a right to compensation to be paid to a real estate licensee for the sale of residential real property containing not more than four (4) residential units, or the sale of a mobile home, shall contain the following statement in not less than 10-point boldface type immediately preceding any provision of such agreement relating to compensation of the licensee.

NOTICE: THE AMOUNT OR RATE OF REAL ESTATE COMMISSIONS IS NOT FIXED BY LAW. THEY ARE SET BY EACH BROKER INDIVIDUALLY AND MAY BE NEGOTIABLE BETWEEN THE SELLER AND BROKER.

questions.prompt: Broker Adams represents a buyer in a single-family home transaction. As an incentive, he agreed to rebate part of his commission to the buyer. Broker Adams is required to:
choices: notify the seller of the rebate.
notify the Real Estate Commissioner of the rebate.
notify the Internal Revenue Service of the rebate.
notify no one as this is a financial matter that affects only the broker and the buyer.
questions.explanation: Failure to disclose to the seller that the buyer will receive any part of the commission may subject the broker to disciplinary action under B & P Code § 10176(a). This section declares such action to be "substantial misrepresentation." A monetary inducement given to the buyer is a material fact and could affect the seller's negotiation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a "dual agency?"
choices: An agent only represents one principal.
The agent acts concurrently for both the buyer and seller in a transaction with the full knowledge and consent of both parties.
The agent is authorized to do all acts connected with a particular trade, business or employment.
The agent is only authorized to perform only those acts specifically authorized by the principal.
questions.explanation: A dual agency is an agency relationship in which the agent acts concurrently for both of the principals in the transaction. A dual agency is lawful if it is created with the full knowledge and consent of both parties.

questions.prompt: A real estate commission is usually based on the:
questions.explanation: Real estate commissions are usually based on a percentage of the selling price.

questions.prompt: What type of agency allows a broker to sign for a principal when there is an emergency?
questions.explanation: Agency by necessity is an agency created by an emergency arising from a situation making it necessary or proper for the agent to act without receiving the sanction or authorization of the principal, in order to prevent harm to the principal. It arises when a duty is imposed on a person to act on behalf of another apart from contract and to prevent irreparable injury. For instance, if a property is damaged by fire while the owner is out of town, another party may temporarily be called in to act as their agent until the owner returns or is able to provide instruction. The doctrine of agency by necessity is confined to fairly narrow limits by the courts.

questions.prompt: The law of agency is concerned with the rights and duties between and among the:
choices: agent and the principal, whether disclosed or undisclosed.
principal and third parties with whom the agent deals on behalf of the principal.
agent and third parties with whom the agent deals on behalf of the principal.
questions.explanation: All three choices describe the fiduciary relationship between the real estate agent and the principal.

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee who misrepresents a property to a buyer while acting as agent for the seller, may face:
choices: disciplinary action by the Department of Real Estate.
questions.explanation: Even though a real estate agent is representing the seller, he/she must still be fair and honest to all the parties to the transaction. Misrepresenting the property to the buyer may subject an agent to choices (a), (b), and (c).

questions.prompt: A real estate broker, licensed only in California, verbally agreed to split a commission with a real estate broker not licensed in California:
choices: This is a violation of the California Real Estate Law.
This is permissible, but the broker must first get permission from the Real Estate Commissioner.
This is unenforceable in a California court as the agreement was not in writing as required by the California Business and Professions Code.
questions.explanation: In California, a real estate broker acting in the capacity of an independent contractor may agree verbally or in writing to split a commission with another broker. Such a contract is enforceable in the California courts.

questions.prompt: A listing broker wants to give $50 to a buyer and $50 credit against his commission to a buyer or seller who either lists with him or purchases one of his listings. With regard to his actions:
choices: it is permissible to give $50 to the buyer but not the seller.
it is permissible to give $50 to the seller only.
it is permissible to give $50 to the buyer and to credit his commission with the seller.
it is against the real estate law to give $50 to either the buyer or the seller.
questions.explanation: It is permissible for a listing broker to rebate a portion of his/her commission to the buyer or seller as long as the rebate and/or credit is disclosed to all parties.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: A dual agency is always a divided agency.
A divided agency is NOT always a dual agency.
A dual agency is NOT necessarily a violation of law.
A dual agency is always a violation of law.
questions.explanation: This is a tricky question, read it carefully. The term dual agency does not, in itself, describe an unlawful activity. In fact, the law is reasonably clear when it states that an agent cannot legally act for two principals in negotations with each other unless both have knowledge of and consent to the dual agency. [B & P Code § 10176(d)]. Thus, we find that an agent can represent both parties in the same transaction.

questions.prompt: The phrase that best describes the nature of a broker's duty to keep a principal fully informed is:
questions.explanation: Among the obligations that a fiduciary owes to his/her principal are the duties of loyalty, obedience, and full disclosure; to be fair and honest; the duty to use skill, care and diligence; and the duty to account for all monies.

questions.prompt: A licensed real estate broker representing the seller becomes the gratuitous agent (no fee) of the buyer and accepts all of the fiduciary responsibilities as the buyer's agent when he/she:
choices: shows the property to the buyer.
arranges financing for the buyer, including a purchase-money-loan.
gives the buyer a list of certified appraisers.
writes up the offer to purchase the seller's property.
questions.explanation: If the agent representing the seller goes as far as setting up the buyer's financing, he/she becomes the buyer's agent and thus assumes all fiduciary responsibilities as the buyer's agent.

questions.prompt: A real estate agent is under a duty to use which of the following in the performance of his/her duties?
questions.explanation: Among the obligations that a fiduciary owes to his/her principal are the duties of loyalty, obedience, and full disclosure; to be fair and honest; the duty to use skill, care and diligence; and the duty to account for all monies.

questions.prompt: A listing agent received two offers in the morning and immediately presented the offers to the seller. In the evening the agent received two more offers, both with a lower price. What should the agent do?
choices: Don't present the evening offers to the seller because the offers were low.
Wait until the seller has made a decision on the morning offers before presenting the evening offers.
Wait until the next day to present the lower evening offers.
Let the seller know of the two new offers immediately.
questions.explanation: Even though it is a temptation to favor the higher offers, it is the listing agent's fiduciary duty to notify the buyer of the new offers immediately.

questions.prompt: If you are a subagent of the listing broker, you are working for the:
questions.explanation:
"Subagent" means a person to whom an agent delegates agency powers. However, "subagent" does not include an associate licensee who is acting under the supervision of an agent in a real property transaction.

The marketing of real property by real estate agents is often a cooperative effort. The listing broker usually makes an offer of compensation to a cooperating broker (subagent) by placing the property on the Multiple Listing Service. Some MLS's make the offer of subagency automatic, while for others, the offer of subagency is optional and requires an affirmative act by the listing broker. If the principal (seller) specifically authorizes his/her broker to appoint a subagent and thus establishes a new contractual and fiduciary relationship, the subagent represents the principal in the same manner as the listing broker.

questions.prompt: An agency relationship can be created by all of the following, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A real estate licensee cannot become your agent by simply volunteering. An agency relationship can be created by written agreement or it may be implied by the acts of the principal and agent. It can also be created by oral agreement.

questions.prompt: Seller "A" lets buyer "B" assume that Broker "C" was his agent. This type of agency relationship is an example of:
questions.explanation: Ostensible authority is that authority which a third person reasonably believes an agent possesses because of the acts or omissions of the principal. Ratification is the adoption or approval of an act performed on behalf of a person without previous authorization, such as the approval by a principal of an agent after the acts have been performed. Estoppel is a legal doctrine which prevents a person from alleging something to be true or a fact which is contrary to a previous affirmation or allegation made by that same person.

questions.prompt: All of the following require an Agency Disclosure Agreement EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: An agency disclosure agreement is required for property with one to four dwelling units, any leasehold in this type of property exceeding one year's duration, and mobile homes, when offered for sale or sold through an agent.

questions.prompt: When a licensee is acting as the buyer's agent, this fact must be disclosed to others:
choices: after the offer has been presented and accepted.
after the licensee receives a commission.
questions.explanation: The form of agency relationship must be disclosed as soon as practicable.

questions.prompt: A salesman asked the listing broker, who was not his employing broker, to advance him $600 against the commission the listing broker had agreed to pay to the selling agent. The listing broker paid the selling salesman the $600, even though the deal had not yet closed escrow. Which of the following is correct?
choices: The listing broker had violated a Real Estate Law.
This is permissible if it is in writing.
None of the preceding apply as brokers are allowed to pay commissions to anyone they wish.
questions.explanation: A salesman may only collect a commission from his employing broker. Likewise, a broker may not pay a commission to anyone other than his employed salesman. The listing broker has violated the Real Estate Law, Section 10137.

questions.prompt: In the correct order, list the chain of events necessary to comply with the agency disclosure law:
questions.explanation: According to the agency disclosure law, the correct order is: Disclose, Elect, Confirm (Memory Aid: DEC).

questions.prompt: A broker has been in the business for many years. He currently has 40 exclusive listings in his office. The broker dies and his daughter who is also a broker, takes over for him. What should she do about the current listings?
choices: Just inform the seller that she is taking over as broker.
She must attempt to renegotiate all of the listings.
She need only inform the Department of Real Estate that she is now the broker of record.
questions.explanation: Listings are personal service contracts and terminate with the death of either party. The listing agreement is between the seller and the broker. When the broker dies, the listing terminates. The new broker must attempt to renegotiate the listings with the sellers.

questions.prompt: Dual agency happens mostly with:
questions.explanation: An "in-house" sale is a form of dual agency where a buyer is represented by the same brokerage firm that has the listing.

questions.prompt: A licensed real estate broker who specializes in property management activities usually receives commissions:
choices: based on a percentage of the rents expected to be collected over the life of the leases.
equal to the first and last month's rent.
based on a percentage of the gross rents collected.
based on the first year's rent.
questions.explanation: A broker specializing in property management generally receives commissions based on a percentage of the gross rents collected, not those that would be anticipated over the term of the leases.

questions.prompt: Select the choice which most nearly represents "price fixing" from the following:
choices: A broker instructing his employees not to accept listings for less than a 6% commission.
A broker casually mentioning, during a luncheon with several other brokers from other offices, that his office is planning to decrease the minimum office commission from 6% to 5%.
At the request of a cooperating agent, the listing broker tells the cooperating agent the amount of compensation on an exclusive right to sell listing taken by one of his salespeople.
Advertising the amount of commission your office charges.
questions.explanation: There is no such thing as an "innocent" discussion of commissions or fees between or among competing brokers and the law views this as price fixing. As a company policy, a broker may set a commission schedule for his/her own employees.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements does NOT correctly describe a fiduciary?
choices: A fiduciary owes loyalty to the principal.
A fiduciary must conform to the principal's legal instructions.
A fiduciary is a neutral third party.
questions.explanation: The broker has a fiduciary duty to work in the best interest of his/her client.

questions.prompt: A Buyer is interested in a property. Buyer calls Broker to see if she has a listing on the property. Broker says no, but that the owner is a client. Broker calls the owner to secure a listing and to let the owner know that she has a buyer. The owner says the property is not for sale. Two weeks later, the owner sells the property to the buyer.
choices: Broker is not entitled to a commission for her efforts
Broker is entitled to 50% of the commission for her efforts
Broker is entitled to all of the commission for her efforts
Broker must share commission with the buyer, who found the property on their own.
questions.explanation: In this case the buyer found the property on their own and wasnâ€™t a buyer of the broker. Without an existing buyer-agency relationship with the Broker, the Broker is NOT entitled to a commission as the broker did not establish procuring cause to the sale.

questions.prompt: All of the following are essential to the creation of an agency relationship, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The payment of consideration need not be involved in an agency relationship. One may gratuitously undertake to act as an agent and will be held to the standards of agency upon assumption of those duties.

questions.prompt: A broker DOES NOT need to disclose if the principle is:
choices: an employee of the broker's corporation.
an acquaintance of either buyer or seller.
a blood relative of the broker.
questions.explanation: A real estate licensee must disclose any personal or business relationship he/she has with the buyer or seller which may influence the transaction or give the appearance of a conflict. This includes any member of the broker's immediate family, firms, or any member thereof, or any entity in which the broker has any ownership interest.

questions.prompt: Owner Johnson tells broker Stone that he wants to sell his house as soon as possible and would accept $350,000. Stone tells buyer Smith that Johnson has financial troubles and will accept a much lower price, possibly as low as $300,000. Johnson, ultimately, accepts an offer from Smith for $300,000. Broker Stone is guilty of:
choices: nothing, since his job is to find a buyer no matter what.
violating the fiduciary duty to buyer Smith.
unethical behavior, but not a serious breach of his fiduciary responsiblity to Johnson.
unethical behavior and a violation of the fiduciary responsibility.
questions.explanation: Broker Stone's actions are a clear violation of his fiduciary responsibility to the seller. This would also be a violation of the Realtors Code of Ethics since the seller did not authorize broker Stone to disclose such information to the buyer. If broker Johnson's financial troubles were in fact true and he authorized broker Stone to inform the buyer of such, it would not be a violation.

questions.prompt: A power of attorney can be terminated by the:
choices: incapacity of the parties to the power of attorney.
questions.explanation: A power of attorney is a written instrument authorizing a person, the attorney-in-fact, to act as the agent on behalf of another to the extent indicated in the instrument. All of the choices would result in the termination of the power of attorney.

questions.prompt: When is a properly licensed real estate salesperson most likely to get his/her commission?
choices: When both the buyer and seller have signed the deposit receipt.
When the grant deed is signed.
When the grant deed is recorded.
questions.explanation: Be careful in reading this question. The salesperson is most likely to get his/her commission when escrow closes.

questions.prompt: The maximum commission a broker may charge for the sale of residential property is:
choices: set forth in the Real Estate Law.
determined by the broker's contract with his principal.
six percent of the total sales price of a residence.
questions.explanation: There is currently no law which controls what amount may be charged by the broker. Therefore, it is set by agreement between the parties.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the unlawful form of dual agency called "divided agency?"
choices: The agent acts concurrently for both the buyer and seller, but keeps them divided by not ever letting them communicate directly.
The agent represents only one principal, but divides the duties to be performed with another agent.
The agent acts concurrently for both the buyer and seller in a transaction without the knowledge and consent of both parties.
The agent represents the seller and two buyers.
questions.explanation: When the agent becomes the agent of both the buyer and seller, without the knowledge and consent of both, the agency may be more accurately described and identified as a "divided agency." When the agency is a divided agency, it is a violation of Section 10176(d) of the Business and Professions Code (the Real Estate Law).

questions.prompt: When selling a business, the rate of commission is determined by:
choices: the agreement between the broker and owner.
questions.explanation: Real estate commissions are always negotiable and are determined by the agreement between the broker and owner.

questions.prompt: All of the following are essential elements of an agency agreement EXCEPT:
choices: fiduciary relationship of the agent to the principal.
questions.explanation: Choices b, c, and d are all essential elements for the creation of an agency relationship. The payment of consideration is not related to the creation of an agency relationship.

questions.prompt: With regards to a fiduciary relationship, a Broker is to a Seller, as a:
questions.explanation: The broker/seller relationship is similar to the beneficiary/trustee relationship as the trustee is holding the deed of trust for the benefit of the lender (beneficiary) and works on behalf of the beneficiary. The trustee has a fiduciary responsibility to the beneficiary.

questions.prompt: An agency relationship may be created by:
questions.explanation: Most agency relationships are created by written agreement. An agency relationship can also be created by ratification (consenting to acts of the agent), and estoppel (principal stopped from denying an inconsistent position in the representation).

questions.prompt: Nondisclosure of a dual agency by a broker can result in:
questions.explanation: Failure to disclose a dual agency can result in rescission of the contract. The agency may also lose his/her commission and be subjected to disciplinary action by the Department of Real Estate.

questions.prompt: A "dual agency" is legal if:
choices: All parties are told before close of escrow.
The buyer and seller consent to it.
The broker and escrow company agree to it.
All parties are told after they sign the contracts.
questions.explanation: The safest rule to apply is than when you represent both parties, in any way, you become a dual agent. When the agent becomes the agent of both, without the knowledge and consent of both, the agency is considered illegal.

questions.prompt: A saleman asks a broker, other than his own, for a $100.00 advance on his next commission. If the broker pays it, he is:
questions.explanation: A real estate broker may never pay money to another broker's salesperson.

questions.prompt: You are a California real estate broker. A prospect is referred to you by an out-of-state broker and a sale is consummated by you. You want to split your commission with the cooperating broker. Under the California Real Estate law:
choices: you may pay a commission to a broker of another state.
you cannot divide a commission with a broker of another state.
you can pay a commission to a broker of another state only if he/she is also licensed in California.
questions.explanation: B & P Code § 10137: "it is unlawful for any licensed real estate broker to employ or compensate, directly or indirectly, any person for performing any of the acts within the scope of this chapter who is not a licensed real estate broker or a real estate salesman licensed under the broker employing or compensating him; however, a licensed real estate broker may pay a commission to a broker of another state."

questions.prompt: An attorney-in-fact can best be described as a(n):
choices: person casually granted the power to act as a principal for another.
properly authorized party who is acting as a dual agent.
attorney appointed by the court to administer an estate of a deceased person.
person authorized to act on behalf of another person by a power of attorney.
questions.explanation:
An attorney-in-fact is a person authorized to act on behalf of another person, but not necessarily authorized to practice law, e.g. a person authorized to act by a power of attorney. An attorney-in-fact is a fiduciary.

For example, Person A might give a power of attorney to Person B that allows Person B to manage Person A's bank accounts. In this example, Person A is the principal, and Person B is the attorney-in-fact.

questions.prompt: Which represents the four unities of market value?
questions.explanation: Referred to as the four characteristics of market value: Demand, Utility, Scarcity, Transferability. On the state exam they are sometimes referred to as the "primary requisites of value." Memory aid: DUST

questions.prompt: The oldest appraisal method is the:
questions.explanation: The sales comparison approach is the oldest and easiest method of appraising property.

questions.prompt: A group of buildings developed in a line along the frontage of a main highway would most likely be a(n):
questions.explanation: Strip centers (sometimes referred to as convenience centers) are characterized by adjoining buildings that are narrow in depth relative to their length. The typical design for these districts is a straight line of stores set back far enough from the street to allow for perpendicular parking.

questions.prompt: Knowing that the value of a home can be influenced by neighboring property, the value of a home would least likely be influenced by a neighborhood containing:
choices: large expensive homes converted to small condominiums.
questions.explanation: Of the choices given, the vacant lots would have the least affect on value.

questions.prompt: To arrive at a capitalization rate in the appraisal of an income producing property, no provisions should be made for:
questions.explanation: To arrive at a capitalization rate, the appraiser makes an allowance for depreciation or a "return of" the investment. No provisions are made for federal income taxes that might become due on the property income.

questions.prompt: Economic obsolescence would be considered:
questions.explanation: Whether an item of depreciation is curable or incurable depends soley on the cost to cure. Since economic obsolescence is caused by external forces there is usually nothing that can be done to change it.

questions.prompt: The relationship between a property and a prospective purchaser is known as:
questions.explanation: Value can also be described as the relationship between a property and a prospective purchaser. The most probable price a property should bring in a competitive and open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale (market value).

questions.prompt: Which is the least important in appraising property using the cost approach?
questions.explanation: Income is not considered when using the cost approach method.

questions.prompt: In appraisal, the adjustment process, whereby, comparables are adjusted to the subject property is known as:
questions.explanation: In appraisal, reconcilation is the process of interpreting the data gathered by bringing the various value estimates into mutual relationship with one another to determine a final estimate of value. With this process, the comparables are always adjusted to the subject property.

questions.prompt: A cul-de-sac is which of the following?
questions.explanation: A cul-de-sac is a dead-end street or a street open at only one end.

questions.prompt: A homeowner builds a $1,200,000 house among $675,000 to $900,000 homes. A loss in value suffered by the expensive home would be best attributed to:
questions.explanation: This would be considered economic obsolescence. Functional obsolescence occurs inside the property lines. Physical deterioration refers to deferred maintenance.

questions.prompt: What part or portion of the narrative report contains the estimate of value?
questions.explanation: The letter of transmittal identifies the property, purpose of the appraisal, methods used, and value estimate.

questions.prompt: A corner lot would most likely add value to:
questions.explanation: Retail property would benefit from the added traffic and visual exposure of a corner lot.

questions.prompt: Evans owns a new personal residence. The transportation agency is widening the street in front of his residence. This will cause Evans to lose 10 feet along the front of his property which borders the street. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Any loss in value would be considered economic obsolescence because it is caused by a force which is outside the property lines.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in the appraisal process?
questions.explanation: The first step in the appraisal process is to write a concise statement of the appraisal problem.

questions.prompt: Any loss in value due to placing a building in an incompatible neighborhood would be an example of:
questions.explanation: The fact that neighboring properties are hurting the value of a building would indicate that it is suffering from economic obsolescence.

questions.prompt: What is a "fee appraiser?"
choices: An appraiser who works for a lending institution.
A certified appraiser who works on salary.
An appraiser who works for a federally insured lender.
An independent appraiser who works on a fee basis.
questions.explanation: A fee appraiser is a non-salaried professional who furnishes appraisal services for a fee.

questions.prompt: An appraiser is appraising a property which is next door to an abandoned gas station. The appraiser should recommend a:
questions.explanation: There is a possibility that the old underground fuel storage tanks used by the gas station were left in the ground and may be leaking. A toxic waste study would require a soil analysis to determine if the tanks have leaked. A soil engineering study is used to test the soil's ability to support a structure. (See Toxic Substance Control Act)

questions.prompt: The principle of anticipation applies when using the:
questions.explanation: The income approach estimates value based on the amount of net income a property is anticipated to produce over its remaining economic life.

questions.prompt: Depression, expansion, prosperity, and recession are all terms related to the:
questions.explanation: Depression, expansion, prosperity, and recession are all terms that refer to the business cycle.

questions.prompt: The effect of depreciation is:
choices: the property is hard to sell.
depreciation continues until the basis is zero.
questions.explanation: Basis, as it relates to income property goes down each year as the owner deducts depreciation. It may also go up with the addition of capital improvements. Basis or book value will never reach zero because the land does not depreciate.

questions.prompt: A property with great amenity value would best be appraised by using the:
questions.explanation: The comparison method would be used in this case by adjusting comparables to compensate for the amenities of the subject property.

questions.prompt: When using the building residual technique, the unknown value is the value of the:
questions.explanation: The building residual technique is used to determine the value of the building only.

questions.prompt: A loss in value due to a city sewer system in poor condition would be classified as:
questions.explanation: A poor sewer system is an outside influence and is considered economic obsolescence.

questions.prompt: When an appraiser uses the term "adjusted sales prices" when describing comparables, he/she is referring to:
choices: sales price plus adjustments for inflation.
sales price plus or minus adjustments for specific characteristics.
questions.explanation: Adjusted Sales Price: In appraisal, increases or decreases to the sales price of a comparable property are made to arrive at an indicated value for the property being appraised.

questions.prompt: What is excess land in the matter of site analysis?
choices: Land not needed to accommodate the site's primary highest and best use.
Land which exceeds that needed to serve or support the existing improvements on the site.
Land identified with sites larger than other marketable lots in the area.
questions.explanation: Each statement relates to different ways an appraiser describes excess land.

questions.prompt: Wear and tear to the load bearing members of a building would be classified as:
questions.explanation: Physical damage to the load bearing members of a building would usually be considered too expensive to repair. If it is too expensive to repair, it is classified as incurable.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an appraiser's primary concern in the appraisal of residential property?
questions.explanation: If a residential property is not marketable, it is worthless.

questions.prompt: The income approach would NOT be used when appraising:
questions.explanation: When there are no suitable comparables or in this case no income to capitalize, the income approach is not a viable method.

questions.prompt: Which would be considered economic obsolescence?
questions.explanation: Economic obsolescence concerns influences outside the property limits and would include a blighted neighborhood.

questions.prompt: When using the cost approach, the appraiser may estimate the cost of reconstruction based on its "reproduction" cost or its "replacement" cost. "Reproduction" cost is:
choices: The cost to replace the current improvements with another structure.
An estimate of the actual cost of the building when originally constructed.
The cost to build an exact replica using the actual materials and design of the present building.
The cost to remodel the existing structure so it meets current building codes.
questions.explanation: "Reproduction" cost is the cost of reconstructing a replica of the existing structure using the same design and materials.

questions.prompt: Putting aside money each year for five consecutive years to replace the roof is an example of:
questions.explanation: A "sinking fund" is established to gradually amass enough money to satisfy a debt or to meet a specific requirement. The sinking fund method of depreciation contemplates periodic investments of equal amounts of money in a compound-interest-bearing account whereby the investment plus the compound interest will be used to replace the improvement at the end of its economic life.

questions.prompt: Both buildings and neighborhoods alike generally exist in one of four life cycle stages; these are:
questions.explanation: Both buildings and neighborhoods go through life cycles. As they are developed, they achieve growth, attain a period of equilibrium (or stability) in which little change is evident, then decline as properties deteriorate. Then, if warranted, they are repaired and undergo a fourth stage, revitalization.

questions.prompt: Which appraisal method values electrical work by number of light fixtures per square yard?
questions.explanation: The unit-in-place method, is a method for computing replacement cost which uses prices for various building components as installed, based on specific units of use such as square footage or cubic footage. For example, insulation may cost $.07 per square foot, drywall $1.50 per square yard, painting $.08 per square foot, and so on.

questions.prompt: An appraiser using the cost method can use the unit cost per square foot or per cubic foot in his/her computations. On a unit cost basis:
choices: a small house would cost more than a large house.
a small house would cost less than a large house.
a large house would cost more than a small house.
the cost would be the same for a small house as a large house.
questions.explanation: The cost of the essential core items such as the kitchen and bathrooms (which are usually the most expensive to produce) would be prorated over a smaller number of square feet so the unit cost would be higher in a small house.

questions.prompt: How would an appraiser define the boundaries of a residential neighborhood?
questions.explanation: A neighborhood is defined as a contiguous area showing common social characteristics.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be included when estimating the value of an income property using the capitalization approach?
questions.explanation: Management expenses should be considered when using the capitalization approach. Loan payments are not considered in capitalizing net income.

questions.prompt: When analyzing the income produced by a property, an appraiser is concerned with:
questions.explanation: All of these are important factors to consider when calculating net income for capitalization purposes.

questions.prompt: The objective value of a property is closest to:
questions.explanation: Objective value is what a reasonable person ends up paying for a property.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which would most likely be the highest value?
questions.explanation: The other choices would most likey be lower than market value.

questions.prompt: In the appraisal of residential property, the cost approach is most appropriate in the case of:
questions.explanation: Cost estimates per square foot can more easily be ascertained with new property. This is not to imply that the cost approach is always the best method for the appraisal of new property.

questions.prompt: Of the following, value is best described as:
questions.explanation: This definition of value is most applicable to income producing properties. The "present worth of future benefits" have to do with the projected income stream.

questions.prompt: The measurement or the length of road that abuts a thoroughfare is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Frontage is a term used to describe or identify that part of a parcel of land or an improvement on the land which faces the street.

questions.prompt: Which of the following has the least to do with market value?
questions.explanation: Book value is the adjusted basis of an asset and usually differs from appraised value or market value.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct regarding the adjustment process for a Comparative Market Analysis (CMA)?
choices: adjust both the subject property and comparable properties
questions.explanation: When completing a Comparative Market Analysis (CMA), adjustments are made to the comparable properties value to remove or add, as much as possible, the differences between your subject property and the comparable properties. Adjustments are made to the comparable properties to show if they are superior or inferior to the subject property.

questions.prompt: In order for demand to be effective, it must be implemented by:
questions.explanation: The element of value known as "demand" is rendered ineffective by lack of purchasing power.

questions.prompt: When using the land residual technique, the goal is to establish the value of the:
questions.explanation: The land residual technique is a method of estimating the value of land through the capitalization of income used when the value of the land is not known.

questions.prompt: A four-bedroom house with a one-car garage would be an example of:
questions.explanation: Functional obsolescence is a loss in the value of a property resulting from a deficiency in the floor plan of a house. A one-car garage would be inadequate for the four bedroom house.

questions.prompt: The period over which a property may be profitably utilized is called its:
questions.explanation: Economic life is the estimated period over which it is anticipated that a property may be profitably utilized.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best expression of why real estate has value?
questions.explanation: Maximum utilization of available resources relates to highest and best use.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would most likely lower the value of a single-family residence?
questions.explanation: Deferred maintenance is physical deterioration or loss in value of a building resulting from postponed maintenance to the building.

questions.prompt: What is least important to an appraiser?
questions.explanation: Location, recent comparable sales, and square footage are all important to an appraiser. Creative financing to facilitate the sale of the subject property may be a factor but is the least important of the choices.

questions.prompt: An appraiser would most likely use a depth table when confronted with a valuation problem involving:
questions.explanation: Depth tables are tables of percentage used to provide a uniform system of measuring the additional value of lots which may be more valuable because of added depth. Depth tables are used on vacant land usually for commercial property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following approaches to real estate appraisal is concerned with "the present worth of future benefits" of a property?
questions.explanation: The income approach is based on the theory that the present worth or value of an income property is the present worth of future net income.

questions.prompt: What is meant by the expression "turnkey project?"
choices: low income, federally funded housing project
a development where everything is ready for the buyer to move in
a development where there is a lock-box on each door
questions.explanation: A turnkey project is a development term meaning the complete construction package from ground breaking to building completion. All that is left undone is to "turn over the keys" to the buyer.

questions.prompt: When appraising a commercial property, an appraiser would be least interested in:
questions.explanation: The value of commercial property is more often derived from its income earning potential.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to appraise a land site?
questions.explanation: The allocation method (also called the abstraction or extraction method) is an appraisal method whereby the appraiser estimates the land value of any improved property by deducting or abstracting the value of any site improvements from the overall sales price of the property. The amount remaining is the estimated sales price or indicated value of the land.

questions.prompt: An appraiser employed to appraise a commercial strip mall valued at $550,000 must hold which of the following appraisal licenses?
questions.explanation: There are different levels of appraiser licenses issued by the Office of Real Estate Appraisers (OREA). A certified general appraiser's license would be required to appraise a commercial strip mall valued at $550,000.

questions.prompt: Property that is very seldom sold would be appraised by which of the following appraisal techniques?
questions.explanation: An example of property that is seldom sold would be government buildings or churches. There is usually no comparative information available on these types of properties. The cost approach relates to construction information which is readily available.

questions.prompt: In an appraisal, the term "utility value" would most nearly be described as:
questions.explanation: Utility value is the value in use to an owner-user. A property that has no utility has no value.

questions.prompt: The economic life of improved property is which of the following in relation to the physical life?
choices: depends on the type of building
questions.explanation: Economic life is the estimated period over which an improved property may be profitably utilized so it will yield a return. The physical life is the estimated period during which a physical thing is habitable if normally maintained. Typically, physical life is expected to be longer than economic life.

questions.prompt: Demand being equal:
questions.explanation: This is an example of supply and demand.

questions.prompt: An appraisal under the cost approach method, places the value of landscaping, fences and walkways:
questions.explanation: Landscaping, fences, and walkways are considered as improvements or simply as part of the land.

questions.prompt: A $1,260,000 house, having been built among $700,000 to $900,000 homes, would eventually see its value go down. This influence on the value of the $1,260,000 house is known as:
questions.explanation: Principle of Regression: Between dissimilar properties, the worth of the better property is adversely affected by the presence of the lesser-quality property. Regression is considered economic obsolescence.

questions.prompt: An appraiser was hired by Williams to appraise Henderson's property. With whom should the appraiser discuss his findings?
questions.explanation: The results of an appraisal are confidential.

questions.prompt: Amenities are:
choices: features that add to the value or desirability of a property.
items of personal property that may be depreciated.
capital improvements that add to the cost basis.
questions.explanation: Amenities are features both tangible and intangible that enhance and add to the value or desirability of real estate. In a condominium for example, common amenities include a swimming pool, clubhouse, and a good view.

questions.prompt: The "Statement of Purpose" section of a narrative appraisal report would contain which of the following?
choices: The type of value being given
questions.explanation: The type of value being given is stated in the "Statement of Purpose." Appraisals are used for various reasons (i.e., loans, insurance, taxation, public acquisition).

questions.prompt: The most important economic consideration in relationship to land is:
choices: the items affixed to the land
questions.explanation: Scarcity is a lack of supply of some type of real property, the supply of which cannot readily be increased. Scarcity results in increased value when demand exceeds supply.

questions.prompt: Which of the following comparables would be the most helpful in appraising a home?
choices: A similar home sold for nonpayment of taxes.
A similar property sold under duress.
A similar home sold by a motivated seller to a motivated buyer.
A similar home sold by an unwilling seller to an unsure buyer.
questions.explanation: This relates to the "willing seller, willing buyer" concept of value.

questions.prompt: If interest rates on loans increase, capitalization rates would tend to:
questions.explanation: The "return on" part of the capitalization rate is the same as interest. If interest rates increase, the capitalization rate increases.

questions.prompt: You are preparing a competitive market analysis on a vacant lot that you hope to list for sale. Which of the following approaches to value will be used in the development of the estimated value?
questions.explanation: The sales comparison approach is most applicable to the appraisal of vacant land. The cost approach is most applicable to the appraisal of special purpose properties such as a church. The gross rent multiplier is used as a substitute for the income approach in the valuation of a single-family home. The income approach is used in the appraisal of an income-producing property.

questions.prompt: The effectiveness of the market data approach would be limited most by:
choices: the types of properties that are regularly sold.
questions.explanation: If economic conditions are rapidly changing, it is difficult to make the adjustments to the price of comparable properties.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the best (or most common) appraisal method used to calculate replacement cost?
questions.explanation: There are 4 major methods of estimating the reproduction or replacement cost: 1) Square-foot method; 2) Unit-in-place method; 3) Quantity survey method; and 4) Index method. The Square-foot method (aka Comparison method) is the one typically used by appraisers and real estate licensees in estimating replacement and/or construction costs. The Square-foot method takes the cost per square foot of a recently developed comparable property and multiplies it by the square footage, using the external dimensions of the structures of the subject property.

questions.prompt: The hardest and yet most important part of the market data method of appraising is:
choices: adjusting for differences between the comparable and the subject property.
analyzing the volume of sales data.
collecting a sufficient volume of sales data.
questions.explanation: The most difficult part of the market data method of appraising is adjusting for differences in the properties.

questions.prompt: All of the following are recognized methods of appraisal EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: There is no appraisal method known as the "economic" method. Allocation and extraction are methods of land or site valuation.

questions.prompt: The immediate surroundings of real estate is important because:
choices: property in an unattractive neighborhood won't sell.
questions.explanation: Real estate is immovable by nature and cannot escape its immediate surroundings.

questions.prompt: The increase of value with the passage of time describes:
questions.explanation: Appreciation is a temporary or permanent increase in the worth or value of property due to economic causes, the opposite of depreciation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following appraisal techniques require a separate estimate for the value of the land?
questions.explanation: The primary steps of the cost approach are to (1) estimate the land value, (2) estimate the replacement cost of the building new, (3) deduct all accrued depreciation from the replacement cost and (4) add the estimated land value to the depreciated replacement cost.

questions.prompt: Two buildings are located in the same area of comparable size, both under long-term leases. One is leased to the government for a post office and the other for a hardware store. Using the income capitalization approach to appraise the properties, which of the following is correct?
choices: The same capitalization rate for both
A lower capitalization rate for the hardware store
A higher capitalization rate for the hardware store
Proportional capitalization rates based on the different uses
questions.explanation: Part of the capitalization rate measures the risk involved in an investment. Thus, the higher the risk the higher the CAP rate; the lower the the risk the lower the CAP rate. Leasing a building for a hardware store involves higher risk of vacancy than leasing for a post office and results in a higher CAP rate.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of functional obsolescence?
questions.explanation: An ornate cornice is an outdated architectural design classified as functional obsolescence. A deteriorated driveway would be physical deterioration. New zoning laws and inharmonious land use would be examples of economic obsolescence.

questions.prompt: The basic valuation principle underlying the market approach is:
questions.explanation: The Principle of Substitution is the basis of all appraisal techniques in determining property value. Simply stated, value will tend to be set by the cost of acquiring an equally desirable substitute.

questions.prompt: An appraiser would use which of the following approaches in appraising a shopping center?
questions.explanation: The shopping center would regularly produce income and would be valued using the capitalization (income) approach to value.

questions.prompt: An appraiser using the cost approach to appraise property would be least concerned about the economy in the area of the subject property when appraising:
choices: A store in a residential area
A strip shopping mall in a residential area
questions.explanation: An electronic assembly plant is producing products which will not depend on the local economy. The products will be distributed either nationally or internationally. The value of the other three choices would be directly affected by the local economy.

questions.prompt: Offers to purchase by prospective buyers will tend to set:
questions.explanation: Sellers list high and buyers usually offer to pay less than they might agree to pay. In bargaining circumstances, asking prices establish the upper limit for prices in an area while offers to purchase will set the lower limit to which prices might fall.

questions.prompt: An appraiser would determine the value of an apartment building by:
questions.explanation: The income capitalization method analyzes a property's anticipated future income.

questions.prompt: An increase in value as a result of taking several small parcels and joining them together to form a larger parcel is called:
questions.explanation: Assemblage is the combining of two or more adjoining lots into one large tract. This is usually done to increase the value of the individual lots because a larger building capable of producing a larger net return may be erected on a larger parcel. The resulting added value is called plottage value.

questions.prompt: All of the following would influence the value of a commercial lot EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The fertility of the soil applies to agricultural land.

questions.prompt: After capitalizing the net income of a property and then deducting the replacement cost of the improvements, an appraiser has established the:
questions.explanation: The total value of a property is made up of the value of the land plus improvements.

questions.prompt: In a tight money market, when interest rates are increasing, but rental rates are stable, how do these circumstances influence the market value of real property?
choices: not significant changes on existing rental properties.
questions.explanation: The value of real property decreases during "tight money" conditions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following includes site plans, elevations drawings and street locations?
questions.explanation: Subdivision Map would include all of these.

questions.prompt: The ultimate test of functional utility is:
questions.explanation: Functional utility is defined as the "the ability of a property or building to be useful and to perform the function for which it is intended, according to current market tastes and standards, as well as the efficiency of a building's use in terms of architectural style, design and layout, traffic patterns, and size and type of rooms." The ultimate test of functional utility is marketability. If the property can be marketed for the same price as others in the area, there is no functional obsolescence.

questions.prompt: If the current highest and best use of a property is expected to change, the current use is referred to as the:
questions.explanation: An interim use is some use the property is put to while waiting for some future action that will make another use the most productive or as we say in the business..."it's highest and best use." Interim use is a form of nonconforming use of property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a method of depreciation?
questions.explanation: Obsolescence is NOT a depreciation method, it is a loss in value due to a decrease in the usefulness of property caused by decay, changes in technology, people's behavior, patterns and tastes, or environmental changes. Don't confuse "methods of depreciation" with "causes of depreciation." Obsolescence is a cause of depreciation NOT a method of depreciation as the question asks.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the cost approach method?
choices: It works best with new properties.
It tends to set the upper value of a property.
questions.explanation: Since the cost approach looks at the cost of constructing an identical building with current materials and techniques, it tends to set the upper value of the property. The cost approach is ideal for new properties and special purpose properties that have no comparables in the area or which produce no income - examples are museums, schools, churches, and libraries.

questions.prompt: The quantity survey method, unit-in-place method, and square foot/cubic foot methods of real estate appraisal most directly relate to the:
questions.explanation: In the cost approach, an appraiser may use all of these methods to determine the cost to build.

questions.prompt: The capitalization rate in the income approach provides for "return of" and "return on" the investment. "Return of" refers to:
questions.explanation: An investor is allowed a "return on," his/her investment which is the same as interest, and a "return of" which is depreciation,. The "return on" is the investor's profit. The "return of" allows for depreciation of the wasting asset.

questions.prompt: Which of the following appraisal methods, prices all labor and material in construction?
questions.explanation: The quantity survey method involves a detailed estimate of the quantities of raw materials used (lumber, plaster, brick, cement), as well as the current price of the material and installation costs. It also includes indirect costs, such as building permit, land survey, and overhead.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best identifies the three phases normally involved in a single-family dwelling?
choices: Construction proposal, map approval, and buyer qualification
questions.explanation: These are the 3 stages of building a single-family dwelling.

questions.prompt: Restoring an old home to its original condition without making any changes in the floor plan or style is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Rehabilitation is the restoration of a property to a satisfactory condition without changing the plan, form, or style of the structure.

questions.prompt: An owner of a property which was located near an airport was constantly bothered by the noise of low flying aircraft. He wanted to bring court action and force the city to condemn the property because of the noise. This would be an example of:
questions.explanation: Inverse condemnation: An action for just compensation brought by a person whose property has been effectively taken, substantially interfered with, or taken without just compensation. For example, when a governmental authority announces it will condemn an owner's property and then unduly delays in taking the property, the owner can bring legal action to force a condemnation and payment for the taking.

questions.prompt: A gross rent multiplier is obtained by:
choices: dividing gross monthly rent by the property's value.
dividing gross monthly rent by the selling price.
dividing sales price by gross monthly rent.
dividing net income by the gross monthly rent.
questions.explanation: The gross rent multiplier is obtained by dividing the sales price or value by the gross monthly rent.

questions.prompt: Capitalization is a process whereby an appraiser:
choices: finds gross income of equity capital.
questions.explanation: Capitalization is a mathematical process used in estimating the value of income producing property by applying a certain capitalization rate to the net operating income.

questions.prompt: Two different properties are located side-by-side in the same neighborhood. They were both built by the same contractor, at the same time, for the same cost, are maintained the same, and contain the same square footage. If one property is worth less than the other, it would be due to:
questions.explanation: The only possible difference is that the properties do not look the same. All forces and factors that could influence value operate on both properties. Possibly the floor plans are different. The difference must be architectural and is considered functional obsolescence.

questions.prompt: A flight pattern to a nearby airport was changed so that planes pass over a single-family residential neighborhood. Any loss in value to these properties would be attributed to:
questions.explanation: This outside influence is considered economic obsolescence.

questions.prompt: The principle of "highest and best use" refers to the use:
choices: that produces the greatest net income attributable to the land.
that produces the largest gross income.
of improvements best adapted to the architectural style and design of the neighborhood.
questions.explanation: Highest and best use refers to use of land. It is that use of the land that will produce the greatest net income designated and credited to the land.

questions.prompt: When using the market-data approach to appraise a single-family home, recent sales are compared to the subject property as to:
questions.explanation: When using the Market Data Approach, the entire property is examined for comparison purposes.

questions.prompt: Market value is determined by:
questions.explanation: Market Value: The most probable price a property should bring in a competitive and open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale. It is assumed that the buyer and seller acted prudently and knowledgeably, and that the price is not affected by undue stimulus.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the biggest problem in using the cost approach to appraise an older building?
choices: construction materials and methods have changed
lack of comparable properties recently sold
questions.explanation: For appraisal purposes, accrued depreciation is the difference between the cost to reproduce the property (as of the appraisal date) and the property's current value as judged by its condition. Accrued depreciation is difficult to estimate on very old properties.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items is NOT deducted from gross income to determine net income for capitalization purposes?
questions.explanation: Interest payments are not considered an expense when estimating the value of the property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following appraisal reports is the most complete and detailed?
questions.explanation: A narrative report is a complete document including all pertinent information about the area and the subject property, as well as the reasons and computations for the value consideration. It includes maps, photographs, charts, and plot plans.

questions.prompt: Value is best described as:
questions.explanation: Value is generally described as the amount of money deemed to be the equivalent in worth of the subject property. Cost does not equal value nor does equity.

questions.prompt: As far as sales are concerned, the most important date on an appraisal is the:
choices: date of acceptance of the offer.
questions.explanation: Since the value could change for a variety of reasons during escrow, the most important date on an appraisal is the date escrow closes or in this question the date of recording.

questions.prompt: In order to accurately calculate a gross rent multiplier, what data would an appraiser obtain from comparable properties:
choices: Original cost and the annual income
Annual rent and the selling price
Net income and the capitalization rate
questions.explanation: The gross rent multiplier is arrived at by dividing the monthly or annual gross rent into the selling price of the property.

questions.prompt: The subjective value of a property is the:
questions.explanation: Since value sometimes depends on the use by a specific owner, it tends to be considered subjective.

questions.prompt: The most difficult step in applying the income approach in the appraisal of income property is:
choices: verifying the income and expense records.
locating similar properties to make a market comparison.
questions.explanation: Capitalization rates are usually established by examining established rates on similar properties. Since few comparables are usually available, it can be difficult to establish an accurate rate.

questions.prompt: When performing an appraisal for insurance purposes, an appraiser would be concerned with:
questions.explanation: Valuation for insurance purposes is concerned with replacement cost.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the three great forces affecting value?
questions.explanation: Real estate undergoes constant change from physical, economic, social, and political forces.

questions.prompt: If a building is in exceptionally good condition, its effective age is:
choices: the same as its actual age.
depends on the type of building.
questions.explanation: Effective age is the apparent age of a building based on observed condition rather than chronological age. The effective age of improvements to real property at the time of inspection differs from actual age by such variable factors as depreciation, quality of maintenance, and the like.

questions.prompt: What is the most expensive and most difficult type of appraisal?
questions.explanation: The quantity survey method of appraisal is a highly technical process that requires the appraiser to list every item of material and the cost to install it in the building. It is a very detailed and expensive way to appraise a building.

questions.prompt: The redemption period for unpaid real property taxes is:
choices: five years from the assessment date.
five years from the tax default date.
five years from the sale by the state at public auction.
five years from loss of possession.
questions.explanation: If there are ANY unpaid taxes as of 5 p.m. on June 30 (end of the fiscal tax year), then the property becomes "tax defaulted." If the property has not been redeemed within five years after the initial declaration of default, the property will become subject to the tax collector's power of sale.

questions.prompt: A broker is acting as the agent of the seller in a transaction in which the seller carried back a second trust deed. The broker must cause the deed of trust to be recorded or advise the seller to record the trust deed:
choices: within one week after close of escrow.
one business day after close of escrow.
none of the preceding as this is not the responsibility of the agent.
questions.explanation: Within one week after closing of a transaction, the broker must cause a deed of trust to be recorded with the county recorder or cause it to be delivered to the beneficiary with a written recommendation that it be recorded forthwith, unless written instructions not to record are received from the beneficiary. If the transaction is closed through escrow and the deed of trust is delivered to the escrow holder within one week, that shall be deemed compliance on the part of the broker.

questions.prompt: The marginal tax rate is the tax rate:
choices: that will be used when you enter the next higher tax bracket.
which is used for the last dollar of taxable income earned.
applied to the highest tax bracket.
applied to the lowest tax bracket.
questions.explanation: The marginal tax rate is the ordinary rate of income tax charged on the last dollar of income, often used when making calculations for investment decisions.

questions.prompt: An escrow agent discovers there is no specified date of closing. In this case, escrow should close:
questions.explanation: If a specific closing date is not specified, the parties may agree in writing to a closing date, otherwise, the escrow would continue and close within a reasonable period of time.

questions.prompt: A home was purchased on February 1st with the understanding that property taxes had been paid for the fiscal tax year. The buyer received a tax bill anyway known as a:
questions.explanation: The supplemental tax bill would adjust for an increase in tax liability for the balance of the tax year.

questions.prompt: The first person to make an acknowledgment on a deed is the:
questions.explanation: The maker acknowledges the deed first by his/her signature before a notary public.

questions.prompt: On an escrow closing statement, due and unpaid taxes are listed as:
choices: a credit to the buyer only.
a debit to the seller always.
either a debit or credit to the buyer or seller depending on the situation.
questions.explanation: Due and unpaid taxes are prorated and can either be debits or credits for the buyer or seller since the buyer must pay the seller's tax obligation.

questions.prompt: Mr. Kwan has a $30,000 loss on the operation of his rental property. This is his only rental investment. With respect to his income tax, he may do which of the following?
choices: Write off $10,000 per year for 3 years
Offset this loss against capital gains
Take the full loss against his personal income
questions.explanation: The $30,000 may be used to offset capital gains for income tax purposes. If he has no capital gains, the maximum loss that may be deducted would be $25,000 with the remaining as a "carryover" loss against future gains.

questions.prompt: When a deed is recorded, according to law:
questions.explanation: It is logical to presume that the grantor intended to deliver the deed if his/her signature has been acknowledged by a notary public, which is required for the recording of a deed. A deed must be delivered to be effective, but does not have to be recorded. Recording establishes presumption of delivery.

questions.prompt: An ALTA policy of title insurance protects the:
Street assessments are distributed to those that benefit by which method?
questions.explanation: Street assessments are levied according to the front footage of the lot benefited.

questions.prompt: What kind of deed clears minor imperfections on the title of real property?
questions.explanation: A quitclaim deed is often used to cure an imperfection or defect (a "cloud on the title") in the recorded history of a real estate title. Title defects include items such as issues with wording (for example, a document does not comply with state standards), a missing signature (such as that of a spouse) or failure to properly record real estate documents. For example, if the name of a grantee is misspelled on a warranty deed placed in the public record, a quitclaim deed with the correct spelling can be executed to the grantee to perfect the title.

questions.prompt: Tax consequences with respect to real estate should take place:
questions.explanation: At any other time, it may be too late.

questions.prompt: A real property sales contract represents a tax advantage because:
choices: it defers payment of capital gains.
questions.explanation: A real property sales contract (formerly referred to as an "installment land sale contract") allows the taxpayer to postpone the receipt and reporting of income tax to future years when his/her other income may be lower. Thus, a taxpayer can avoid paying the entire tax on the gain in the year of sale.

questions.prompt: What type of title insurance policy covers all risks?
