questions.explanation: No title insurance policy covers all risks. It is a good idea to familiarize yourself with the various types of title insurance policies and their coverage.

questions.prompt: Real property taxes become a lien on:
questions.explanation: Next year's real property taxes become a lien on January 1st.

questions.prompt: Tax delinquent real property not redeemed by the owner during the five year statutory redemption period is deeded to the:
questions.explanation: If the property is not redeemed by the owner during this statutory redemption period, the property is deeded to the state.

questions.prompt: Who may obtain a copy of a termite report after it has been filed with the Structural Pest Control Board?
choices: Only the escrow agent involved in the transaction
Any agent or party involved in the transaction
questions.explanation: Anyone may search the Structural Pest Control Board's system to see if a specific property has been inspected within the last two years.

questions.prompt: How would a taxpayer adjust the tax basis of his/her personal residence for Federal tax purposes?
questions.explanation: The tax basis on a personal residence consists of the cost of the property plus capital improvements like the addition of a concrete patio.

questions.prompt: When a real estate licensee accepts trust funds from his/her client in connection with the purchase of real property, the licensee must place these funds in: 1) a neutral escrow depository; 2) the hands of the offeree or owner; or 3) a trust account. The licensee must place these funds into one of these three authorized places:
choices: by the next working day following receipt.
within three business days following receipt.
by midnight of the current day.
by midnight of the second business day following receipt.
questions.explanation: If the broker or broker's salesperson fails to place the funds into one of these three authorized places within three business days following receipt, he/she is liable for commingling the funds.

questions.prompt: During a sales escrow, the escrow officer receives two structural pest control reports. The escrow officer should:
choices: contact the inspection companies to determine which one is most recent.
send the report that requires the most work to the buyer and obtain his/her approval.
notify the broker and obtain written instruction from the buyer and seller concerning the reports.
request the broker to find out from the seller which report to use.
questions.explanation: The escrow agent is the agent of both the buyer and the seller, and should receive instructions from both if a conflict arises such as this.

questions.prompt: If Johnson's intent is to accomplish a "tax-free" exchange of his apartment building, he should exchange for:
choices: an apartment building of greater value with boot paid to balance the trade.
an apartment building of equal value with Johnson receiving net mortgage relief.
a smaller, less expensive apartment building and take cash boot to make up the difference.
an owner-occupied, single-family residence of equal or greater value.
questions.explanation: All choices except (a) would result in tax consequences.

questions.prompt: A quitclaim deed conveys only the present right, title and interest of the:
questions.explanation: The quitclaim deed transfers only whatever right, title and interest the grantor had in the property at the time of the execution of the deed and does not pass to the grantee any title or interest subsequently acquired by the grantor (after-acquired title).

questions.prompt: A title plant refers to the title records of properties in a:
questions.explanation: A title plant is an accumulation of title records in a specific county.

questions.prompt: An exception in a grant deed:
choices: makes the deed invalid to future grantees.
has no effect on the property value.
withdraws a portion of the property from the grant.
questions.explanation: An exception in a grant deed means the grantor is holding back part of the estate being granted. This would withdraw part of the property from the grant deed and reduce the property or rights given to the grantee.

questions.prompt: For tax purposes, points paid by the seller would:
choices: be treated as a selling expense.
questions.explanation: When the seller pays points, he/she may deduct this cost as a selling expense. This will increase the cost basis and reduce capital gains. Buyer points are treated as interest.

questions.prompt: The unadjusted basis of a taxpayer's residence would be:
questions.explanation: For federal income tax purposes in determining gain or loss on real property, the term "unadjusted basis" most nearly means "original cost."

questions.prompt: Which of the following is required for a couple to qualify for the "Universal Exclusion" from capital gains?
choices: Occupancy of your primary residence for at least 24 consecutive months you owned the home during the 5 years leading up to the date of sale.
Your home must be your primary residence for at least 24 of the months you owned the home during the 5 years leading up to the date of sale.
Your home must be your primary residence for at least 12 of the months you owned the home during the 5 years leading up to the date of sale.
Occupancy of your primary residence for at least 12 consecutive months you owned the home during the 5 years leading up to the date of sale.
questions.explanation: To qualify for the Universal Exclusion from capital gains, your home must be your primary residence for at least 24 of the months you owned the home during the 5 years leading up to the date of sale. The 24 months of residence can fall anywhere within the 5-year period. It doesn't even have to be a single block of time. All you need is a total of 24 months (730 days) of residence during the 5-year period.

questions.prompt: When there is a substantial discrepancy between the dates for close of escrow and the new owners occupying the property, the agent must prepare a(n):`
questions.explanation: Closing delays can occur due to a number of reasons. For example, delays in obtaining a homeowner's insurance policy or if the funding check from the buyer's lender isn't issued in time. Sometimes work on the property needs to be completed before close of escrow. Another common reason for a delay is when two home sales are closing concurrently and a delay in one causes a delay in the other. Ideally, buyers shouldn't take possession of their new homes until the sale has closed. As a last resort, the buyer can ask the seller for permission to occupy the property before the closing and if the seller agrees, an interim occupancy agreement should be signed by the buyer and seller, and the buyer's personal and liability insurance should be in effect as of the date of occupancy.

questions.prompt: A Notary Public can do all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: Witness and authenticate the execution of documents
questions.explanation: A Notary’s duty is to screen the signers of important documents — such as property deeds, wills and powers of attorney — for their true identity, their willingness to sign without duress or intimidation, and their awareness of the contents of the document or transaction. Some notarizations also require the Notary to put the signer under an oath, declaring under penalty of perjury that the information contained in a document is true and correct. A Notary Public cannot demand or accept promissory notes – this is typically done in escrow.

questions.prompt: The buyer and seller agree on a 60-day escrow. As the closing date approaches, it becomes obvious that it will not close on time. Which of the following is TRUE?
choices: The escrow can close as originally scheduled.
The escrow is automatically terminated after 60 days.
The buyer and seller must agree to extend the escrow or it is cancelled.
The escrow agent has the authority to extend the escrow.
questions.explanation: If the escrow cannot be completed on time, the escrow would terminate unless both parties agreed in writing to an extension. This would be accomplished with an amendment to the escrow instructions extending the closing date.

questions.prompt: A Standard Policy of Title Insurance covers all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: lack of signature of either husband and/or wife.
questions.explanation: Zoning is excluded from the coverage of title insurance. The standard policy also does not protect the policyholder against defects in title known to the holder to exist at the date of the policy and not previously disclosed to the insurance company.

questions.prompt: The term impounds refers to:
questions.explanation: Impounds are monies set aside (reserves) to cover future payments of recurring costs such as taxes and insurance.

questions.prompt: Mr. and Mrs. Homeowner realized a $600,000 profit by selling the home they had lived in for three years. What amount is subject to taxes?
questions.explanation:
Universal Exclusion (two year rule): In 1997, the old 24 month trade up and 55 year old rules changed. The new law states that there will be no tax on gains up to $250,000 for single people and $500,000 for married people who file joint returns. To qualify, the home must have been your principal residence for at least 2 years during the preceding 5 years prior to sale. Both spouses must have lived there for the 2 year period to get the maximum exemption of $500,000 with joint filing. The full exclusion can only be used once every 2 years.

Solution: $600,000 - 500,000 exclusion = $100,000 taxable amount.

questions.prompt: Buyers' and sellers' closing statements are:
questions.explanation: Separate closing statements are prepared for the buyer and seller showing debits and/or credits at closing. Buyers and sellers always have different closing statements.

questions.prompt: The recording of an instrument gives:
questions.explanation: Constructive notice is knowledge the law presumes a person has about a paritcular fact regardless of whether the person knows about the fact or not. Examples of constructive notice would include the proper recording of a deed in the public records or the physical possession of property by an owner or tenant.

questions.prompt: The document issued to a person as a receipt for paying delinquent taxes on a property owned by another is called a:
questions.explanation: A tax certificate is the document issued to a person as a receipt for paying delinquent taxes on a property owned by another, entitling the person to receive a deed to the property if the property is sold for unpaid taxes and not redeemed within a certain period of time.

questions.prompt: Pest control reports which contain information concerning wood destroying insects are kept on file with the:
choices: United States Department of Insect Control.
questions.explanation: You may search the Board's Wood Destroying Organism System to see if a specific property has been inspected within the last two years.

questions.prompt: A lender uses an impound account to protect against non-payment of all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Mortgage interest is part of the loan payment. The others are held by the lender in a reserve account called impounds. Lender pays these bills as they become due.

questions.prompt: The adjusted basis of a taxpayer's residence would be:
questions.explanation: Since you cannot depreciate your personal residence, the adjusted basis would be cost plus capital improvements.

questions.prompt: How much of a broker's personal funds may be contributed to a client's trust fund bank account to offset any bank service charges?
questions.explanation: Since banks sometimes have service charges; out of necesssity, the broker is allowed to maintain up to $200 of personal funds in a trust account to cover these type of bank charges.

questions.prompt: The purpose of the assessment roll, as compiled by the assessor's office is:
choices: The equalization of the assessments among the various properties
The setting of the tax rates
The establishment of the tax roll
questions.explanation: The assessment roll serves as the tax base.

questions.prompt: Ad valorem is best defined as:
questions.explanation: Ad valorem means according to value.

questions.prompt: During escrow, if an unresolved dispute should arise between the seller and buyer preventing the close of escrow, the escrow holder may legally:
choices: arbitrate the dispute as a neutral party.
rescind the escrow and return all documents and monies to the respective parties.
file an interpleader action in court.
questions.explanation: The escrow holder does not arbitrate arguments between buyer and seller. He/she would most likely file an interpleader action in court. By filing an interpleader action, the escrow agent is asking the court to accept any money or property he or she holds and distribute it to the rightful claimant.

questions.prompt: Under the Street Improvements Act of 1911, how long does an owner have to pay the bill?
questions.explanation: Street improvements assessments must be paid off within 30 days after receipt.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is most likely to pay property taxes?
choices: Income property owner with negative cash flow
questions.explanation: Negative cash flow might be deductible against ordinary income, but not property taxes.

questions.prompt: Which of the following represents one of the essentials of a grant deed:
choices: Parties capable of receiving the grant
questions.explanation:
There are several different essentials to a valid deed, namely:

It must be in writing.

The parties must be properly described.

The parties must be competent to convey and be capable of receiving the grant.

The property conveyed must be adequately described.

There must be a granting clause, operative words or conveyance ("I hereby grant").

The deed must be signed by the party or parties making the conveyance or grant.

Delivery and acceptance is required.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be true about a lis pendens:
choices: It can only be removed by court action
It can be recorded no matter what type of lawsuit it is
It may affect title to real property based on the results of the lawsuit
questions.explanation: A lis pendens is recorded to warn anyone interested in the property, that it is subject to a lawsuit. The property can be sold with the lis pendens filed against it, but the sale may be set aside and the property may be used for execution depending on the results of the lawsuit.

questions.prompt: A property owner builds a swimmimg pool at his apartment building in order to attract more tenants. For tax purposes, he can:
choices: deduct the cost of the pool, dollar-for-dollar, from his income tax.
deduct the cost of the pool from his vacancy losses.
add the cost of the pool to his book value and depreciate it.
questions.explanation: The cost of the pool may be added to the book value (cost basis) and then be depreciated.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be treated as a credit on the seller's closing statement?
questions.explanation: Since this is prepaid insurance, it would be a credit on the seller's closing statement.

questions.prompt: A resident of Nevada dies in Nevada but owns property in California. The probate proceedings for this property would be held in:
questions.explanation: The probate proceedings are held in the state where the property is located.

questions.prompt: What usually happens to a person's property who died intestate?
choices: It is distributed to his/her heirs.
It is distributed according to his/her will.
questions.explanation: Intestate means dying without a will or leaving a defective will. The intestate decedent's property passes to his/her heirs according to the laws of descent in the state where such real property is located.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may NOT engage in the escrow business?
choices: An individual who is not a real estate broker or attorney
questions.explanation: An individual who is NOT an attorney may not engage in the escrow business.

questions.prompt: An escrow prorates based on a:
questions.explanation: Escrow prorates using a 360 day year and a 30 day month.

questions.prompt: In the sale of a business, bulk transfer laws pertain to:
questions.explanation: A "bulk transfer" is any transfer in bulk (not in the ordinary course of the seller's business), of a major part of the materials, inventory, or supplies of the business. The main purpose of the bulk transfer law is to afford a merchant's creditors an opportunity to satisfy their claims against a merchant who owes them money before the merchant can sell assets and vanish with the proceeds.

questions.prompt: The second property tax installment is due and delinquent on:
The doctrine of "first in time, first in right" refers to:
choices: Date and time one signs a contract.
questions.explanation: In California, lien priority (and, therefore, right to payment) is determined by the maxim "first in time, first in right" (Civil Code 2897). Thus, liens that are recorded first have priority over later-recorded liens. The recording statutes were enacted for the purpose of establishing priorities among claims upon property and provide adequate means by which those with an interest in property may protect their rights. Moreover, a properly recorded lien serves as constructive notice of its contents to all subsequent purchasers and encumbrances (Civ. Code 1213).

questions.prompt: A broker can, without being licensed as an escrow, handle the escrow on transactions where he or she:
questions.explanation: A broker may act as an escrow on his/her own sales or on sales in which he/she acts as a principal.

questions.prompt: A recorded deed:
questions.explanation: Delivery presumes acknowledgement and gives constructive notice. Recording establishes presumption of delivery.

questions.prompt: A document that describes the property and any existing encumbrances is called a:
questions.explanation: The preliminary report describes the property and current owner of record, as well as any recorded liens or other encumbrances. The escrow holder reads the report to verify the legal description and to determine if there are any child support liens, taxes, or judgments for which a release will be required prior to the close of escrow. The buyer is required to review and sign acceptance of the preliminary report.

questions.prompt: A title officer of a title insurance company is familiar with an "Abstract of Title" and would know that it is:
choices: where the legal description of the property is found in the title policy.
a written summary of the various recorded documents relating to the title of the subject property.
a standard form of title insurance that is used by most title companies.
an opinion of the title officer as to the condition of the title.
questions.explanation: An abstract of title is a written summary of the recorded documents relating to a particular property. It is no longer used today in favor of a policy of title insurance.

questions.prompt: What does the term "short rate" refer to?
questions.explanation: Short Rate: A higher periodic rate charged for a shorter term than that originally contracted. The increased premium charged by an insurance company on early cancellation of a policy to compensate the insuror for the fact that the original rate charged was calculated on the full period of the policy. This increased charge enters into a buyer's decision whether to assume the seller's existing homeowner's hazard insurance policy or to cancel it and obtain a new policy.

questions.prompt: Mr. Johnson deeds a parcel of land to Mr. Smith, but the deed is never recorded. How can Mr. Smith transfer title back to Mr. Johnson?
choices: simply hand the deed back to Mr. Johnson.
write "void" across the deed, have it notarized, then give it back to Mr. Johnson.
questions.explanation: Once there is a valid delivery and acceptance, the act of the grantee in surrendering the property or destroying the deed will not put title back to the original grantor. To accomplish this, the grantee must execute a new deed back to the original grantor.

questions.prompt: All of the following are usually treated as credits on the seller's closing statement EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: It is important to understand that this can change based on geographic region and custom. Who pays for title insurance is ultimately a negotiable item.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for reporting a sale to the IRS?
questions.explanation: The escrow agent (title company, escrow corporation, etc.) is responsible for reporting sales to the IRS.

questions.prompt: A federal income tax advantage can be realized by:
questions.explanation: Depreciation is an expense deduction that allows for the recovery of the cost of the investment. An installment sale allows one to save on taxes by postponing the receipt and reporting of income to future years. Exchanging property of "like kind" is a popular method of deferring capital gains taxes.

questions.prompt: A will written in the testator's own handwriting is called a:
questions.explanation: A holographic will is written, dated and signed in the testator's handwriting but not witnessed.

questions.prompt: Owner bob owns an apartment complex which is managed by broker X. Owner bob wants to sell his apartments and broker X is the listing broker. Who distributes the security deposit?
questions.explanation: Security deposits technically belong to the tenant. However, they are held by the owner until the tenant leaves and the owner inspects the unit. It is probably true that Broker X must hand the deposits to escrow, but escrow distributes everything at the close to the new buyer. This includes all proration of prepaid rent, taxes etc. The security deposits would be a credit to the buyer.

questions.prompt: A deed would contain all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A valid grant deed requires the signature of the grantor, not the grantee.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE with respect to reserves in an escrow?
choices: The lender holding the reserves pays the same interest rate on funds that savings and loans pay on savings accounts.
They benefit both the trustor and the beneficiary.
The maximum amount cannot exceed five percent of the annual disbursements.
Reserves are required on all homes.
questions.explanation: Reserves in escrow (impound accounts) are there for the benefit of both the trustor (borrower) and the beneficiary (lender). By impounding taxes and insurance, the lender is certain that these debts will be paid. The borrower is also certain that the payment will be made.

questions.prompt: A man appointed by the court to settle the estate of a person who died intestate is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An administrator (male, administratix-female) is appointed by the court when the deceased died without leaving a will (intestate). A devisee is one who receives a gift or real property by will. A testator (male, testatrix-female) is one who makes a will. An executor (male, executrix-female) is the one appointed by the deceased to execute (carry out the terms of) a will.

questions.prompt: By Proposition 13, the annual real estate tax on a parcel of property in California is limited to:
questions.explanation: By Proposition 13, the annual real estate tax on a parcel of property is limited to 1% of its assessed value. This "assessed value," may be increased only by a maximum of 2% per year, until and unless the property has a change of ownership. At the time of the change in ownership the low assessed value may be reassessed to complete current market value which will produce a new base year value for the property, but future assessments are likewise restricted to the 2% annual maximum increase of the new base year value.

questions.prompt: When a valid grant deed is prepared, title passes when:
questions.explanation: A deed must always be signed by the party or parties making the conveyance or grant of the premises, and it must be delivered to the party to whom the property rights are to be transferred. A deed is of no effect unless delivered.

questions.prompt: The California sales tax is a(n):
choices: tax paid on tangible personal property.
tax paid on all personal property.
questions.explanation: The California State Sales Tax is imposed on retailers for the privilege of selling tangible personal property at retail.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would protect a buyer against a right of a party in possession?
questions.explanation: An extended-coverage policy insures the title against matters that might be discovered by an inspection of the premises. Its coverage includes mechanics' liens, tax liens, miscellaneous liens, encumbrances, easements, rights of parties in possession and encroachments which may not be disclosed by the public records.

questions.prompt: When a person dies intestate and no heirs claim his/her property, it reverts to the state by:
questions.explanation: In cases where a decedent dies intestate and there are no heirs capable of inheriting, the property escheats to the state.

questions.prompt: The most important element of proper and effective delivery of a deed is:
choices: knowledge of its existence by grantee.
questions.explanation: The grantor must intend for a deed to be delivered or the deed is not effective. Recording and acknowledgment are not required for the effectiveness of a deed.

questions.prompt: The selling price on a buyer's closing statement is treated as:
questions.explanation: A closing statement is a detailed cash accounting of a real estate transaction prepared by a broker, escrow officer, attorney or other persons designated to process the mechanics of the sales, showing all cash received, all charges and credits made and all cash paid out in the transaction. Selling price on the buyer's closing statement is treated as a debit to the buyer.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is required for the existence of a valid escrow?
choices: A binding contract and conditional delivery
The services of a licensed real estate broker
questions.explanation: A valid escrow cannot exist without a binding contract between buyer and seller and the conditional delivery of transfer documents to a third party.

questions.prompt: Money in an impound account belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Impound accounts usually contain money prepaid by the trustor (buyer).

questions.prompt: The Office of Interstate Land Sales Registration (OILSR) applies to:
choices: development of 100 or more unimproved lots for sale.
questions.explanation: The Office of Interstate Land Sales Registration (OILSR) oversees implementation of the 1968 Interstate Land Sales Full Disclosure Act (ILSA). The Act requires a developer of a subdivision containing 100 or more nonexempt lots to register its subdivision with the DRE. The developer must also provide lot purchasers with a disclosure statement known as a property report before a sales contract is signed.

questions.prompt: What is an imputed interest rate?
choices: An estimated interest rate used instead of the established interest rate associated with a debt.
The rate at which banks loan money.
The interest rate before taking inflation into account.
The annual rate charged for borrowing or earned through an investment.
questions.explanation: An imputed interest rate is an estimated interest rate used instead of the established interest rate associated with a debt. An imputed rate is used because the established rate does not accurately reflect the market rate of interest, or there is no established rate at all. From a real estate/finance standpoint, imputed Interest refers to interest that is considered by the IRS to have been paid for tax purposes, even if no interest payment was made. The IRS uses imputed interest as a tool to collect tax revenues on loans that don't pay interest, or stated interest is very low.

questions.prompt: In order to alienate property you must:
choices: create a cloud on the title.
questions.explanation: Alienation: The act of conveying ownership, title or an interest or estate in real property from one person to another. Property is usually sold or conveyed by voluntary alienation as with a deed or an assignment of lease. Involuntary alienation takes place when property is sold against the owner's will as in a foreclosure sale or a tax sale.

questions.prompt: What kind of deed transfers the title to real property without receipt of consideration?
questions.explanation: A gift deed is a formal written legal document which gives legal ownership in property from one person (commonly referred to as the "donor") to another person. Since the transfer of ownership is based upon a gift, there is no money, or consideration (something of value) exchanged for the transaction.

questions.prompt: Escrow instructions should be:
questions.explanation: Escrow instructions should be executed by both parties to satisfy the requirements of the contract and complete the escrow.

questions.prompt: An exception in a grant deed:
choices: excludes part of the property from the grant.
questions.explanation: An exception in a grant deed excludes some part of the property granted. The title to that withdrawn part remains in the grantor by virtue of the original title rights. For example, a conveyance by Grant Park to Bob Lee of a 10-acre parcel "exception of a strip of land 10 feet wide running along the northerly boundary" constitutes a legal exception.

questions.prompt: Which type of deed has no express or implied covenants or warranties?
questions.explanation: A quitclaim deed transfers only whatever right, title and interest the grantor had in the land at the time of its execution, without any implied covenants or warranty.

questions.prompt: An investor owned less than a 10% interest in an investment group that owns a major income producing property. If the property operates at a sizeable loss for income tax purposes and the investor's adjusted gross income is $100,000, the maximum amount of passive income loss that could be deducted by the investor is:
questions.explanation: Taxpayers having an adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less, can shelter (deduct) real estate losses up to $25,000 of active income (e.g. wages).

questions.prompt: Boot refers:
questions.explanation: Boot is money or other property that is not like-kind, which is given to make up any difference between exchanged properties.

questions.prompt: A standard policy of title insurance covers all of the following EXCEPT:
When using a grant deed, title transfers at the time of:
questions.explanation: Technically, delivery is the legal act of transferring ownership.

questions.prompt: If a property owner believes that the assessed value on his or her property has been set too high, the owner could file a request to seek a reduction from the:
questions.explanation: Each county has an Assessment Appeals Board to which an individual can question their property's value set by the assessor.

questions.prompt: Shortly after a valid escrow is established, both the buyer and seller die. What should the escrow agent do?
questions.explanation: Under something called the "Doctrine of Relation-Back," death of the grantor does not terminate the escrow or revoke the agent's authority to deliver an executed deed. Delivery of the deed to the grantee relates back to the date it was originally deposited with the escrow agent, and it is considered as if the grantor made delivery to the grantee before the grantor's death.

questions.prompt: A deed is recorded and indexed:
choices: by grantor and grantee names alphabetically.
questions.explanation: The County Recorders Office must keep an adequate index system by grantee and grantor names alphabetically.

questions.prompt: Which of the following dates represent the final date the property owner may file for the State Homeowner's Property Tax Exemption?
questions.explanation: A timely filing for the Homeowner's Property Tax Exemption is February 15th. However, if the homeowner does not file before February 15th, he/she may make a late filing up until December 10th.

questions.prompt: An exact history of conveyances and encumbrances affecting the title of property is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A chain of title is the recorded history of matters that affect the title to a specific parcel of real property, such as ownership, encumbrances and liens, beginning with the original recorded source of the title. The chain of title shows the successive changes of ownership, each one linked to the next so that a "chain" is formed.

questions.prompt: When does the broker's commission get paid?
choices: When the broker obtains an offer and communicates acceptance
When the buyer's deposit is logged into escrow
questions.explanation: On the state exam you may see two very similar questions, one asking when the broker's commission is paid and another asking when the broker has earned his/her commission. The broker's commission is paid at close of escrow. The broker has earned his/her commission when the buyer's offer is accepted.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered an ad valorem tax?
questions.explanation: Real estate taxes are assessed according to value.

questions.prompt: Homebuyers are most likely to purchase:
questions.explanation: Most homebuyers purchase a standard policy of title insurance. "ALTA" stands for American Land Title Association and is an extended coverage policy.

questions.prompt: A reservation in a deed:
choices: is a retention of an interest.
questions.explanation: A reservation in a deed is the creation on behalf of the grantor, of a new right issuing from what was granted. A reservation thus is something that did not exist as an independent right before the conveyance. For example, Smith conveys to Jones a 10-acre parcel "reserving to Smith a life estate therein."

questions.prompt: A property sold for a total of $800,000. An existing loan of $100,000 was assumed. What would the Documentary Transfer Tax be?
questions.explanation:
Documentary Transfer Tax is calculated at a rate of 55 cents for each $500 of consideration or fraction thereof. A portion of the total price paid for the property may be exempt because a lien remains on the property.

$800,000 - $100,000 (assumed loan) = $700,000
$700,000 ÷ $500 = 1,400
1,400 x .55 = $770.00

questions.prompt: To determine property taxes on a residence:
choices: assess land and improvements together, then multiply by separate tax rates.
total all land and improvements, then multiply by one tax rate.
assess land and improvements separately and multiply each by a different tax rate.
assess land and improvements separately, then multiply the total by one tax rate.
questions.explanation: Land and improvements are added separately and then multiplied by one tax rate.

questions.prompt: Once an offer has been made and accepted by the seller, the buyer would have:
questions.explanation: Title remains with the owner (seller) until all the contingencies of the contract have been met and escrow closes. When escrow closes, legal title would transfer from the seller to the buyer.

questions.prompt: A valid deed must contain:
questions.explanation: A valid deed must have a granting clause or some words to indicate that the grantor wishes to transfer the property to the grantee ("I hereby grant").

questions.prompt: On an escrow closing statement, an existing mortgage that is to be assumed by the buyer is treated as:
questions.explanation: A loan being assumed by the buyer is listed as a credit to the buyer and a debit to the seller.

questions.prompt: Baker sells a property to Davis and executes a grant deed in favor of Davis. Davis then takes the deed and places it in a safety deposit box. Baker then sells the same property to Charles who subsequently records it. Which of the following is correct?
choices: Davis can sue Baker for fraud.
Charles is the legal owner of the property.
Davis is the legal owner of the property.
Any loan on the property would be void.
questions.explanation: The first to record is the legal owner. The only exceptions to the recording statute would involve possession or actual notice, neither of these apply in the example. Davis had the right to record and failed to do so.

questions.prompt: A will is said to be ambulatory because it can be:
questions.explanation: The legal definition of ambulatory is "not fixed; alterable." A will takes effect only upon the testator's death, and thus can be revoked or amended at any time during the testator's life.

questions.prompt: Deed restrictions are valid:
questions.explanation: Unless there's a written expiration date, deed restrictions don't expire automatically and continue in perpetuity.

questions.prompt: With reference to an escrow, recurring costs mean:
questions.explanation: Most mortgage lenders require an impound account to cover future payments of recurring costs, such as taxes, assessments, private mortgage insurance and home insurance to protect their security from defaults and tax liens.

questions.prompt: Probate proceedings are conducted by:
questions.explanation: Most real estate matters including probate are handled by the superior court.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can a property owner expect after sewer lines are installed in front of his/her property?
questions.explanation: A special assessment is a tax imposed against only those specific parcels of realty that will benefit from a proposed public improvement, as opposed to a general tax on the entire community.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a requirement of a valid will?
questions.explanation: The testator must be of sound mind and of adult age, and must declare the writing to be his/her last will and testament and sign it, usually in the presence of two or more credible witnesses.

questions.prompt: A homeowner took a $30,000 loss on his property. For federal income tax purposes, he can declare:
choices: the capital gain less the loss as deductible.
questions.explanation: Although capital gains on the sale of the owner's principal place of residence may be taxed if the gain exceeds the statutory amount, losses on the sale of a principal place of residence are not deductible.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would constitute boot in an exchange transaction?
questions.explanation: In an exchange, it is rare to find two properties of equal value and equity; therefore, to balance the equities, one party usually also pays some money or assumes a larger amount of underlying debt. This mortgage relief would be treated as boot and will be taxed to the extent of the boot received.

questions.prompt: How often should a trust fund account be reconciled?
questions.explanation: Similar to balancing your checkbook, reconciliation is the process of comparing two or more sets of records to determine whether their balances agree. This should reveal if the records are completed accurately. To assure the accuracy of the records, they must be reconciled at least once-a-month.

questions.prompt: All of the following will terminate an escrow EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Since a broker is not a party to the transaction, he/she cannot order an escrow terminated.

questions.prompt: Personal income taxes are structured using rates that are:
questions.explanation: Progressive means the more you make, the more you pay. It might also be termed "graduated."

questions.prompt: Without any agreement on a specific date, physical possession should be given:
choices: one week prior to close of escrow.
one week after close of escrow.
questions.explanation: In the absence of an agreement, possession would be given when all escrow instructions have been met (close of escrow).

questions.prompt: A deed is presumed to be delivered when:
choices: the seller handed the deed to the buyer, but the buyer did not record it.
the escrow officer mailed the deed which had been acknowledged by the seller, but delivery was made after the seller died.
the escrow company delivered the deed to the buyer prior to the buyer meeting all the terms of escrow.
the deed was delivered to the grantee after the death of the grantor in accordance with instructions the grantor left with his attorney.
questions.explanation: A deed need not be recorded to be considered delivered. As long as it is given to the grantee and accepted, it will be considered delivered.

questions.prompt: To be recorded, a deed must have:
choices: an address where tax bills should be mailed.
questions.explanation: To be recorded, a grant deed must have an address where tax bills should be mailed. A valid grant deed requires the signature of the grantor not the grantee.

questions.prompt: When a fire insurance claim is filed which of the following is true? The claimant would:
choices: Gain financially, but lose value on the property
Might lose financially, but not lose value on the property
Might lose financially and lose on the value of the property
questions.explanation: In theory, this is the correct answer.

questions.prompt: The term title plant refers to:
choices: records of a title insurance company.
questions.explanation: A title plant is the storage facility of a title insurance company in which it has accumulated complete title records of properties in its area. Many of the larger title insurance companies maintain their own title plants containing copies of all recorded instruments.

questions.prompt: The signed escrow instructions disagree with the purchase contract. As to the disagreement, which of the following is TRUE?
choices: The true intent of the parties must first be discovered.
The courts would have to decide the matter.
questions.explanation: Escrow instructions are a more current and more accurate reflection of the true intent of both parties.

questions.prompt: When a real estate broker speaks of "tax shelter," he/she is referring to:
questions.explanation: "Tax Shelter" refers to income tax shelter.

questions.prompt: When the first party agrees to pay for a financial loss arising from a specific event, and the second party agrees to make periodic payments to the first party, the agreement is known as:
questions.explanation: This is a good definition of an insurance policy.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes a "perfect escrow?"
choices: All documents submitted to escrow have been proofed for errors.
All documents, funds, and instructions needed to close the transaction are in the hands of the escrow agent.
The title search has taken place and the policy of title insurance has been issued.
All financial settlements have taken place and the documents are recorded.
questions.explanation: An escrow is said to be "perfect" (or perfected) when all documents, funds, and instructions needed to close the transaction are in the hands of the escrow agent.

questions.prompt: To adjust for any increase in tax liability due to a reassessment after the property was purchased, the tax authority would issue a:
questions.explanation: Since few people take possession of real estate on July 1st, the first day of the tax year, supplemental assessments are made to adjust for any increase in tax liability.

questions.prompt: Property taxes are assessed:
questions.explanation: Property taxes are "assessed" annually with a property tax bill mailed to the homeowner in early October of each year. The bill is payable in two installments.

questions.prompt: The Street Improvements Act of 1911 allows the issuance of bonds to raise funds for subdivision improvements on:
questions.explanation: The Street Improvements Act of 1911 is used for improvements such as streets and sewers.

questions.prompt: An owner-occupied residence qualifies for a homeowner's exemption of:
questions.explanation: An owner-occupied residence, including a condominium or duplex unit, qualifies for a homeowner's exemption of the first $7,000 of full cash value.

questions.prompt: All of the following must be recorded to have effect EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: A grant deed is valid without recording.

questions.prompt: Added improvements to an existing structure that increase the value of the property will be taxed:
choices: only when the property is sold.
questions.explanation: The assessor does not wait for a new tax year to reassess the improved property. As soon as the improvements are completed, the property is reassessed and the supplemental tax bill is issued that year.

questions.prompt: During a title search, the word "land patent" came up. This would be a(n):
choices: Escheat to the state of land left after the death of a person with no will and no known heirs
Transfer of title from the government to the first private individual
questions.explanation: A land patent is an exclusive land grant made by a sovereign entity (the government) with respect to a particular tract of land.

questions.prompt: Holographic wills cannot be:
choices: written in anything other than ink.
questions.explanation: Since a holographic will is handwritten, it is assumed that the person is capable of signing his/her full name.

questions.prompt: When the Federal Reserve Board wants to tighten the money supply, it would:
choices: raise the amount of reserves required for member banks.
raise the discount rate for member banks.
sell government bonds on the open market.
questions.explanation: The Federal Reserve Board ("Fed") would take all of the above actions to curb inflation.

questions.prompt: The beneficiary of a second trust deed sold his interest in the property for less than the unpaid balance of the note. This action is most commonly described as:
questions.explanation: To discount means to sell at a reduced value. When an investor sells a note at a discount, he/she is converting investment inflows to a present value. Since money has a time value, every dollar of that note to be received in the future is worth less than one dollar now, thus the discount.

questions.prompt: A broker negotiated a loan for a buyer. He will need to prepare a:
questions.explanation: A person who acts as a Mortgage Loan Broker and negotiates a loan for which a license is required and for compensation which is secured directly or collaterally by a lien on real property regardless of the size of the loan, must deliver a written disclosure statement to the borrower. The statement must be delivered within three business days of receipt of the borrower's written loan application or before the borrower becomes obligated to the loan, whichever is earlier. This is true whether the loan is being processed manually or electronically.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes "Cash-On-Cash" return?
questions.explanation: Cash-on-Cash Return is the ratio of income received by the investor based only on the cash invested. It is expressed as a percentage and does not include appreciation. Calculated as Annual Dollar Income ÷ Total Dollar Investment. For example when you purchase a rental property, you might put down only 10% for a cash down payment. Cash-on-cash return would measure the annual return you made on the property in relation to the down payment.

questions.prompt: Mutual Mortgage Insurance is paid for by:
choices: the buyer under an FHA loan.
the buyer under a VA loan.
the buyer under a Cal-Vet loan.
questions.explanation: MMI is paid for by the purchaser (buyer) under an FHA loan.

questions.prompt: The term "Secondary Market" as used in financing, refers to:
questions.explanation: Broadly speaking, mortgage markets are classified as "primary" and "secondary." A secondary market is one in which existing mortgages are bought, sold, or borrowed against. The mortgagee (lender) transfers the loan.

questions.prompt: The type of mortgage loan which permits borrowing additional funds at a later date is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An open-end provision in a mortgage allows the borrower to borrow additional amounts in the future without rewriting the loan documents.

questions.prompt: How long does a lender like to see a person in the same job or field to qualify for a loan?
questions.explanation: It is typical for lenders to consider your last two years of employment. But that doesn't mean you need to have been in the exact same job for the past two years. Generally, lenders will accept a 2-year history of consistent work in the same field.

questions.prompt: A homeowner would be least likely to obtain a $50,000 home improvement loan from a(n):
questions.explanation: In general, life insurance companies make conventional loans on most types of properties, but usually not on single-family homes.

questions.prompt: Why would the payor consider a straight note over an amortized note?
choices: To put working capital back into his/her business
questions.explanation: Since a straight note is an interest only note, the monthly payments would be smaller because there is no payment of principal. The drawback is a potential balloon payment at maturity.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE with regard to a "beneficiary statement?"
choices: The lender may charge up to $60 for preparing the statement.
Upon the request of the borrower, the beneficiary must furnish the statement within 21 days.
Failure to provide the statement in time can result in $300 damages.
questions.explanation: Upon the written request of an authorized person, the beneficiary must furnish a beneficiary statement within 21 days. There may be a $300 penalty for failing to comply. Although the beneficiary must provide an annual statement at no charge, additional statements may carry a maximum $60 charge.

questions.prompt: Who funds private mortgage companies?
choices: Private premiums of insurance and pools of insurance policies
questions.explanation: Private mortgage companies are really Mortgage Bankers. Most Mortgage Bankers fund loans themselves through a contract with an insurance company.

questions.prompt: The beneficiary of a trust deed is usually a:
questions.explanation: In a trust deed, the beneficiary is the lender (usually a bank).

questions.prompt: Broker Jones uses ABC Escrow for every transaction because of an arrangement with ABC Escrow that the company gives Broker Jones $100 for every transaction. This arrangement violates:
questions.explanation: Section 8 of RESPA prohibits any settlement service provider from giving or receiving any fee, kickback, or anything of value for the referral of business. By reimbursing the real estate agent for the referral of business, the title agency has given the broker a thing of value in consideration for the referral of business. Both the escrow company and the broker could be held responsible for the RESPA violation.

questions.prompt: For FHA purposes, acquisition costs include nonrecurring closing expenses. Which of the following would NOT be included:
questions.explanation: Nonrecurring costs are only paid one time in escrow. Impounds for property taxes are recurring. They may collect a couple months in advance during escrow, but impounds will continue for the life of the loan.

questions.prompt: Which of the following hold title under a Cal-Vet loan?
questions.explanation: Cal-Vet loans are administered by the California Department of Veterans Affairs (CDVA). CDVA buys the selected property from the seller and resells the property to the veteran on a land contract.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the most commonly used credit rating system?
questions.explanation: A FICO score is a credit score developed by Fair Isaac & Co. Credit scoring is a method of determining the likelihood that credit users will pay their bills. Fair, Isaac began its pioneering work with credit scoring in the late 1950's and, since then, scoring has become widely accepted by lenders as a reliable means of credit evaluation. A credit score attempts to condense a borrower's credit history into a single number.

questions.prompt: Under the "power of sale" clause in a trust deed, the authority to sell is placed with the:
choices: clerk of the County Court by court order.
questions.explanation: A power-of-sale clause is found in a trust deed where the trustor gives the trustee authority to sell the trust property under certain circumstances.

questions.prompt: Under which of the following types of financing is the borrower required to purchase term life insurance?
questions.explanation: A veteran is required to secure life insurance under the Cal-Vet Home Protection Plan.

questions.prompt: Why was HUD, Section 8, created?
choices: For Federal employees to obtain housing
To allow affordable housing for all United States citizens
questions.explanation: The HUD, Section 8 Program is a federal rent subsidy program for low-income and moderate-income tenants. Section 8 allows families to choose privately owned rental housing. The public housing authority generally pays the landlord the difference between the HUD-determined payment standard and the fair market rent, which must be reasonable.

questions.prompt: When a loan is fully amortized by equal monthly payments of principal and interest, the amount applied to principal:
choices: decreases while the interest payment increases.
increases while the interest payment decreases.
questions.explanation: With an amortized loan, the amount allocated to interest decreases while that applied to reduction of principal increases.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not require a down payment?
questions.explanation: VA loans can be made with no down payment required. The other financing programs generally require a down payment.

questions.prompt: A subdivider and developer purchased considerable acreage and now plan to construct a tract of 50 homes. In arranging the financing for the new construction, the lender has agreed to advance part of the funds immediately and will release a set of additional money as each home is completed. The funds that will be forthcoming as construction progresses are known as:
questions.explanation: Obligatory advances represent one form of construction loan distribution, often used in subdivision financing activities.

questions.prompt: All of the following are considered advantages of FHA financing EXCEPT:
choices: buyer is protected with FHA insurance.
questions.explanation: The FHA neither builds homes nor lends money directly, rather it insures loans on real property. Should the homeowner default on the mortgage, the lender is protected, not the buyer.

questions.prompt: A package mortgage is a loan in which:
choices: more than one parcel of land in a subdivision is covered.
the first and second trust deeds are included in one instrument.
personal property is included in the real estate loan.
additional financing is secured from a lender at a later date.
questions.explanation: A package mortgage is a method of financing in which the loan that finances the purchase of a home also finances the purchases of items of personal property.

questions.prompt: A veteran may purchase a home under Cal Vet by a:
questions.explanation: The property the veteran wishes to buy is purchased by the Department of Veteran's Affairs and in turn re-sold to the veteran on a Land Contract of Sale.

questions.prompt: During the one-year redemption period of a mortgagor in default:
choices: the mortgagee can sue for rent.
the mortgagee is not entitled to possession.
questions.explanation: The redemption period is a period of time established by state law during which a property owner has a right to redeem real estate after a judicial foreclosure by paying the sales price, interest and costs.

questions.prompt: An adjustable-rate loan stabilizes at an interest rate above the loan index. This increase above the index rate is known as the:
questions.explanation: Another variation to test your knowledge of the term margin.

questions.prompt: What is the definition of an Offset Statement?
choices: Notes the unpaid balance remaining on a mortgage loan as of a certain date.
Uncovers defects in the note that the property owner might assert against enforcement.
Indemnity insurance that protects lenders and homebuyers from financial loss sustained from defects in a title to a property.
An official document that proves your work is genuine and authentic.
questions.explanation: When a note and trust deed is offered for sale, a due diligence investigation is conducted that includes obtaining a trustor’s offset statement to uncover defects in the note that the property owner might assert against enforcement. The offset statement is prepared by the beneficiary selling the note (or the loan broker or escrow), then delivered to the property owner for review and confirmation of the information contained in the statement. Once reviewed and signed by the property owner, it is delivered to escrow for further approval by the trust deed investor prior to closing and acquiring the trust deed note.

questions.prompt: All of the following are characteristics of FHA loans EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The FHA does not guarantee loans, rather it insures loans on real property.

questions.prompt: To subordinate means to:
questions.explanation: Subordinate means to occupy a lower position in a regular descending series.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a down payment?
questions.explanation: Down payment (or downpayment, also called a deposit), is an initial up-front partial payment for the purchase of a house. It is usually paid in cash or equivalent at the time of finalizing the transaction. A loan of some sort is then required to finance the remainder of the payment.

questions.prompt: Who would sign an assignment of a land contract?
questions.explanation: If the seller (vendor) under a land Contract wishes to sell his/her interest to a third party through assignment, he/she must also convey title. The vendor's (seller's) signature would be required. The new contract holder must notify the buyer that title has been conveyed so they don't keep paying the original contract holder.

questions.prompt: Mortgages and trust deeds are both considered:
questions.explanation: Both a mortgage and trust deed are considered personal property.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be security for a note and deed of trust?
questions.explanation: The value of the property serves as security for a note and deed of trust.

questions.prompt: The seller (vendor) under a real property sales contract CANNOT:
choices: use something other than a legal description.
questions.explanation: A real property sales contract (formerly referred to as an "installment land sale contract") must contain the names of the buyer and seller, the sales price, the terms of payment, a full legal description and a lengthy statement of the rights and obligations of the parties.

questions.prompt: A loan to be completely repaid, principal and interest, by a series of regular equal installments is a:
questions.explanation: Amortization is the gradual repayment or retiring of a debt by means of systematic payments of principal and/or interest over a set period so that at the end there is a zero balance. The principal is thus directly reduced or amortized over the life of the loan.

questions.prompt: On a fully amortized loan, principal _________ as interest _________.
questions.explanation: With an amortized loan, interest is charged on the unpaid balance each month. The principal is being paid down each month. The payment remains constant over the entire life of the loan. The interest decreases each month and the amount applied to principal increases each month.

questions.prompt: A document used to transfer legal title from the trustee back to the borrower (trustor) after the debt has been repaid is called a:
questions.explanation: A deed of reconveyance is used to transfer legal title from the trustee back to the borrower (trustor) after a debt secured by a deed of trust has been paid to the lender (beneficiary).

questions.prompt: The nominal rate of interest is the:
choices: rate set forth in the note.
questions.explanation: The nominal rate of interest is the rate set forth in the promissory note.

questions.prompt: A buyer has monthly gross income of $5,000; total mortgage payments of $1,171; and total long-term debts of $325 per month. The back-end ratio is:
questions.explanation: Lenders also take into account the borrower's long-term debt for loan qualification purposes. This is the relationship between the borrower's long-term debt payments and the monthly income called the "back-end" ratio. The formula is: total monthly expense ÷ gross income = back-end ratio. In this question, long-term debts total $325 per month which added to the mortgage payment of $1,171, gives us the total monthly expense of $1,496. $1,496 ÷ 5,000 = 30%.

questions.prompt: Upon receiving notification of default on the first trust deed, the holder of a second trust deed would most likely:
choices: wait until the sale to buy the property at a bargain price.
redeem the first mortgage and foreclose under the second.
foreclose on the first to eliminate the second.
questions.explanation: In the event of default under the first trust deed, the holder of a second trust deed can elect to make the trustor's payments and thereby stop foreclosure. The junior liens holder may then foreclose on his or her own lien and take title subject to prior liens. If the junior lienholder does nothing, he/she will have to bid cash for the purchase price at the foreclosure sale or risk losing out completely, since foreclosure wipes out all junior lien. This is an inherent risk associated with junior loans.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes VA loans from FHA and other loans?
choices: down payment determined by Notice of Value (NOV)
questions.explanation: VA loans can be made with no down payment.

questions.prompt: A loan that requires a balloon payment at its maturity is called a(n):
questions.explanation: Under a partially amortized loan, the balance at maturity has only been partially reduced. The remaining balance due at maturity is referred to as a balloon payment .

questions.prompt: Who prepares the "beneficiary statement?"
questions.explanation: The beneficiary (lender) prepares the beneficiary statement upon written demand by an entitled person or his/her authorized agent. A beneficiary statement is usually requested in connection with the recording of a notice of default under a deed of trust or mortgage.

questions.prompt: In purchasing a home, the purchaser generally gives a note secured by a first deed of trust to a lending institution. In addition, he may give the seller cash and a note secured by a second deed of trust on the property. A "request for notice" would be filed for the benefit of the:
questions.explanation: A "request for notice of default" is filed with the county recorder when the second trust deed is recorded. If there is a default on the first trust deed, the recorder will send a copy of the "Notice of Default" to the holder of the second. This gives the holder of the second time to reinstate the first and begin foreclosure on the second.

questions.prompt: During periods of tight money:
questions.explanation: A tight money market is an economic situation in which the supply of money is limited and the demand for money is high. Due to the economic forces of supply and demand, interest rates typically go up during a period of tight money.

questions.prompt: What does it mean when a lender "calls" a loan?
choices: The interest rate and payment goes down early in the loan term.
The full payment of the remainder of a loan is due immediately.
The home is seized and put up for sale by the bank.
The loan resets to a new interest rate based on current market rates.
questions.explanation: The bank can “call” the loan and demand full payment of the remainder of the loan immediately. While this practice is legal if disclosed in the terms of the loan, a bank likely will never call the loan unless you fail to meet the loan’s terms.

questions.prompt: An insurance company is LEAST LIKELY to make a loan on a(n):
questions.explanation: Insurance companies typically deal with commercial properties and multi-family buildings. They favor loans for apartments, office, retail, and industrial properties, but may finance other property types (i.e. hotel or mixed used) on a case-by-case basis.

questions.prompt: Mr. Johnson agrees to assume a trust deed from Mr. Jones. Which of the following is correct?
choices: Mr. Johnson is primarily liable and Mr. Jones would remain secondary liable.
Mr. Jones would remain primarily liable.
Mr. Johnson and Mr. Jones would agree to liability.
questions.explanation: When the buyer agrees to assume the seller's liability on a trust deed, the seller (Mr. Jones) would remain secondary liable on the loan unless there is a substitution of liability which would relieve the seller of all liability.

questions.prompt: An adjustable-rate loan has an index that has risen from 5% to 10% with a margin of 2%, but the lender is still charging only 11% interest on the loan. This lower interest rate is most likey due to:
questions.explanation: The cap rate is a ceiling or limit on the adjustments made in the payments, interest rate or balance of an adjustable-rate loan.

questions.prompt: A legal act to bring about a trust deed sale can be:
questions.explanation: A mortgage without a power of sale can only be foreclosed judicially (i.e., by owner proceeding). A mortgage or deed of trust which expressly provides for power of sale may be foreclosed judicially or by trustee's sale.

questions.prompt: Why should a buyer seek legal counsel before assuming the seller's first mortgage?
choices: It is illegal to assume a loan in California.
The lender has to approve the assumption.
The buyer cannot qualify for a loan independently.
The seller will be able to foreclose.
questions.explanation: The most obvious pitfall to a buyer is thinking that the loan is fully assumable, but in fact it is not, and the lender can declare the entire loan due and payable. In order to assume an existing mortgage loan it is generally necessary to obtain consent from the lender prior to the assumption process. Transfer of property with an existing mortgage loan that is made without the lender's consent is sometimes referred to as a sale "subject to" the existing loan. In most cases, this type of transfer does not avoid the lender's right to call the loan due under the due-on-sale provision in the loan.

questions.prompt: The instrument used to secure a loan on personal property is called a:
questions.explanation: A security agreement is a document that creates a lien on personal property. To perfect a security interest, a form called a financing statement should be recorded.

questions.prompt: Proceeds from a trustee's sale go to the:
choices: costs of sale first, then first lien holder, then junior lien holders with the balance to the trustor.
first lien holder with the balance to junior lien holders.
costs of sale first with the balance to the beneficiary.
questions.explanation: Costs and expenses of the action are paid first, then the parties to the transaction are paid in order of their priority.

questions.prompt: A low loan-to-value ratio indicates:
questions.explanation: A large down payment by the borrower would lower the loan-to-value ratio.

questions.prompt: A release clause associated with a blanket mortgage is a provision which:
choices: causes the first loan to become subordinate to junior loans.
releases a portion of property covered by the blanket encumbrance when certain conditions are met.
questions.explanation: This is referring to a partial release clause which enables the mortgagor to obtain partial releases of specific parcels from the mortgage upon a payment larger than the pro rata portion of the loan.

questions.prompt: The FHA was created primarily to provide:
choices: a primary market for home mortgages.
insurance for home loans from qualified lenders.
a flow of money and credit.
questions.explanation: The Federal Housing Administration (FHA) was established to encourage improvement in housing standards and conditions and to provide an adequate home-financing system through the insurance of housing mortgages and credit. FHA does not make loans, but it insures loans made by lending institutions such as banks, life insurance companies, and mortgage companies.

questions.prompt: What is the form a lender must give the buyer-borrower when the loan terms have changed prior to the close of escrow?
questions.explanation: According to the new TILA–RESPA Integrated Disclosure (TRID) law (TILA and RESPA Integrated Disclosures), if there are changes in the loan terms prior to consummation, but after issuance of the Closing Disclosure, the lender must provide the buyer-borrower with updated information in a revised Closing Disclosure no later than consummation. "Consummation" occurs when the buyer-borrower becomes contractually obligated to the creditor (lender) on the loan. In California, the buyer-borrower becomes contractually obligated to the lender upon recordation of the loan documents. The TILA–RESPA Integrated Disclosure (TRID) rule went into effect on October 3, 2015.

questions.prompt: At the close of a Land Contract, the vendee is entitled to:
questions.explanation: During the term of a Land Contract, title remains in the name of the seller (vendor) until the provisions of the contract have been met. Upon satisfactory performance, the vendor conveys legal title to the buyer (vendee). During the term of the contract, the vendee holds the equitable title or equitable ownership.

questions.prompt: A contractor obtained a construction loan and the loan funds are to be released in a series of progressive payments. Most lenders disburse the last payment when the:
choices: period to file a lien has expired.
questions.explanation: The usual waiting period for the final disbursement is 35 days after the recording of the Notice of Completion. It would be hazardous to advance the final disbursement before that time for fear that there might be subcontractors who have not been paid and will file mechanic's liens. The subcontractors are wiped out 31 days after recording the Notice of Completion.

questions.prompt: Equity financing refers to:
choices: borrowing on the difference between property value and liens.
questions.explanation: Equity is the difference between the property value and the amount of remaining debt. A property owner's equity will build up gradually through periodic amortized payments. Equity financing refers to borrowing against this value.

questions.prompt: A first trust deed can be distinguished from a second trust deed by:
choices: the time and date of recording.
questions.explanation: The time and date of recording establishes the priority of the lien. The first trust deed would have an earlier time and date of recording.

questions.prompt: The buyer under the terms of a land contract is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Under the terms of a Land Contract, the seller (vendor) passes possession and equitable title of the property to the buyer (vendee) but retains title until the total or a substantial portion of the purchase price is paid.

questions.prompt: The ratio of a loan's principal to the property's appraised value is called the:
questions.explanation: The loan-to-value ratio is the percentage of a property's value that a lender can or may loan to a borrower. For example if the ratio is 87%, this means that a lender may loan 87% of the property's appraised value to the borrower. For instance, if someone borrows $130,000 to purchase a house worth $150,000, the LTV ratio is $130,000 to $150,000 or $130,000 Ã· $150,000, or 87%. The remaining 13% represents the borrower's equity. The higher the LTV ratio, the riskier the loan is for a lender.

questions.prompt: After a trustee's sale, there is money left over after paying the beneficiary of the first trust deed. This money would go first to the:
questions.explanation: A deficiency occurs when the foreclosure sale of a property produces less than the amount needed to pay the costs and expenses of the action and to pay off the balance of the loan. The parties to the transaction are paid in order of their priority.

questions.prompt: Who would be responsible for paying the 1% origination fee on an FHA loan?
questions.explanation: The 1% loan origination fee is required by FHA and is paid by the borrower.

questions.prompt: A home loan in which the lender offers a below-market interest rate in exchange for a share of the profit when the house is sold describes a:
questions.explanation: A shared appreciation mortgage, or SAM, is a home loan in which the lender offers a below-market interest rate in exchange for a share of the profit when the house is sold. A SAM usually has a deadline for paying off the principal, for example, 10 years.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a general difference between individual and institutional lenders?
choices: Individual lenders make larger loans than institutional lenders.
Individudal lenders charge lower interest rates.
Individual lenders give loans for shorter terms.
Individual lenders do not undertake foreclosure proceedings.
questions.explanation: Loans made by individual lenders are usually for a shorter loan term. Private individuals are the primary source of secondary financing.

questions.prompt: When comparing mortgage bankers and mortgage brokers, which of the following is true?
choices: Both deal exclusively in the primary mortgage market
Mortgage bankers usually lend their own funds while mortgage brokers arrange loans
questions.explanation: A mortgage banker is a person, corporation or firm that normally provides its own funds for mortgage financing. A mortgage broker is a person or firm that acts as an intermediary between borrower and lender who negotiates, sells or arranges loans and sometimes continues to service the loans (also called a loan broker).

questions.prompt: A promissory note that provides for payment of interest only during the term of the note is a(n):
questions.explanation: A straight note is defined as one in which payments of interest only are made periodically during the term of the note with the principal payment due in one lump sum upon maturity.

questions.prompt: Foreclosure by sale would NOT involve a:
questions.explanation: When the trustee sells property under the power-of-sale provision in a deed of trust, the recording of the Notice of Default by the trustee commences the three month reinstatement period. When the trustor's right of reinstatement has run out, advertising of the sale begins by publishing the Notice of Sale. A Notice of Default is sent to junior lien holders advising them of a pending foreclosure on the first.

questions.prompt: Total foreclosure time under a trust deed most nearly approaches:
questions.explanation: A three month reinstatement period plus 20 days advertising of the sale by publishing the Notice of Sale.

questions.prompt: Which of the following gives the most protection to a property owner in default?
questions.explanation: The one-year redemption period under a mortgage gives the greatest protection to the owner.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would have the least impact on evaluating a prospective borrower's income for a loan?
questions.explanation: Since overtime is typically sporadic, it is of least concern to the lender.

questions.prompt: The Irwin's made an offer to purchase the Grey's property. As part of the offer, the Irwin's agreed to take title "subject to" an existing VA loan which the Greys obtained when they purchased the property in the approximate amount of $39,000. If the Greys sell to the Irwins under these conditions, which of the following is true concerning liability for a loss suffered by the government after a foreclosure on the VA loan:
choices: The Irwins will be primarily liable.
The Greys and Irwins will be equally liable.
The Greys will be primarily liable.
Neither couple is liable because the Irwins took title "subject to" the existing loan.
questions.explanation: The Grey's will be primarily liable since VA did not approve an "assumption" of the loan. If there is a deficiency in a foreclosure, VA may get a deficiency judgment against the Greys.

questions.prompt: A disadvantage for the buyer under a Land Contract is:
choices: If the seller dies during the contract term, litigation may be necessary to obtain clear title.
Financial institutions consider land contracts unsatisfactory collateral.
Transfer of vendee's interest may be restricted by covenants.
questions.explanation:
The disadvantages of a Land Contract to the buyer are several, chiefly:

Covenants or restrictions of assignment or transfer of the land contract may hamper or prevent the transfer of buyer's interest therein. The buyer may not be aware of these problems until the time to transfer title.

A prevailing opinion among financial institutions that a Land Contract is poor collateral because it is subject to a more rapid termination in the event of default.

After full performance, the buyer may receive defective title or no title at all, although normally the contract will require delivery of a policy of title insurance. The buyer may have to pay the premium for this.

Lack of assurance that the seller has good title at the time the contract is made, coupled with the fact that prior to full performance by the buyer, the buyer may not rescind the contract on these grounds.

If during the contract term the seller should go bankrupt or die and title passes to heirs or be declared incompetent or have a conservator appointed, the buyer can at the very least anticipate time consuming, frustrating, and expensive litigation before obtaining a deed and policy of title insurance.

questions.prompt: All of the following fees are allowed under RESPA except:
choices: Cooperative agreements between listing and selling real estate brokers.
Payments to an attorney for services actually rendered.
Payment for the referral of business, rather than for services actually performed.
Payments for services actually rendered or goods actually provided.
questions.explanation: Section 8 of RESPA prohibits a person from giving or accepting any “thing” of value for referrals of settlement service business related to a federally related mortgage loan. It also prohibits a person from giving or accepting any part of a charge for services that are not performed.

questions.prompt: Most real estate loans charge the following kind of interest rate:
questions.explanation: Interest is termed "simple" or "compound". Simple interest is interest paid only on the principal owed. Compound interest is interest paid on accrued interest as well as on the principal owed. Most real estate loans charge simple interest rates.

questions.prompt: The trustor under a trust deed is the party who:
choices: holds the title to the property in trust.
questions.explanation: The trustor is the borrower under a deed of trust and is the one who signs the note and deed of trust.

questions.prompt: Who would most likley pay a premium for mutual mortgage insurance?
choices: The homeowner who assures an FHA loan.
A buyer with a Cal-Vet loan.
A home buyer with a conventional loan from a life insurance company.
A home buyer who wants to insure real and personal property.
questions.explanation: Mutual Mortgage Insurance (MMI) is mandatory on all FHA loans.
