questions.prompt: If a real estate licensee sells a real property sales contract for a seller (vendor), the licensee is responsible for making sure the contract is recorded:
questions.explanation: If a real estate broker negotiates the sale of a real property sales contract (formerly referred to as an "installment land sale contract"), he/she is responsible for making sure it gets recorded within 10 working days.

questions.prompt: A mortgage is a:
choices: loan secured by collateral of real property.
loan secured by the credit rating of the borrower only.
loan without collateral to secure the loan.
three party instrument with power of sale.
questions.explanation: A mortgage is an instrument recognized by law by which property is pledged as security for the loan without the necessity of giving up possession of it.

questions.prompt: Upon full repayment of a Cal-Vet loan, the borrower receives a:
questions.explanation: The CDVA holds title until the veteran has repaid the amount owed. Upon repayment, title is conveyed to the veteran in the form of a grant deed.

questions.prompt: With a mortgage, who signs the note?
questions.explanation: The mortgagor (borrower) signs the note.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lenders invest more heavily in single-family home loans?
questions.explanation: Savings and loan associations, also known as "thrifts," fomerly accounted for more home loans than any other source. The distinction between banks and S&L's has almost disappeared since deregulation, and a great many S&L's have become banks.

questions.prompt: Deregulation of financial institutions most nearly means:
choices: government controls no longer apply to financial institutions.
the amount of interest paid on savings accounts is no longer regulated.
financial institutions can no longer respond to market conditions.
examining the enforcement responsibilities of regulators have been relaxed.
questions.explanation: Under deregulation, financial institutions may now pay any amount of interest on deposits.

questions.prompt: The government actually lends the money for a(n):
questions.explanation: The Department of Veteran's Affairs buys the property and then sells it to the veteran on a Land Contract of Sale.

questions.prompt: The owner of a property encumbered with a first and second trust deed wants to refinance the first trust deed. What should the second trust deed contain?
questions.explanation: A subordination clause is a clause in which the holder of a mortgage or trust deed holder permits a subsequent lien to take priority. Subordination is the act of yielding priority. This clause provides that if a prior mortgage is paid off or renewed, the junior mortgage will continue in its subordinate position and will not automatically become a higher or first mortgage.

questions.prompt: The Gonzales family wanted to purchase a property and assume the seller's VA loan, "subject to". Which of the following is correct?
choices: The seller will be relieved of all liability for the loan.
Both the buyer and seller will be liable for the loan.
The seller will remain liable for the loan.
questions.explanation: If the VA does not approve the assumption, the loan is taken "subject to" the existing loan. This means the original borrower will remain liable for the loan. If there is a foreclosure, it will be against the original borrower (the seller).

questions.prompt: Which of the following fees are allowed under RESPA?
choices: One person marks up the cost of a third party service and keeps the difference without providing any goods or services to justify the additional charge.
Two or more persons split a fee and one person did not perform any services to receive a share of the fee.
A payment for the referral of business, rather than for services actually performed.
Payments to an attorney for services actually rendered.
questions.explanation: Section 8 of RESPA prohibits a person from giving or accepting any “thing” of value for referrals of settlement service business related to a federally related mortgage loan. It also prohibits a person from giving or accepting any part of a charge for services that are not performed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following acts by the trustor requires the beneficiary's consent?
choices: creating an easement on the property
questions.explanation: The trustor cannot perform acts pertaining to the securing property without the consent of the beneficiary.

questions.prompt: A veteran is eligible to use either the VA program or the DVA program in purchasing his owner occupied house. In which of these programs would the governmental body retain legal title to the house?
choices: The buyer would have title regardless of which program he used
The VA and DVA both retain legal title
questions.explanation: This is a Cal-Vet loan. Buyer is buying the property by using a land contract. DVA retains title until the veteran pays off the loan.

questions.prompt: The relationship of the trustor to the beneficiary in a deed of trust is comparable to:
questions.explanation: The relationship of the trustor to the beneficiary is similar to the borrower/lender relationship in that the mortgagee (lender) extends credit to the mortgagor (borrower). Memory AID: The "OR" gives something of value to the "EE" in exchange for money.

questions.prompt: Mortgages and deeds of trust differ in every respect EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The property is security for a loan under both a mortgage and deed of trust. A mortgage has two parties while a trust deed has three. A mortgage promises the title - a trust deed conveys legal title from the trustor to trustee.

questions.prompt: The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act provides for violation penalties of:
choices: up to one year in jail.
questions.explanation: Violation of RESPA may result in a monetary fine and/or jail time.

questions.prompt: If there has not been an agreement to the contrary, all of the following would qualify as a negotiable instrument EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Mortgages and trust deeds are NOT negotiable instruments. The promissory note that goes with it is a negotiable instrument.

questions.prompt: The primary activities of FNMA in the secondary market involves:
choices: all types of real estate loans.
second mortgages and trust deeds up to $20,000.
questions.explanation: The Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) was originally organized to create a secondary market in mortgage loans. The primary activities of the agency involve FHA Title II loans (insured) and VA loans (guaranteed).

questions.prompt: The purchasing power of a dollar is measured:
choices: by the interest paid on savings.
by reference to the local real estate market.
questions.explanation: The purchasing power of a dollar is measured by the Consumer Price Index.

questions.prompt: The right of rescission under truth-in-lending would apply to a(n):
questions.explanation: The borrower's rescission rights apply to non-business loans only.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the purpose of the Federal Truth-In-Lending Act?
choices: To regulate fees charged by lenders
To assure a meaningful disclosure of credit terms
questions.explanation: The purpose of the Federal Truth-in-Lending Act is to assure consumers that they are provided information on the costs of credit by disclosing credit terms.

questions.prompt: An agent places an ad in the newspaper saying that he will give $500 to anyone who sells or buys a property through him. Which of the following is TRUE?
choices: The broker cannot give $500 to the buyer or seller.
The broker cannot give $500 to the buyer only.
This would violate the real estate law concerning compensation of unlicensed persons performing real estate acts.
The agent can give $500 to the buyer or seller.
questions.explanation: The agent can give a monetary incentive to prospective clients as long as a full disclosure is made to all parties to the transaction.

questions.prompt: Why would a lender be interested in making a government-insured or government-guaranteed loan over a traditional conventional loan?
questions.explanation: A government guarantee or government insurance lowers the risk for the lender.

questions.prompt: To pledge a thing as security for an obligation without surrendering possession of it refers to:
questions.explanation: Hypothecate means to pledge specific real or personal property as security for an obligation without surrendering possession of it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following pairs of words are synonymous (the same)?
questions.explanation: The construction loan is often a short-term or interim loan. When the construction is completed, the take-out loan is used to pay off the construction loan.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would contribute the most in creating a period of inflation?
questions.explanation: Appreciation is really a result of inflation as well as a contributor to inflation. Rising rent costs are a result of inflation. Declining dollar value abroad is also a contributor to inflation.

questions.prompt: A request for notice of default would be of most help to the:
choices: beneficiary of a second trust deed.
beneficiary of a first trust deed.
questions.explanation: Since foreclosure wipes out all junior liens, the holder of a junior lien should request the recording of a request for notice of default announcing that a default has occurred.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes the term "beneficiary statement?"
choices: A statement of the unpaid balance of a loan.
A statement designating the one who will receive the property if the borrower dies.
An itemization of the amount paid to the policy holder for insurance purposes.
A description of the beneficial features of an assumable loan.
questions.explanation: A beneficiary statement is a statement of the unpaid balance of a loan and the condition of the indebtedness, as it relates to a deed of trust transaction.

questions.prompt: A GPAM is what kind of loan:
questions.explanation: This is a Graduated Payment Adjustable Mortgage. This plan combines elements of a Graduated Payment Mortgage and an Adjustable Rate Mortgage. It starts like a GPM with lower payments that increase in fixed steps until they level off, after which the interest rate may vary. This loan may produce negative amortization.

questions.prompt: Commercial banks are interested in liquidity and marketability of their loans. Which of the following loans would they prefer?
questions.explanation: Liquidity means assets that can be turned into cash quickly. Since short-term loans pay off quickly, the lender has access to a ready cash reserve.

questions.prompt: How much is the borrower paying if a lender charges 1 points on a $250,000 loan with a purchase price is $300,000?
questions.explanation: The lender sometimes charges points as a form of pre-paid interest. One point equals one percent of the loan amount. By charging a borrower points, a lender effectively increases the yield on the loan above the amount of the stated interest rate. Borrowers can offer to pay a lender "discount points" as a method to reduce the interest rate on the loan, thus obtaining a lower monthly payment in exchange for this up-front payment.

questions.prompt: Under the Truth-in-Lending Act (Regulation Z), which of the following need NOT be included in the total "finance charge" required as part of the disclosure statement?
choices: commissions or finder's fees to lenders
cost of a credit report and appraisal fee
questions.explanation: Fees for a credit report or appraisal are excluded from the costs which must be included in the finance charge.

questions.prompt: Title I FHA loans are for:
questions.explanation: Title I FHA guidelines authorize insurance of repair and improvement loans.

questions.prompt: Once the debt secured by a deed of trust has been paid in full to the lender, the trustee must give a deed of reconveyance to the trustor:
choices: within 60 days of the trustor's demand.
within 30 days of the trustor's demand.
within 21 days of the trustor's demand.
questions.explanation: The trustee must deliver a deed of reconveyance within 21 days of the trustor's demand.

questions.prompt: When lenders use the term "mortgage yield," they are describing:
choices: an increase in the value of a property which has a mortgage.
the effective interest return obtained from a first trust deed by an investor.
all of the money received by a lender after deducting closing costs and loan fees.
what the lender receives when a mortgage is paid off.
questions.explanation: The mortgage yield is the return on an investment or the amount of profit stated as a percentage of the amount invested-the rate of return. In real estate, yield refers to the effective annual amount of income that is being accrued on an investment. The yield or profit to a lender is the spread of differential between the cost of acquiring the funds lent and the interest rate charged.

questions.prompt: A deficiency judgment is possible:
choices: where foreclosure is by court action.
questions.explanation: A deficiency judgment is a judgment against a borrower for the balance of a debt owed when the security for a loan is insufficient to satisfy the debt. A deficiency occurs when the foreclosure sale of a property produces less than the amount due on the loan. In California, a mortgagee cannot recover a deficiency judgment on a purchase-money loan. In those states where mortgages generally carry a "power of sale," creditors must bring a separate action to obtain a deficiency judgment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would NOT be illustrative of an institutional lender?
questions.explanation: Institutional lenders are those lenders who lend their own money. A mortgage company usually does not lend its own money, but rather acts in most cases as the representative of an institutional lender. They are sometimes referred to as "loan correspondents" or "loan brokerage firms."

questions.prompt: Prepayments is permissible on a Land Contract, however, the seller may prohibit prepayment for up to:
questions.explanation: Prepayment by the buyer on a land contract is allowed, but the seller may prohibit prepayment for up to 12 months following the sale. This means that the seller does not have to give title for one year. The buyer cannot waive his/her right to prepay.

questions.prompt: The term mortgage warehousing refers to:
questions.explanation: Mortgage warehousing is the process by which a mortgage banker or mortgage broker assembles mortgages that he/she has made and prepares the mortgages to be sold in the secondary market.

questions.prompt: Mortgage loan brokers are regulated primarily by:
questions.explanation: Loan brokers are regulated by the California Loan Brokerage Law.

questions.prompt: From which of the following could you most likely secure the greatest amount of money for the longest period of time?
questions.explanation: Insurance companies lend the largest amounts for the longest time.

questions.prompt: Which of the following laws applies to federally related transactions?
questions.explanation: RESPA applies when the purchase of a one-to-four family residential dwelling is financed by a federally related mortgage loan.

questions.prompt: A buyer has a monthly gross income of $5,000; total mortgage payments of $1,171; and total long-term debts of $325 per month. The front-end ratio is:
questions.explanation: Lenders use the monthly payment on a property in determining a borrower's qualifications. This is the relationship between the total mortgage payment and the monthly gross income called the "front-end" ratio. The payment includes principal and interest, property taxes, and insurance (commonly referred to as PITI). The formula is: mortgage payment ÷ gross income = front-end ratio. $1,171 ÷ $5,000 = 23%.

questions.prompt: The functions of Ginnie Mae include all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: special programs for low-interest home loans.
questions.explanation: The Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) is an agency under HUD that guarantees securities sold and issued by Fannie Mae. Ginnie Mae does not insure loans.

questions.prompt: A trust deed foreclosed as a mortgage would be foreclosed by:
questions.explanation: A deed of trust may be foreclosed by judicial proceedings in superior court.

questions.prompt: The first step a mortgagee would take to foreclose on a mortgage would be to:
questions.explanation: In the event of the mortgagor's default before final payment, the mortgagee's remedy is judicial (court-ordered) foreclosure. The mortgagee's first step would be to initiate the court action.

questions.prompt: What can the lender advertise in the newspaper for a loan offering that includes negative amortization?
choices: "We can help you finance the purchase of your home"
"We can approve you over the phone"
questions.explanation: Negative amortization occurs when a monthly loan payment is too small to cover even the interest, which gets added to the unpaid balance. It can result in a borrower owing substantially more than the original amount borrowed. Certain "buzz words" in an ad trigger additional mandatory disclosures. For example, an ad that says, "Low Fixed Rate," or "No Cost Loan," must also prominently mention all associated fees. It is illegal to make loan approvals over the phone.

questions.prompt: All of the following are characteristics of VA loans EXCEPT:
choices: used for housing or farm property
lower interest rates than conventional loans
okay to use for the purchase of rental units
questions.explanation: VA loans can be made for a home, farm, or business. If the loan is for a home it must be for personal use, not rental purposes.

questions.prompt: Default in a mortgage may be caused by:
questions.explanation: A default is generally defined as nonperformance of a duty or obligation that is part of a contract.

questions.prompt: A construction loan would most likely be made by a(n):
questions.explanation: Commercial banks typically prefer short-term, high interest rate construction loans.

questions.prompt: If the payments of the buyer under a Land Contract include taxes and insurance, the seller must:
choices: pay the insurance company and the IRS on behalf of the buyer.
hold this money in a trust account for this purpose.
hold this money in his or her personal checking account.
cash the buyer's check within three working days of receipt.
questions.explanation: If the seller receives money from the buyer under a land contract for taxes and insurance, either as part of the payment or separately, he/she must hold this money in trust for this purpose.

questions.prompt: Private Mortgage Insurance (PMI) can be canceled when you've paid down your mortgage to:
questions.explanation: The federal Homeowners' Protection Act, which applies to people who bought their homes after July 29, 1999, says that you can ask that your PMI be canceled when you've paid down your mortgage to 80% of the original loan, if you have a good record of payment and compliance with the terms of your mortgage.

questions.prompt: An assignment of a rent's clause in a trust deed benefits the:
questions.explanation: An assigment of rents clause in a trust deed is an agreement between the trustor (property owner) and the beneficiary by which the beneficiary receives as security the right to collect rents from the trustor's tenants.

questions.prompt: Naked legal title is held by the:
questions.explanation: A trustee in a deed of trust holds naked legal title to a secured property. Naked legal title is only such title as is needed to carry out the terms of the lien document, and is lacking the usual rights and privileges of ownership.

questions.prompt: The Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA) was primarily created to:
choices: increase the availability of secondary financing.
serve as a secondary mortgage market.
questions.explanation: The Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) was originally organized to create a secondary market in mortgage loans.

questions.prompt: Funds for Cal-Vet loans come from:
questions.explanation: Funds for Cal-Vet loans come from voter-approved State General Obligation Bonds and Revenue Bonds issued by the legislature.

questions.prompt: Who enforces the Truth-in-Lending Act?
questions.explanation: The Federal Trade Commission is in charge of enforcing the Truth-in-Lending Act (Regulation Z).

questions.prompt: Which of the following would most likely charge the highest interest rate?
questions.explanation: This type of loan is referred to as a "hard money loan." It is a mortgage loan given to a borrower in exchange for cash, as opposed to a mortgage given to finance a specific real estate purchase. Hard money loans often involve more risk for the lender and thus carry a higher interest rate.

questions.prompt: When the FED takes measures to implement a "tight money" market, the net effect usually results in an increase in the:
choices: loan funds for new home construction.
use of second trust deeds in real estate financing.
sales volume of single family residence.
use of new first trust deed financing in real estate transactions.
questions.explanation: The use of second trust deeds is most prevalent when there is a tight money market. This means that interest rates are high and money is more difficult to get.

questions.prompt: In an adjustable-rate loan, the amount added to the index rate that represents the lender's cost of doing business is called the:
questions.explanation: The margin is the amount added to the interest rate of an adjustable-rate loan that represents the lender's cost of doing business (includes costs, profits and risk of loss of the loan). Generally, the margin stays constant during the life of the loan.

questions.prompt: A prepayment penalty clause found in a contract is often:
choices: written into the contract for the trustee's protection.
a charge to the buyer if he/she is late in making a monthly payment.
for the benefit of the trustor.
a penalty the buyer is charged for paying the contract off early.
questions.explanation: A prepayment penalty clause is charged against the borrower for early retirement of the loan. The main reason for the charge is that money paid early to the lender often sits dormant and does not earn interest. To avoid this, the lender charges the borrower a penalty.

questions.prompt: A seasoned loan is a:
questions.explanation: A seasoned loan is one with a payment history. If a note shows a good payment record by the payor, it is considered more desirable and usually sells for more in the secondary market.

questions.prompt: Buyer B has purchased under a contract of sale from Seller A. "A" is one month behind in his mortgage payments on the property which is the same amount that "B" pays each month to "A". With regard to the current payment "B" makes to "A":
choices: it must be immediately applied to A's mortgage.
it need not be applied unless A is three months delinquent.
"A" should not have sold his property with an outstanding loan balance.
a buyer on a land contract should check on encumbrances before entering into a contract of sale.
questions.explanation: The seller is required by law to apply the payment received from the buyer to the amount due on the existing trust deed.

questions.prompt: The practice of charging discount points on FHA insured loans is because the lender desires to:
choices: equalize the yield on FHA loans to the yield on conventional loans.
create a competitive environment between FHA loans and conventional loans.
close the gap between FHA loans and conventional loans on the secondary market.
questions.explanation: Lenders would not be willing to make FHA loans if they could not receive the same yield on FHA loans as they do on conventional loans. The secondary market would not be willing to purchase FHA loans if the yield was lower than on conventional loans. In order to solve this problem and to make these loans available to buyers, discount points are charged. They may be paid by either buyer or seller.

questions.prompt: The conscious charging by a private lender of more than the maximum amount of interest allowed by law is known as:
questions.explanation: Usury is defined as a conscious taking by a lender of more than the maximum amount of interest as allowed by law.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is most nearly true concerning the activities of mortgage companies?
choices: They are organized under federal laws and thus are not subject to state regulations.
They never service the loans they create.
They prefer negotiating loans which are saleable in the secondary market.
They are not active in the field of government insured loans.
questions.explanation: Mortgage companies (loan brokers) often do service the loans they originate, are active in FHA and VA loans and are usually organized under state laws. They prefer to negotiate loans which are sold on the secondary market.

questions.prompt: By law, a monthly payment on a mortgage loan is considered late when it is received by the lender:
choices: more than 10 days after the due date.
questions.explanation: Although most California mortage lenders allow the borrower a 15-day grace period in getting the payment to the lender, federal guidelines would allow the lender to declare the payment late if it is received more than 10 days after the due date.

questions.prompt: From the lender's perspective, a large down payment:
choices: makes it more likely that the property will be properly maintained.
questions.explanation: Most lenders realize that the greater the equity a borrower has in a property, the less inclined he/she will be to default and lose the property through foreclosure. This should also encourage the borrower to keep the property in good shape. A large down payment usually streamlines the loan qualification process.

questions.prompt: The Truth-in-Lending Act is part of the:
questions.explanation: The Federal Truth-in-Lending Act is part of the Federal Consumer Protection Act.

questions.prompt: From a financing standpoint, the relationship of the parties to a Land Contract would be closest to:
questions.explanation: The Real Property Sales Contract also known as the Land Contract, is an agreement between two parties in which the seller (vendor) passes possession and equitable title of the property to the buyer (vendee) but retains title until the total or a substantial portion of the purchase price is paid. This type of contract usually does not require conveyance of title within one year. It is similar to the beneficiary/trustor relationship in that the buyer only has a possessory interest with equitable title and is making monthly installment payments over a period of time.

questions.prompt: Which of these pairs of terms have the closest relationship to each other:
questions.explanation: Interim loan is another name for a construction loan.

questions.prompt: A commercial bank agreed to loan George $180,000 for a one year term, but required George to maintain a savings account of $180,000 at all times during the term of the loan. This provision is known as:
questions.explanation: A compensation balance is used when the borrower has less than perfect credit. The lender will require a savings account. If the borrower defaults, the lender will use the funds in the savings account to offset any losses during foreclosure.

questions.prompt: An adjustable-rate mortgage loan is tied to an interest rate called the:
questions.explanation: The index rate is the rate to which the interest rate on an adjustable-rate mortgage is tied. At set adjustment periods, the borrower's interest rate will move up or down as the index rate changes.

questions.prompt: A subordination clause would be found in a:
questions.explanation: A subordination clause is a clause most likely found in a trust deed. A subordination clause is usually standard in a junior trust deed because the junior trust deed gets a higher interest rate and is often not concerned about the inferior lien position.

questions.prompt: A purchaser of a home five years ago is now interested in securing an FHA loan. A salesperson would most likely introduce the homeowner to:
choices: a conventional bank or savings & loan.
questions.explanation: The FHA insures the loan but does not actually lend the money. This would most likely occur through a conventional lender.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct regarding current rules and requirements of reverse mortgage loans?
choices: The borrower must complete credit counseling before a reverse mortgage.
The borrower must meet with at least three reverse mortgage providers.
The borrower is required to take out an equity line of credit as a condition of the reverse mortgage loan.
The borrower has three months after loan closing to change their mind and cancel the reverse mortgage loan.
questions.explanation: The FHA has set some additional safeguards to protect borrowers and encourage responsible reverse mortgage loan use. Before loan approval, part of the process is to complete a counseling session with an FHA-approved counselor. This counselor will make sure the borrower knows all of his/her options and has all the reverse mortgage information they need to be able to decide if this loan is best for their situation. (See Reverse Mortgage Rules & Requirements: https://www.americanadvisorsgroup.com/news/reverse-mortgage-rules). Note: Reverse Mortgage may also be referred to as a Reverse Equity Mortgage (RAM) loan on the state exam.

questions.prompt: Mr. and Mrs. Lee sell their house and agree to carry back a second trust deed from the buyer to help complete the financing for the sale. This is most likely due to:
choices: The first trust deed is a VA loan.
The seller doesn't need the immediate cash.
questions.explanation: When the Fed takes steps to implement a "tight money" market, it usually means an increase in interest rates and a decrease in available loan funds. The sales volume of existing home sales decreases and borrowers have more difficulty in obtaining loans. The net effect is that sellers are forced to take back seconds to sell their property.

questions.prompt: What loan has negative amortization for the first few years?
questions.explanation: A graduated payment mortgage loan, often referred to as GPM, is a mortgage with low initial monthly payments which gradually increase over a specified time frame. In finance, negative amortization (also known as NegAm, deferred interest or graduated payment mortgage) occurs whenever the loan payment for any period is less than the interest charged over that period so that the outstanding balance of the loan increases.

questions.prompt: A man bought a small apartment building. He put a down payment on the property and financed the rest with a loan. One year later the property was appraised. His equity had increased 300%. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Leverage is broadly defined as the impact of borrowed funds on investment return. It is more specifically the use of borrowed funds to purchase property with the anticipation that the acquired property will also increase so that the investor will realize a profit on his/her investment.

questions.prompt: The clause in a mortgage note which permits the lender to declare the unpaid balance due and payable upon default by the borrower is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An acceleration clause is a provision in a mortgage, trust deed, promissory note or land contract that upon the occurrence of a specified event, gives the lender the right to call all sums due and payable in advance of the fixed payment term.

questions.prompt: Buyer Frank sued broker Sam for a misrepresentation in the sale of a single family residence. He was awarded a judgment but Broker Sam was bankrupt and unable to pay the judgment. Buyer Frank appealed to the Real Estate Recovery Account. Assuming the Recovery account agrees to pay Frank, he will receive a maximum of ______ for this single transaction.
questions.explanation: The fund will pay a maximum of $50,000 for a single transaction and $250,000 maximum for any one licensee. If the broker or salesperson is bankrupt, he/she will not be granted reinstatement until the fund is repaid in full, plus interest at the prevailing legal rate.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT included in the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement?
questions.explanation: Weather conditions are NOT considered a natural hazard.

questions.prompt: In making adjustments to effective gross income for management expenses, on which of the following would an adjustment be made:
choices: An apartment which is occupied by an owner who is also the property manager.
An apartment which is occupied by an on-site manager who receives no compensation.
An apartment which is occupied by an on-site manager who lives in his apartment rent-free in return for his services.
A manager from a neighboring building owned by the same owner.
questions.explanation: Since the on-site manager is living in his unit rent-free, the amount of rent which should be paid by the manager is the management fee and can be deducted by the landlord as an operating expense. The owner may not charge for managing the property himself. If an on-site manager receives no compensation, there would be nothing for the owner to deduct. A manager's salary on another building owned by the same owner would be deducted as an expense against the income from the building he manages.

questions.prompt: A broker is showing property to a person who is an ethnic minority. The broker decided to show property in a certain area because of his customer's race. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Steering is the illegal practice of channeling prospective home purchasers or renters into homogenenous neighborhoods and actively directing them away from neighborhoods of different racial or ethnic composition.

questions.prompt: A mobilehome park is defined as:
choices: 5 motor homes for rent or sale.
5 scattered mobilehome sites for rent or sale.
2 contiguous mobilehome sites for rent or sale.
questions.explanation: A "mobilehome park" is defined as a parcel (or contiguous parcels) of land divided into two or more mobilehome lots for rent or sale.

questions.prompt: The seller must disclose the presence of a military base if it is within:
questions.explanation: It is now well known that certain military bases in California contain live ammunition for various reasons. A seller of residential property located within one mile of such a hazard must give the buyer written notice as soon as practicable before transfer of title. An ordnance location is an area identified by the state or federal government as an area once used for military training purposes and that may contain explosive munitions.

questions.prompt: If a landlord is going to increase the rent, how does he/she need to notify the current tenant?
choices: Deliver written notice in person or by regular mail
Deliver the letter by Certified Mail
questions.explanation: A landlord's notice of rent increase must be in writing. The landlord may deliver a copy of the notice personally or by regular US mail, with proper postage and addressed to the tenant at the rental unit.

questions.prompt: An unlicensed person could receive a finder's fee from a broker:
choices: if the action constituted no more than an introduction of a potential buyer to the broker.
as long as the fee is disclosed.
as long as the fee is not charged to either the buyer or the seller.
questions.explanation: A broker may pay a finder's fee to an unlicensed person for recommending the broker to the buyer or seller providing the unlicensed person does nothing which would require a real estate license.

questions.prompt: If a subdivision project will have a significant effect on the environment, the government agency that approves the project may be required to prepare a(n):
questions.explanation: An Environmental Impact Report (EIR), authorized by the California Environmental Quality Act of 1970 (CEQA), may be required before subdivision approval if the project will have a significant effect on the environment.

questions.prompt: The basic regulation of the housing and construction industries is accomplished by:
questions.explanation: All three of these jurisdictions work together to regulate activities in the housing and construction industries.

questions.prompt: The seller must disclose any material change in the condition of the property or the title that occurs or is discovered by the seller:
choices: after close of escrow and within one year of ownership by the new buyer.
after close of escrow and within a reasonable amount of time, thereafter.
after the contract is executed and prior to the close of escrow.
questions.explanation: The seller must disclose any material change in the condition of the property or the title that occurs or is discovered by the seller after the contract is executed and prior to the close of escrow.

questions.prompt: A blanket encumbrance exists on a large subdivision. The owner negotiates to pay off the loans on certain lots as they are sold. To accomplish this the beneficiary would execute a:
questions.explanation: Under the provisions of a blanket encumbrance, as each individual lot is sold, it is released from the blanket loan which is correspondingly reduced. The beneficiary (lender) requests the trustee to execute and record a deed of partial reconveyance describing the portion of the property released from the blanket loan.

questions.prompt: Jones, who does not have a real estate license, is the owner and president of an investment firm. He advertises and sells properties for his clients. Since these transactions involve real estate, who will prosecute him for violating the real estate law:
questions.explanation: The Real Estate Commissioner can take disciplinary action against a licensee by suspending or revoking the license, and also has the authority to investigate non-licensees alleged to be performing activities for which a license is required, but would not prosecute. County district attorneys are responsible for prosecuting violations of the Real Estate Law that occur in their county (Criminal Action).

questions.prompt: When a broker keeps records electronically, the program he would use for record retrieval is:
questions.explanation: WORM means "write once read many." This indicates that the record cannot be changed once it is entered.

questions.prompt: What should sellers do when they are uncertain whether the property is located within one of the designated natural hazard areas?
choices: Claim (in writing) that you have no actual knowledge that the property is located in a hazardous area.
Hire a third-party professional who specializes in natural hazard disclosures to find out if in fact the property is located within one of the specified hazard zones.
Make a notation in the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement that you have no actual knowledge that the property is located in a hazardous area.
questions.explanation: If the seller (or seller's agent) is not sure, they should hire a third-party professional who specializes in natural hazard disclosures, pay for the cost of obtaining this information, and find out if the property is located within one of the specified hazard zones.

questions.prompt: When a "release schedule" is put into a blanket mortgage for a subdivision, the amount of the loan to be paid off for each lot would likely be proportionately larger for the first lots that are sold. The reason for this practice is:
choices: to increase the security value of the remaining lots.
to compensate for the loss of security as the lots under the blanket encumbrances are removed.
to compensate for the loss of security due to the best lots being sold first.
questions.explanation: All three of these choices are good reasons for requiring larger repayment when the first lots are sold under a blanket encumbrance.

questions.prompt: A broker convinces a white family to put their home up for sale after saying that minority families are moving into the neighborhood. The broker's actions are all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Blockbusting or panic selling violate both federal and state fair housing laws, as well as real estate licensing law.

questions.prompt: Generally, a fact concerning a transaction is considered "material" if:
choices: the seller elects to disclose the fact prior to consummation of the transacation.
prior knowledge of the fact would have prevented the other party from entering into the contract.
all parties to the transaction agree in advance that the fact is important.
the seller's agent determines that the fact warrants disclosure.
questions.explanation: Material Fact: Generally, a matter is considered material if the other party would not have entered into the contract had he/she known the true facts.

questions.prompt: The Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zoning Act resulted in the establishment of Earthquake Fault Zones. How wide is the "typical" zone boundary?
questions.explanation: The Alquist-Priolo Special Studies Zones Act of 1972, renamed the "Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zoning Act" in 1994, regulates development and construction of buildings intended for human occupancy in Earthquake Fault Zones. These zones span the "surface traces" of delineated active faults. The "typical" zone boundaries are set back approximately 660 feet on either side of the fault trace or 1/4 mile in width.

questions.prompt: Properties built before which year DO NOT need a geological report?
questions.explanation: Sellers of homes built before 1960, with one to four units of conventional light-frame construction, require the seller or agent to deliver to the buyer the "Homeowner's Guide to Earthquake Safety," and if the property is commercial the "Commercial Property Owner's Guide". If the buyer receives these booklets, neither the agent nor the seller is required to obtain a geological report. If the property is in an earthquake fault area, a Natural Hazard Zone Disclosure Statement must be delivered to the buyer.

questions.prompt: What is required of a pre-paid rental service when the business plans to move offices?
choices: The company must inform clients of the new address before the move.
The company must inform the clients of the new address within 10 days of the move.
They must inform the clients within 5 days.
They must inform the clients within a month.
questions.explanation: If a prepaid rental listing service (PRLS) licensee or a real estate broker operating a prepaid rental listing service under his broker license proposes to move either the principal location or main office to a different address, he shall, prior to effecting the move, give notice of the address and telephone number of the new principal location or main office in a manner reasonably calculated to reach all of the prospective tenants with whom the PRLS licensee or broker has contracts that have not expired.

questions.prompt: Seller Smith hires broker Jones to list his home. Neither have actual knowledge that the property is located in a hazardous earthquake, flood, or fire area, and for that reason they decide they will not make the Natural Hazard disclosure. After close of escrow the buyer checks with the county and finds out that a map exists that shows the property located within a particular hazard zone. Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: Since the seller and seller's agent had no actual knowledge that the property was located in a hazardous area, they cannot be held responsible.
Since the buyer had the opportunity to hire a third-party professional to investigate this matter, the seller and seller's agent would be without fault.
Since there had never been a fire, flood, or earthquake in the area, the buyer has no recourse.
Since the map was available from the county where the property is located, the seller and his agent will be considered to have knowledge of the fact that the property is in a hazardous area.
questions.explanation: The Natural Hazard Disclosure must be made if the property is located on a list of parcels of properties located within a special hazard's area, or a map exists that specifies the property located within a particular hazard zone. If this information has been made available to the local jurisdictions where the property is located and the property is on either the list or map, the sellers and their agents will be considered to have knowledge of the fact that the property is in one of these high-sensitivity areas. This applies whether or not they have actual knowledge of that fact.

questions.prompt: Regarding environment standards, Federal law requires the seller of a new home to disclose which of the following to the buyer?
questions.explanation: Federal law requires that a "new home" seller (including a subdivider) disclose in every sales contract the type, thickness, and R-value of the insulation which has been or will be installed. (Federal Trade Regulation Section 460.16; Public Resources Code Section 25402 et seq.)

questions.prompt: How long can a broker's commission remain in a trust account?
questions.explanation: Commissions, fees, and other income earned by a broker and collectible from trust funds may remain in the trust account for a period not to exceed 25 days. Regulation 2835 recognizes that it may not always be practical to disburse the earned income immediately upon receipt. So as long as the broker disburses the commission from the trust account within 25 days after it is earned there is no commingling violation.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement and the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement?
choices: Only the seller is responsible for the TDS but the buyer is responsible for the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement.
Only the buyer is responsible for the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement but the seller is responsible for the TDS.
The buyer and seller are equally responsible for both statements.
The seller is responsible to check the map and make the natural hazard disclosure if necessary; on the other hand, the seller is responsible to disclose known facts only on the TDS.
questions.explanation: The Natural Hazard Disclosure must be made by the seller if the property is located on a list of parcels of properties located within a special hazard area or a map exists that specifies the property located within a particular hazard zone. This applies whether or not the seller has actual knowledge of that fact. The Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement (TDS) is the responsibility of the seller and serves to disclose known facts regarding the physical condition of the property.

questions.prompt: In what situation can the listing broker fill in the Natural Hazard Disclosure (NHD) for the seller?
choices: When the disclosure was verbally communicated to the listing agent by the seller.
When the seller is out of state.
When the property is being sold in foreclosure by a representative.
questions.explanation: The seller's agent should NEVER complete any portion of the Natural Hazard Disclosure (NHD) for which the seller is responsible.

questions.prompt: Within how many days should a property manager send out the tenant's refund check with a receipt of deducted amount (if any)?
questions.explanation:
After a tenant moves out, a landlord has 21 calendar days to return the tenant's deposit in full, or mail or personally give to the tenant:

- A written letter explaining why he or she is keeping all or part of the deposit,
- An itemized list of each of the deductions,
- Any remaining refund of the tenant's deposit, and
- Copies of receipts for the charges/deductions, unless repairs cost less than $126 or the tenant waived (gave up) his or her right to get the receipts. If the repairs cannot be finished within the 21-day period, the landlord can send the tenant a good faith estimate of the cost of repairs. Then within 14 days of the repairs being done, the landlord must send the tenant the receipts.

questions.prompt: The Bulk Transfer Law may be found in the:
questions.explanation: The Bulk Transfer Law is part of the Uniform Commercial Code.

questions.prompt: If more than one licensed real estate broker is acting as an agent in a transaction, who is responsible to assure the delivery of the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement (TDS) to the buyer?
choices: The broker who represents the seller.
The broker who has obtained the offer made by the buyer.
The broker who holds a valid Listing Agreement with the seller.
The seller is ultimately responsible no matter how many agents are involved.
questions.explanation: If more than one licensed real estate broker is acting as an agent in a transaction, the agent who has obtained the offer made by the buyer (buyer's agent) is responsible to assure the delivery of the statement to the buyer, unless the seller has given other written instructions for delivery. If the agent who obtained the offer is other than the listing agent, he/she must also fill out and sign the "Agent's Inspection" section of the form.

questions.prompt: Who regulates electronic signature requirements?
questions.explanation: The regulations adopted by the Secretary of State define the types of technologies that are acceptable for creating digital signatures for use by public entities in California.

questions.prompt: Who must sign and deliver a copy of the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement to the buyer?
questions.explanation: The transferor (seller) of any real property subject to the statutory requirements for delivery of the TDS must sign the written statement and deliver it to the buyer.

questions.prompt: A broker may store records in which of the following formats?
questions.explanation: In California, real estate brokers must hold on to their records for three (3) years. That means all listings, deposit receipts, cancelled checks, trust fund records and other documents executed in connection with any transaction must be kept. Records can be created and kept in electronic format or they can be converted to electronic format for storage purposes.

questions.prompt: The Commissioner paid from the Recovery Fund for settlement of a claim based upon a judgment against a licensed broker. If the broker is bankrupt, he/she would be required to:
choices: pay the fund back in full plus interest.
pay back only a certain percentage.
questions.explanation: No broker or salesperson shall be granted reinstatement until he/she has repaid in full, plus interest at the prevailing legal rate, the amount paid from the Recovery Fund.

questions.prompt: Copies of real estate transaction documents must be kept:
choices: by the broker only for 3 years.
questions.explanation: A broker must maintain the records for three years. The retention period runs from the date of the closing of the transaction or if there is no closing from the date of the listing. The law requires a broker to maintain copies of "all listings, deposit receipts, canceled checks, trust records, and other documents executed by him or her or obtained by him or her in connection with any transactions for which a real estate broker license is required." (Bus. and Prof. Code section 10148).

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act?
choices: To standardize the minimum requirements for loan eligibility
To standardize the down payment amounts to prevent discrimination
To prohibit lenders from discriminating on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, family size, handicap, or marital status
questions.explanation: The main purpose of the Equal Credit Opportunity Act is to prohibit lenders from discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, family size, handicap, marital status, or on the grounds of receipt of income from a public assistance program.

questions.prompt: Which of the following documents DOES NOT need to be stored for 3 years?
questions.explanation: It is the broker's responsibility to keep all transaction documents and records for at least 3 years.

questions.prompt: All of the following are transferred by a bill of sale EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Goodwill, stock-in-trade and fixtures would all be included on the bill of sale as part of the transfer of a business. The provisions for transferring a lease would be provided in the lease or a new lease would be drawn up.

questions.prompt: When leasing a commercial property that is merely a "shell" space, the landlord often agrees to spend a specific amount for a qualified tenant. This amount is properly designated as:
questions.explanation: When the landlord or property manager allows a certain sum of money to the tenant to be used for improvements within the rental space, it is called a "tenant improvement allowance." This is usually only found with commercial leases.

questions.prompt: A document which details the responsibilities of a property manager would be called a(n):
questions.explanation: The Management Agreement would delineate the duties and responsibilities of the property manager. This contract creates an agency relationship with the owner of the property.

questions.prompt: Salesperson Kim has several listings and is an agent of Broker Ling. These listings are:
choices: Void if Salesperson Kim changes brokers
The property of Salesperson Kim and Broker Ling
questions.explanation: The listing agreement is a contract between the broker and the seller. It remains the property of Broker Ling if Salesperson Kim changes brokers and the listing remains valid.

questions.prompt: After passing the real estate license examination, a person must apply for the license within:
choices: one year of the passing the examination.
one year of notification of failing.
six months of notification of passing.
questions.explanation: A person must apply for their license within one year from the date you successfully completed (passed) your state licensing examination.

questions.prompt: What happens if you fail to renew your license on-time?
choices: You must reapply and retake the state examination.
You have two years to submit your renewal application and late fees.
You fall into a two year grace period but may continue doing business.
You must complete a 3-hour course in Ethics but may continue doing business.
questions.explanation: If you fail to renew your license on-time (prior to your license expiration date), you may renew your license during the two-year late renewal grace period immediately following your license expiration date. However, you cannot perform activities requiring a real estate license until your license has been renewed.

questions.prompt: In the sale of a business, bulk transfer laws pertain to:
questions.explanation: A "bulk sales transfer" is any transfer in bulk (not a transfer in the ordinary course of the seller's business) of a major part of the materials, inventory, or supplies of an enterprise (stock-in-trade).

questions.prompt: How long does a buyer have to sue the seller of a single family dwelling for something that was not disclosed but should have been disclosed after the buyer moves into the home?
questions.explanation: A lawsuit alleging a breach of a licensee's duty under this law must be filed within two years from the date of occupancy, the date of recordation of the deed to the buyer, or the date of close of escrow, whichever occurs first.

questions.prompt: An unlicensed secretary in a real estate office can:
choices: type listings and sales contracts for salespeople.
prepare and mail postcards for salespeople.
questions.explanation: An unlicensed secretary can only take messages and type for agents. The other choices would be considered activities that would require a real estate license.

questions.prompt: An unlicensed assistant puts together information and assists in writing an advertisement for a broker. For this to be legal, the broker must:
questions.explanation: An unlicensed assistant can gather information and help the broker create ad copy, but the broker must approve it first.

questions.prompt: A broker advertises properties through the World Wide Web. Rules exist making it mandatory for the broker to do which of the following?
choices: Return all messages promptly and correctly within 24 hours.
Employ only real estate licensees to respond to queries.
Exercise proper supervision over non-licensees responding to queries.
Report all international queries to the DRE.
questions.explanation: Only licensed individuals can answer questions (queries) about properties.

questions.prompt: According to California Real Estate Law an unlicensed person may be paid a finder's fee:
choices: as long as it is disclosed.
when it is given just to influence someone to do something.
questions.explanation: A finder's fee is allowed to be paid to an unlicensed person to influence them to do something; for example, to refer potential sellers or buyers to a real estate broker. The broker may NOT pay an unlicensed person to perform an act which would require a license.

questions.prompt: A loan broker asks a person, applying through the broker's office for a new loan, to fill out a questionnaire which asks the borrower's race and marital status. The applicant can:
choices: refuse to disclose his race or marital status.
file a complaint with the real estate commissioner.
supply the information requested so his credit history can be properly checked.
questions.explanation: With reference to a loan application, the borrower is not obligated to disclose either race or marital status.

questions.prompt: Neither the seller nor any listing or selling agent shall be liable for any error, inaccuracy, or omission of any information delivered to the buyer if:
choices: the seller or agent(s) did not know of the mistake.
that item of information containing a mistake was provided by a public agency or third-person professional.
the item of information containing the mistake was provided by a third-person expert but the mistake was known by the seller and seller's agent.
questions.explanation: Neither the transferor nor any listing or selling agent shall be liable for any error, inaccuracy, or omission of any information delivered to the transferee as long as the transferor did not know of the mistake. The seller would also be relieved of responsibility for mistakes if the information was provided by a public agency or third-person professional as to that item of information. The receipt of a report from a third-person expert would not relieve the seller or the seller's agent from the common-law duty to disclose defects in the property which were known or reasonably should have been known.

questions.prompt: The seller of a home died of AIDS in the hospital four days before the sale of the home. Which of the following is correct regarding the broker’s obligated to disclose this to the buyer?
choices: The broker is only required to disclose if the buyer asks.
The broker is not obligated to disclose whatsoever if the death was AIDS-related.
The broker is only required to disclose if the death occurred on the premises.
The broker is only required to disclose that a prior occupant was afflicted with AIDS, not the death.
questions.explanation:
The California Civil Code provides immunity from liability for failure to disclose that an occupant of a property if: 1) The death occurred more than three years before the offer to purchase, lease, or rent the real property; or, 2) The occupant of the property was afflicted with or died from AIDS.

An owner/or agent is NOT required to voluntarily disclose that a prior occupant of the property was living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), or died from Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS)-related complications while living on the property which is being sold. Individuals diagnosed with HIV or AIDS fall into a protected class under Federal law. Therefore, if a buyer specifically asks an agent or seller whether a person had or died from HIV or AIDS-related complications while living in the home, they should answer that any such disclosure of that information could be a violation of the federal fair housing laws. Accordingly, if such information appears to be relevant and material to the buyer, the seller and/or agent should further advise the buyer to pursue such investigation as to the manner of death on their own.

questions.prompt: A broker communicates information given to him by the seller to the buyer in full faith that the seller's information is true. It is later proven that the information was false, and the buyer rescinds. The broker is subject to:
questions.explanation: Even though the broker acted in good faith and was simply passing on information provided by the seller, he/she might still get sued (civil action). The real estate commissioner would not get involved unless it could be proven the broker committed fraud. This is not a criminal case.

questions.prompt: Dividing office overhead by the number of salespersons gives:
questions.explanation: The term "desk costs" reflect the fact that salespeople do, in fact, make use of support staff, have telephone calls, need desk space, and take up some of the time of colleagues and managers. Overhead is divided by the number of salespersons NOT desks.

questions.prompt: A condition or situation where the landlord doesn’t decide to evict the tenant but rather the tenant chooses to leave the property as they deem it to be uninhabitable is called:
questions.explanation: Constructive eviction is a condition or situation where the landlord has not evicted the tenant but rather the tenant chooses to leave the property as they deem it to be uninhabitable. When the landlord (lessor) engages in constructive eviction the tenant may move without giving the thirty day notice or may correct the situation by paying for the repair and deducting the bill from the rent.

questions.prompt: A public report is required if a person is going to subdivide a lot for condominiums into:
questions.explanation: A subdivision (requiring a public report) is the dividing of improved or unimproved land for the purpose of sale, lease, or financing into five or more parcels.

questions.prompt: A licensee was farming a non-integrated neighborhood which was next to an integrated neighborhood by telling the owners that if minority people moved into their neighborhood, their property values would do down. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Blockbusting or panic selling (or panic peddling) violate federal fair housing laws.

questions.prompt: The notice of sale required by the Bulk Transfer Law must include all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: the name and address of the seller.
the description and location of the property.
the name and address where claims can be filed.
questions.explanation: In certain cases the final sales price may not be known yet (i.e., sale at auction).

questions.prompt: The fundamental basis for Fair Housing throughout the United States stems from:
choices: the First Amendment of the Constitution.
the National Association of Fair Housing.
questions.explanation: The constitutionality of all Fair Housing laws is based on the 13th Amendment of the Constitution.

questions.prompt: The maximum security deposit allowed by law for a furnished rental is:
questions.explanation: California state law limits the maximum security deposit for furnished rentals to one months' worth of rent.

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee's business card must include which of the following?
choices: NMLS ID number if the licensee is a Mortgage Loan Originator
questions.explanation: Solicitation materials intended to be the first point of contact with consumers" includes business cards, stationery, advertising fliers, and other materials designed to solicit the creation of a professional relationship between the licensee and a consumer, and excludes an advertisement in print or electronic media and "for sale" signs. First point of contact advertising must contain: 1) the licensee's DRE identification number of each licensee; 2) the license designation by use of the terms broker, agent, Realtor, loan correspondent or the abbreviations bro., agt., or other similar terms or abbreviations and, 3) if that licensee is a mortgage loan originator, the unique identifier assigned to that licensee by the Nationwide Mortgage Licensing System (NMLS).

questions.prompt: A salesperson tells his broker that he is quitting and plans to go to work for another broker. His present employing broker should:
choices: notify the real estate commissioner and hold the license until further notice from the commissioner.
give the salesperson his license and notify the real estate commissioner immediately in writing.
request cancellation of the salesperson's license.
call the other broker to confirm the change.
questions.explanation: The Commissioner's Regulations state that upon termination of employment of a salesperson, the broker shall immediately return the license certificate to the salesperson and immediately notify the commissioner, thereof in writing.

questions.prompt: A landlord must give the lessee (tenant) a copy of the lease within:
questions.explanation: Under California Civil Code Sec. 1962, the landlord or rental agency must provide the lessee (tenant) with a copy of the lease or rental agreement within 15 days of signing in order for the lease to be binding.

questions.prompt: A broker owns many rental properties. He is selling one of the properties and the buyer gives him a check as a deposit. He should:
choices: place the deposit check and all rents in his trust account.
open a separate trust account for rents and put the deposit check in his old trust account.
not deposit either the rents or the deposit check in his trust account.
questions.explanation: The rents and the deposit are personal funds of the broker. Remember, the deposit belongs to the seller and in this case the seller is the broker. Rents only belong in a trust account when the property does not belong to the broker and the broker is managing the property for an owner.

questions.prompt: Each tenant of a proposed conversion of their building from residential property to a condominium has the right to:
questions.explanation: Each tenant of a proposed conversion has an exclusive right to contract for and purchase the unit he/she lives in. The tenant must be offered the same or better terms and conditions that such unit would be initially offered to the general public.

questions.prompt: When the property of the borrower is not adequate security for the loan, the instrument the lender will most likely employ is a(n):
questions.explanation: A blanket encumbrance is used to place a lien simultaneously on more than one property by a single financing instrument.

questions.prompt: The fees charged for property management are usually:
choices: a flat fee and a percentage of gross rents.
questions.explanation: Property managers can charge a flat fee and/or a percentage of gross rents. Usually when they take over a property, the manager may require the flat fee in order to bring the property up to market.

questions.prompt: All of the following are TRUE about a Certified Property Manager (CPM) EXCEPT:
choices: The CPM designation can be given to an individual or a company.
Must be affiliated with the NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF REALTORS®.
Have 3 years of qualifying real estate management experience as defined by IREM.
questions.explanation: Be careful, this is a double-negative question. A Certified Property Manager (CPM) is a real estate professional designation awarded by the Institute of Real Estate Management (IREM) and recognized by the National Association of Realtors (NAR). The CPM designation cannot be given to a company. See https://www.irem.org/credentials/for-individuals/cpm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT included in Phase I of an Environmental Report?
questions.explanation: The correct term is Environmental Site Assessment (ESA). In the United States, an environmental site assessment is a report which identifies potential or existing environmental contamination liabilities. The actual sampling of soil, air, groundwater and/or building materials is typically NOT conducted during a Phase I ESA.

questions.prompt: What is the landlord's responsibility if a tenant notices that some construction in the building may contain asbestos?
choices: The landlord is required to notify the owner in writing.
There are no state laws requiring a landlord to provide asbestos disclosures.
The landlord is required to notify other tenants of the presence of asbestos.
The landlord must provide tenants with alternate living accommodations.
questions.explanation: The Occupational Health and Safety Administration (OSHA) ensures that owners of buildings constructed before 1981 are responsible for locating any existing asbestos. It is the landlord's responsibility to inform tenants of any presence of asbestos, carry out the necessary checks and, if required, remove harmful asbestos.

questions.prompt: When a deed contains discriminatory language or clauses:
choices: the deed must be rewritten by the owner before the property may be sold.
the title company must re-write the deed.
the discriminatory words or clauses are unenforceable.
the clauses may be enforced, since they would be considered "grandfathered" into law.
questions.explanation: Clauses which were written into deeds or CC&R's which allow discrimination are unenforceable. There is no requirement that the deeds or CC&R's must be rewritten.

questions.prompt: Accounts payable of a business would be a(n):
questions.explanation: Accounts payable is considered a liability.

questions.prompt: Which of the following qualifies as a "bulk transfer sale?"
choices: A judicial transfer of a business including all stock used for resale, fixtures, licenses and leases.
A lumber company who transfers a substantial amount of lumber not in the ordinary course of business.
A subdivider who transfers an entire 50-parcel unimproved subdivision.
questions.explanation: A bulk sales would contain the words "not in the ordinary course of the transferor's business."

questions.prompt: When converting an existing residential property to a condominium, existing tenants must be given:
questions.explanation: Before approving the conversion of an existing residential property to a condominium, community apartment, or stock cooperative, the local government agency cannot give its approval unless each of the existing tenants is given written notice of the developer's intention to convert at least 180 days prior to the termination of the tenancy.

questions.prompt: When a licensee is employed as an independent contractor, the employing broker may still have to cover the licensee for:
questions.explanation: By law, all employers are required to maintain workers' compensation insurance for their employees for injuries occurring within the course and scope of the employment. While independent contractors are excluded from coverage, the California Labor and Workforce Development Agency has taken the position that a real estate salesperson is nearly always an employee for workers' compensation insurance purposes. Thus, it is highly recommended that coverage be obtained for salespersons as a matter of sound business practice. The penalties can be very costly if a broker is found to be in violation of the workers' compensation laws. The California Labor and Workforce Development Agency can even shut down the business.

questions.prompt: Brokerage A and Brokerage B agreed to charge all their clients the same percentage commission on all listings. This is a violation of the:
questions.explanation: The foundation for federal Anti-Trust laws is the Sherman Act. The three types of anti-trust violations which are most important in the real estate industry are; 1) conspiracy to fix commissions; 2) imbalanced commission splits; and 3) conspiracy to boycott.

questions.prompt: In July, Easton bought Rothchild's home through the listing broker, McGrew. In November when the first rain came, the tile roof leaked badly in many places. Easton sued Rothchild and McGrew for the cost of the new roof. Testimony in court showed that Rothchild mentioned the need for a new roof to McGrew, but McGrew did not mention it to Easton because "he had not asked about it." What would most likely occur?
choices: Easton would be successful in his suit against Rothchild who would be entitled to recover damages from McGrew.
Easton could recover from Rothchild, but McGrew is not liable to Rothchild.
McGrew is liable to Easton, but Rothchild is not.
Easton is not entitled to recover from either Rothchild or McGrew on the basis of caveat emptor.
questions.explanation: The principal is responsible for all acts of his agents within the authority of the contract. In this case, Rothchild would be responsible for McGrew's negligence and Easton would probably be successful in a suit against Rothchild.

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee did not use diligence in researching problems with a home he had listed and failed to disclose these problems to the buyer. How long does the buyer have to bring a lawsuit against the agent?
questions.explanation: A lawsuit alleging a breach of a licensee's duty must be filed within two years from the date of occupancy or the date of recordation of the deed to the buyer or the date of close of escrow, whichever one occurs first.

questions.prompt: To engage in retail sales you must have a:
questions.explanation: A sales tax permit (seller's permit) authorizes one to engage in the business of selling tangible personal property at a specific location. This permit assigns the retailer a resale number.

questions.prompt: The Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement (TDS) is NOT required when the transfer involves:
choices: transfer of a unit in a subdivision when the buyer has been given a public report.
a transfer ordered by a probate court in administration of an estate.
transfers by foreclosure sales after default.
questions.explanation:
Certain types of transfers are specifically exempted in Civil Code 1102.1. They are as follows:

Transfers requiring a public report pursuant to 11018.1 of the Business and Professions Code and transfers pursuant to 11010.8 of the Business and Professions Code where no public record is required.

Transfers pursuant to court order (such as probate sales, sales by a bankruptcy trustee, etc.)

Transfers by foreclosure (including a deed in lieu of foreclosure and a transfer by beneficiary who has acquired the property by foreclosure or deed in lieu of foreclosure).

Transfers by a fiduciary in the course of the administration of a decedent's estate, guardianship, conservatorship, or trust.

Transfers from one co-owner to one or more other co-owners.

Transfer made to a spouse or to a child, grandchild, parent, grandparent, or other direct ancestor or descendant.

Transfers between spouses in connection with a dissolution of marriage or similar proceeding.

Transfers by the State of Controller pursuant to the Unclaimed Property Law.

Transfers or exchanges to or from any government entity.

*It should be noted, however that a real estate licensee still has a duty to conduct a reasonably competent and diligent visual inspection of accessible areas in almost all of the above situations. In other words although the seller is exempted from having to provide a disclosure statement in certain situations, a licensee must conduct this inspection and disclose the results of the inspection in almost all residential transactions involving one to four units.

questions.prompt: A landlord CANNOT use a security deposit towards which of the following:
choices: Repair damages caused by the tenant, other than normal wear and tear
Replacing lost keys and garage door openers

questions.prompt: For his/her own protection, the purchaser of a business should obtain a:
questions.explanation: To avoid any liability for unpaid sales tax, the purchaser of a business should obtain a clearance receipt from the state Board of Equalization stating that the sales tax has been paid through a particular date.

questions.prompt: A broker communicates information given to him by the seller to the buyer in full faith that the seller's information is true. It is later proven that the information was false, and the buyer rescinds. The broker is subject to:
questions.explanation: Even though the broker acted in good faith and was simply passing on information provided by the seller, he/she might still get sued (civil action). The real estate commissioner would not get involved unless it could be proven the broker committed fraud. This is not a criminal case.

questions.prompt: The Subdivided Lands Act applies to:
choices: the owner of the subdivided property.
any subdivider engaged by the owner of the property.
any real estate licensee acting as an agent for the seller of a subdivision.
questions.explanation: The Subdivided Lands Act applies both to the owner of the subdivided property and to any subdivider engaged by the owner of the property. The law also applies to any real estate licensee acting as an agent for the seller of a subdivision.

questions.prompt: The potential penalties for a licensee's violation of the laws concerning the handling of trust funds include:
questions.explanation: The potential penalties for a licensee's violation of the laws concerning the handling of trust funds are diverse and may be very costly in terms of money, reputation, and ability to continue licensed real estate activities. Potential penalties range from possible violations of the Realtors Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, and injunctions, and receivership, to suspension or revocation of the real estate license.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum amount that could be recovered from the Recovery Fund for one salesperson?
questions.explanation: This question is asking for the maximum amount that may be recovered for any one salesperson. 50,000 for a single transaction, but $250,000 maximum for any one licensee.

questions.prompt: A buyer signs the purchase agreement and the seller accepts. The agent personally delivers acceptance of the offer to the buyer and also drops off the seller's Transfer Disclosure Statement. How long after receiving the TDS does the buyer have to rescind the contract?
questions.explanation: Section 1102.3 of the Civil Code says, "If any disclosure or any material amendment of any disclosure required to be made public by this article, is delivered after the execution of an offer to purchase, the transferee shall have three days after delivery in person or five days after delivery by deposit in the mail to terminate his or her offer by delivery of a written notice of termination to the transferor or transferor's agent."

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee sells a used mobilehome. How much time does the licensee have to submit a contract of sale to the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)?
questions.explanation: A real estate licensee must give written notice to HCD of the transfer on an HCD form not later than the end of the 10th calendar day after the sale. (Real Estate Commissioner's Regulation 2861.)

questions.prompt: Which of the following defines the term "reconciliation?"
