choices: comparing two or more sets of records to determine whether their balances agree
periodically emptying an account to obtain a zero balance
making sure debits always equal credits
checking the chronological sequence of trust fund receipts and disbursements
questions.explanation: There is an interrelation between the trust fund bank account record, the separate beneficiary or transaction record, and the bank statement. If there is an entry made on one record, there must also be a corresponding entry on the other records. Reconciliation is the process of comparing two or more sets of records to determine whether their balances agree.

questions.prompt: To assure the accuracy of trust fund accounting records, they must be reconciled at least:
questions.explanation: To assure the accuracy of trust fund records, they must be reconciled at least once-a-month, usually at the end of each month.

questions.prompt: A licensed real estate broker who owned a large real estate firm operating under the name ABC Realty Company, listed a property for a total price of $40,000. The broker and many of his salespersons were all principals in an investment company operating under the name of Realty Income Investment Company. The investment company decided to purchase the property so the broker presented an all cash offer to the owner for the full price, but did not disclose to the seller who the purchasers were. The seller accepted the offer and opened escrow. Under these circumstances:
choices: the broker's actions were perfectly legal since he offered the full cash price.
the broker's offer would be legal provided he added to the escrow instructions the fact that the purchasing firm was composed of brokers and salespersons.
the broker acted properly provided he agreed to waive any commission.
the broker's action was improper because he did not reveal the true identity of the purchaser.
questions.explanation: The broker has a duty to the seller to reveal all material facts. The fact that the buyers are licensed would be considered a material fact, and therefore, must be revealed before the buyer accepts the offer.

questions.prompt: A broker is selling an apartment complex and puts together a prospectus which shows a 12% yield. In the prospectus, the broker shows the correct gross scheduled income, but fails to show a vacancy and bad debt deduction. He also fails to include management, maintenance and several other operating expenses. The buyer buys the property based on the income analysis given to him by the broker. The broker is guilty of:
questions.explanation: Based on the facts presented in this question, answer (B) is the best choice. The question does not state whether the omission of the operating expenses was intentional or whether it was an oversight. If it was intentional, the broker would most likely have committed fraud since he would be attempting to deceive the buyer. If the broker's actions were not intentional, it would be misrepresentation. While there are no criminal penalties for misrepresentation, this type of conduct could make the purchase contract voidable, expose the licensee to civil damages and lead to the suspension or revocation of his/her real estate broker license.

questions.prompt: When a new real estate brokerage is establishing a website, the first step is:
questions.explanation: The first step is registering the domain name. For example, in the URL https://www.XYZrealty.com, the domain name is XYZrealty.com.

questions.prompt: A broker has a management contract on an apartment building complex. He collects rents and deposits them in his trust fund bank account. He also acts as a broker on other transactions and puts buyer deposits in the same trust fund bank account. Which of the following is correct regarding this practice?
choices: It is legal as long as he keeps records of beneficiary transactions.
It is legal as long as he is bonded for the maximum amount of the trust fund bank account.
It is legal as long as he does not deposit more than $30,000.
questions.explanation: A real estate broker may operate a property management company and a real estate sales office with his or her broker license. Client's trust funds from both activities may be placed in one trust account. It is not necessary for the broker to maintain separate trust accounts for each activity.

questions.prompt: A broker must have a written broker-salesperson agreement with each of his/her:
questions.explanation: Every broker must have a written agreement with each of his/her salespersons, whether licensed as a salesperson or as a broker under a broker-salesperson arrangement. The agreement shall be dated and signed by the parties and shall cover material aspects of the relationship between the parties, including supervision of licensed activities, duties and compensation.

questions.prompt: A seller (or seller's agent) must give the buyer a separate "Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement" if the property lies within which of the following specified areas?
choices: A very high fire hazard severity zone
questions.explanation:
In addition to the usual Transfer Disclosure Statement required by Civil Code Section 1102.6, a seller (or the seller's agent) must give the prospective buyer a separate "Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement" if the residential property lies within one or more of six statutorily specified areas:

A special flood hazard area designated by the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

An area of potential flooding in the event of a dam failure, designated by the state Office of Emergency Services.

A very high fire hazard severity zone designated by the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection.

A wildland fire area that may contain substantial forest fire risks and hazards, designated by the State Board of Forestry.

An earthquake fault zone designated by the State Geologist.

A seismic hazard zone designated by the State Geologist.

questions.prompt: Which of the following events would require the subdivider to notify the Real Estate Commissioner?
choices: The subdivider changes provisions in the purchase contract.
questions.explanation: Any material change involving the subdivision must be reported to the Real Estate Commissioner. Examples of material changes include physical changes, changes in contracts, or changes in deed restrictions. New ownership of the subdivision would also constitute a material change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would realize the greatest benefit from the Bulk Sales Law?
questions.explanation: The major purpose of the bulk transfer status is to afford a merchant's creditors an opportunity to satisfy their claims against a merchant who owes them money before the merchant can sell his/her assets and vanish with proceeds of the sale.

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee can list or sell:
choices: a mobilehome with a tax ID number.
questions.explanation: A real estate broker may list and sell a mobilehome if it has been registered with the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD).

questions.prompt: Realtor Ken hired an unlicensed person named Jose to hand out his brochures, fliers, and door hangers in his farm neighborhood. Ken also instructed Jose to go to his health club and hand out printed information. Property owner Mary, who has already listed her home with another broker, received a phone call from Jose talking about a possible meeting with Ken. Jose was using dialogue which was a scripted pitch written by Ken. Mary happened to record the conversation. Which of the following statements is correct?
choices: This is perfectly acceptable for the unlicensed person and the broker.
The unlicensed person is performing acts for which a real estate license is required.
An unlicensed person may pass out brochures, but under no circumstances talk to a prospective client.
It is unethical for a Realtor to solicit business from an owner who has a listing with another broker.
questions.explanation: The Realtor's Code of Ethics considers this to be unethical behavior. One Realtor may not solicit owners who have listed their property with another licensed real estate broker.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is TRUE regarding trust fund accounting records?
choices: Only manually produced accounting records are acceptable.
Only computerized accounting records are acceptable.
Either manually produced or computerized accounting records are acceptable.
Only professionally produced accounting records are acceptable.
questions.explanation: Either manually produced or computerized accounting records are acceptable.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is required to operate as an advance-fee rental agent?
choices: a written contract with prospective tenants
access to the Multiple Listing Service
questions.explanation: An advance-fee rental agent collects a fee in advance from prospective tenants to find them suitable rental properties. An advance-fee rental agent must have a Prepaid Rental Listing Service license (PRLS), but real estate brokers are exempt from this license requirement. PRLS contracts must be in writing and approved by the Real Estate Commissioner.

questions.prompt: Real estate licenses are issued for:
questions.explanation: Real estate licenses are issued for a four year term.

questions.prompt: A subdivider must give a copy of the Commissioner's public report to:
choices: anyone who intends to purchase one or more lots.
any person, at any time on request.
only purchasers of lots just before they sign the purchase contract.
questions.explanation: All prospective purchasers must be given a copy of the public report and be allowd to read it. A copy of the report must be given to anyone requesting a copy at any time.

questions.prompt: A tract developer learns that a large national cosmetics manufacturer is moving one of his plants near an area in which he is building a large number of new homes and condominiums. Since a great number of the employees of the cosmetic firm will be women, he decides to gear his sales promotion towards this group. He tells his advertising agency to aim all of their ads to reflect a preference for female buyers. Realizing he can't discriminate against any one group, he advises his sales agent to be sure to set up a quota for Caucasian, Black, Chicano, and Asian buyers. Once the quota has been reached they should discourage any further sales to that racial group by adjusting the prices. If the developer follows this plan, he violates:
choices: the fair housing laws based on his ad campaign, but not the quota system.
the fair housing laws based on his racial quota system, but not the ad campaign.
the fair housing laws in both his ad campaign and racial quota system.
questions.explanation: A developer cannot gear ads to just one group. Racial quotas are also considered discriminatory. Using prices to exclude certain racial groups also violates fair housing laws.

questions.prompt: What are the seller and broker disclosure requirements regarding Megan's law?
choices: The location of registered sex offenders in the area must be disclosed.
The names and location of registered sex offenders in the area must be disclosed.
Only a specified notice about the database of registered sex offenders is required.
There is no registry of convicted sex offenders so it does not need to be disclosed.
questions.explanation: California Civil Code Section 2079.10a requires that the following notice be given to a purchaser of residential real property of one-to-four units as required by Megan's Law. Once the specified notice is given, the notice is deemed to be sufficient to notify the buyer of the statewide database. Real estate brokers are not required to provide any other information regarding the proximity of registered sex offenders, absent actual knowledge (Cal. Civ. Code § 2079.10a(b)).

questions.prompt: The Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement (TDS) provides information regarding the:
choices: chain of title of the property.
agency relationships between the parties to the transaction.
commission split between real estate agents.
questions.explanation: As required by California Civil Code Sections 1102 - 1102.14, a transferee (buyer) of residential real property is entitled to a statement from the transferor (seller) which provides information regarding the physical condition of the property. (See Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement)

questions.prompt: A broker wanted to operate a real estate office under the fictitious name MLB Realty. Before operating under a fictitious name, the broker must:
choices: publish the fictitious name in a newspaper of general circulation.
file under the Secretary of State.
obtain a DRE license bearing the fictitious business name.
file with the city as a fictitious business.
questions.explanation: Although the other choices may be steps in obtaining a fictitious business name, the broker may not do business under a fictitious name until he/she has a DRE license issued in the fictitious name.

questions.prompt: The term "Housing Accommodation" refers to real property of how many units when occupied by the owner?
questions.explanation: The phrase "Housing accomodations" is defined as improved or unimproved real property used or intended to be used as a residence by the owner and which consists of not more than four dwelling units.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is provided by the purchaser upon resale of a business?
questions.explanation: A resale certificate allows a buyer (retailer) to purchase inventory without paying sales tax as long as the goods are going to be resold to customers. In the sale of a business, sales tax is not charged on stock-in-trade which was held for resale.

questions.prompt: A city's master plan would include:
choices: circulation, including distribution of transportation facilities and public utilities.
land use in terms of population and building density.
noise problems, both existing and foreseeable.
questions.explanation: Every city and county within California now is required by state law to adopt a comprehensive, long-term General Plan, also referred to as the Master Plan, for development within its jurisdiction. It usually includes background information on the area economy, its development, population growth, and existing land uses. The Government Code requires that every General Plan include provisions for land use, circulation, housing, open space, noise, and safety.

questions.prompt: A profit-and-loss statement would include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The value of inventory would appear on the balance sheet.

questions.prompt: Under the Subdivision Map Act, subdivision reports must be filed with the:
choices: city or county where the land is located.
questions.explanation: The Subdivision Map Act gives the local authorities control over the physical aspects of the subdivision as to zoning, building, and health codes.

questions.prompt: How much of a fee can the property manager charge a tenant for insufficient funds on a rent payment? (not from what the bank charges).
questions.explanation: California rules on bounced check fees allow landlords to charge $25 for the first bounced check, and $35 for each additional bounced check.

questions.prompt: A broker sells a house advertised "as-is". There are no obvious defects that would be evident to a prudent buyer upon inspection, but the seller and the broker know that the plumbing is very defective. The buyer moves in and discovers the defects. The buyer then sues the broker and the seller for misrepresentation. The suit will probably be:
choices: successful because the seller and the broker withheld material information that should have been disclosed.
successful because an "as-is" clause does not relieve a seller or broker from liability for disclosing material facts which they knew of.
unsuccessful because selling the property "as-is" gives constructive notice that there are defects.
unsuccessful because the defects would have been revealed if the purchase agreement had contained an inspection clause.
questions.explanation: An "as-is" clause by itself does not relieve a residential property seller or broker from liability for latent defects which they knew of or latent defects which the seller or broker had a duty to inspect for and discover. This is because an "as-is" clause by itself never bars claims of fraudulent misrepresentation and does not even bar claims of negligent misrepresentation, concealment, or nondisclosure.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must comply with the Subdivision Map Act?
questions.explanation: Parcels of any size fall under the Map Act. Parcels of 160-acres or more are exempt from the Subdivisions Lands Law.

questions.prompt: When a real estate licensee accepts trust funds from his/her client in connection with the purchase of real property, the licensee must place these funds into the proper place:
choices: by the next working day following receipt.
within three business days following receipt.
by midnight of the current business day.
by midnight of the third business day following receipt.
questions.explanation: If the broker (or broker's salesperson) fails to place the funds into one of the three authorized places within three business days following receipt of the funds by the broker or by the broker's salesperson, he/she is liable for commingling the funds.

questions.prompt: In real estate transactions, the type of misrepresentation which occurs least often is:
questions.explanation: Fraud is deliberate. Few brokers try to deliberately commit fraud.

questions.prompt: In an effort to enforce trust fund handling requirements, the Real Estate Commissioner continuously:
choices: sponsors lectures on trust fund handling throughout the state.
audits and examines broker's trust fund records on a state-wide basis.
calls brokers to keep them up to date on trust fund handling requirements.
changes the trust fund handling laws to keep brokers on their toes.
questions.explanation: The Real Estate Commissioner continuously audits and examines broker's trust fund records on a state-wide basis.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding public reports?
choices: A public report may be renewed under certain circumstances.
A copy of the public report must be given to anyone on request.
A copy of the public report must be displayed in the subdivision sales office.
questions.explanation: All of the choices are true as to public reports. If all parcels have not been sold within five years of issuance of a final public report, it can be renewed for an additional five years.

questions.prompt: A Master Plan would be concerned with all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Deed restrictions are prohibitions against a property's use that are imposed in the grantee's deed.

questions.prompt: Funds may be withdrawn from a real estate broker's trust account by an unlicensed employee:
choices: for payment of general operation expenses provided proper accounting is made and money is returned.
when the unlicensed employee has written authorization from the broker and has fidelity bond coverage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following need NOT comply with the requirements of the Map Act?
questions.explanation: Local control of the physical aspects of this subdivision would happen in Nevada.

questions.prompt: The Subdivision Map Act requires:
choices: delivery of a copy of the public report to purchasers.
special financing terms for purchasers of subdivisions.
subdividers to file tentative maps with the city or county planning commission.
questions.explanation: The Subdivision Map Act covers local control over the physical aspects of a subdivision. Under this Act, subdividers are required to file a tentative map to the local planning commission showing streets, property lines, utilities, etc.

questions.prompt: The maximum security deposit allowed by law for an unfurnished rental is:
questions.explanation: In July 2024, California passed a law saying Unfurnished and Furnished rentals have a set limit that cannot exceed one month's rent.

questions.prompt: Agent Jones has an offer on a listing contingent on the buyer's uncle approving the property, since he will be financing the loan. Agent Jones hasn't discussed this with the buyers, but assures the seller that there will be no problems regarding the uncle. After the seller accepts the offer, the buyers tell the agent that the uncle is out of town and they don't know when he will return. With regard to the seller, the agent acted:
questions.explanation: The listing agent has acted unethically in this case since he failed to explain the potential risks concerning the contingency. An agent must explain the meaning and probable significance of any contingency in an offer that he/she knows or reasonably believes may affect the closing date of the transaction, or the timing of vacating the property by the seller, or its occupancy by the seller.

questions.prompt: A public report is good for five years from the:
choices: date the first lot is sold.
date of delivery to the buyer.
questions.explanation: A public report is good for five years from the date of issuance.

questions.prompt: According to the case of Easton v. Strassburger, a real estate broker is required to reveal:
choices: those defects which are known by the broker.
those defects which are known or should be known by the broker.
only those defects which the seller has revealed.
questions.explanation: The broker must do a competent, diligent visual inspection of the accessible areas and reveal all material facts. Competent implies that the broker should see certain defects that would be discovered by the ordinary standard of care. (See Easton v. Strassburger)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered trust funds?
choices: A check used as a deposit
A personal note made payable to the seller
questions.explanation: Trust funds are money or other things of value that are received by a broker or salesperson on behalf of a principal or any other person, and which are held for the benefit of others in the performance of any act(s) for which a real estate license is required. Trust funds may be cash or non-cash items. Some examples are: cash, a check used as a deposit(whether made payable to the broker or to an escrow or title company), a personal note made payable to the seller, or even a pink slip to a car that is given as a deposit.

questions.prompt: Someone that sells his findings, but is not accountable to another for the methods used is called an:
questions.explanation: An independent contractor is one who is retained to perform a certain act, but who is subject to the control and direction of another only as to the end result and not as to how he or she performs the act.

questions.prompt: City and County Planning Commission members:
choices: have the authority to make recommendations to the City Council or Board of Supervisors on subdivisions.
must possess experience and background in real estate.
are appointed in cities and elected in counties.
questions.explanation: Each city and county must appoint a planning commission. Planning commission members do not need real estate experience. They are delegated the authority to make recommendations concerning the processing of subdivisions under the Subdivision Map Act.

questions.prompt: Which of the following allows a subdivider to enter into binding contracts with purchasers for lots but does not allow transactions to be completed?
questions.explanation: Because the public report may take months to compile, the subdivider may begin taking reservations for future purchases on the basis of an approved conditional public report (called the "pink report"). No sales can be closed or transaction completed, however until the final public report (called the "white report") is received.

questions.prompt: How much of a broker's personal funds may be contributed to a client's trust fund bank account to offset any bank service charges?
choices: $25.00 or the amount of charges by the bank
questions.explanation: Since banks sometimes have service charges, out of necessity, the broker is allowed to maintain up to $200 of personal funds in a trust account to cover these type of bank charges. Trust funds may not be used to pay for these type of expenses. The better practice is to have the bank charge the broker's office or general account for the trust account fees and charges.

questions.prompt: The Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zone Act is concerned with:
choices: all buildings in the entire state of California.
all residential buildings within an earthquake fault zone.
all buildings within an earthquake fault zone.
commercial buildings within an earthquake fault zone.
questions.explanation: The Alquist-Priolo Earthquake Fault Zone Act was passed to prevent buildings constructed for human occupancy from being constructed astride active faults. The State Geologist has identified earthquake fault zones called "Special Studies Zones." Any development located within one of these Special Studies Zones (which is not exempt) must have a geologic analysis.

questions.prompt: What does the Homeowner's Guide to Earthquake Safety discusses?
choices: Underground gas lines, electrical lines, and water pipes.
Existing fault lines and there exact location.
The most common weaknesses that can cause earthquake damage to a home.
questions.explanation: The Homeowner's Guide to Earthquake Safety describes the most common weaknesses that can cause damage to homes, in the event of an earthquake and provides the homeowner with basic information about finding and fixing those weaknesses.

questions.prompt: A real estate salesperson shows their own income property to a prospective buyer. The buyer seems interested and salesperson says, "you should submit a full price offer" but never tells the buyer it is his own property. This behavior is:
questions.explanation: It is unlawful for the licensee-agent to fail to disclose to the buyer of real property, in a transaction in which the licensee is an agent for the buyer, the nature and extent of the licensee's direct or indirect ownership interest in such real property.

questions.prompt: What is the definition of MLS?
questions.explanation: A Multiple Listing Service (MLS) is a service used by a group of real estate brokers. They band together to create a MLS that allows each of them to see one another's listings of properties for sale.

questions.prompt: In addition to the licensee's duty to disclose matters known to the licensee, he/she also has the duty to:
choices: provide legal advice in situations where there is not time to consult an expert.
make minor repairs to a property when absolutely necessary.
conduct a reasonable investigation to discover the true facts regarding the property.
provide tax advice regarding the transfer of real property.
questions.explanation: In addition to the licensee's statutory requirement to make certain disclosures to the buyer, both the listing agent and the selling agent have a statutory duty to conduct a reasonably competent and diligent visual inspection and disclose to a prospective purchaser all facts which materially affect the value or desirability of the property that such an investigation would reveal.

questions.prompt: Regulation of proper sewage and sanitation construction practices are enforced by the:
choices: Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
questions.explanation: Drainage, plumbing, water, and sewage are under the control of the state Department of Public Health and are enforced by the local health officer.

questions.prompt: When broker Smith accepts a deposit check from a client, he forwards the check directly to escrow. According to trust fund record keeping requirements, which of the following is CORRECT?
choices: It is NOT necessary to keep a record of trust funds received and forwarded to escrow.
It is NOT necessary to keep a record of trust funds not deposited into the trust account.
A record of trust funds received but not deposited to the trust fund bank account must be maintained.
Transaction folders maintained by a broker for each transaction showing the receipt and disposition of undeposited checks are acceptable alternatives to formal records.
questions.explanation: Even if the trust funds are forwarded directly to escrow, a broker is still required to keep track of funds received and not deposited to a trust fund bank account.

questions.prompt: A "dedication" under the Map Act would happen:
choices: when the final public report is completed.
when the approved subdivision map is recorded.
when the last lot of a subdivision is sold.
when the first lot of a subdivision is under contract.
questions.explanation: This dedication is accomplished by recording a subdivision map approved by local officials expressly indicating those areas dedicated to the public.

questions.prompt: When an agent is accused of "puffing", the agent might be guilty of which of the following:
choices: Trying to convince a potential seller of his wide popularity among local people.
Convincing the appraiser to assign a higher value to the property than is justified by the comparable recent sales in the area.
Exaggerating the features of the property or neighborhood when showing the property to prospective buyers.
Convincing a seller to offer a higher commission than is customary for that type of property.
questions.explanation: Puffing is the exaggerating of features of neighborhood or property.

questions.prompt: The requirement of the seller to provide a "Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement" to the buyer covers:
questions.explanation: The Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement is now a legally required part of most residential property transactions.

questions.prompt: Broker A meets the Brown family and the Browns make an offer on a house on Elm Street which is owned by Jones. The offer is contingent on the sale of the Brown's house on Main Street which is several counties away. Seller Jones accepted the offer. Broker A refers the Browns to Broker R for the sale of their Main Street home. A written compensation referral form is executed. According to Article 7 of the Code of Ethics, Broker A must disclose:
choices: The compensation on Elm St. to both Brown and Jones
The compensation on Main St. to Brown only
Both the compensation on Elm St. and Main St. to Brown
Both the compensation on Elm Street and Main Street to Brown and Jones
questions.explanation: According to Article 7 of the Code of Ethics, of the National Association of Realtors®, all compensation must be revealed to all principals in the transaction.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be considered a violation of the Fair Employment and Housing Act?
choices: An owner of a single family residence who refuses to rent a room in his home for religious reasons.
Failure to include accommodations for handicapped people when constructing a new building.
An advertisement in a newspaper which states, "Catholic roommate wanted."
questions.explanation: Under the Fair Employment and Housing Act, failure to design or build a multi-family dwelling of four or more units in a manner that allows disabled persons access and use is considered discrimination.

questions.prompt: The Unruh Civil Rights Act prohibits discrimination in:
choices: all business establishments of every kind.
questions.explanation: The Unruh Civil Rights Act prohibits housing discrimination as to sex, race, color, religion, ancestry, or national origin in all accommodations and business establishments.

questions.prompt: The stock of a business sold under the bulk sales law is transferred by:
questions.explanation: The stock of a business is personal property. Personal property is transferred by a bill of sale.

questions.prompt: In addition to the Subdivided Lands Law and Map Act, there is federal control of subdivisions under the:
questions.explanation: In addition to state control under the Subdivided Lands Law and control under the Map Act, the federal government controls subdivisions under the Interstate Land Sales Act. The Act requires developers to file a development statement describing the details of a subdivision with the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development. The California public report can be substituted for the federal report.

questions.prompt: In order for a licensed salesperson of a broker to legally manage the office, initial contracts, and constitute proper supervision, which of the following is required:
choices: 2 years full-time experience during the (immediate) preceding 5 years.
2 years full-time experience during the (immediate) preceding 5 years plus 16 college units.
2 years full-time experience during the (immediate) preceding 10 years.
Experience is not required as long as they are licensed.
questions.explanation: The salesperson must have 2 years full-time experience during the (immediate) preceding 5 years.

questions.prompt: California real estate law originated from:
questions.explanation: In general, California's laws relating to real estate originated from English common law.

questions.prompt: A broker is representing a subdivider selling a new large subdivision of single family dwellings. The broker knows that conformity is the key to maintaining optimum value in the new subdivision. The broker and his salesperson decide that in order to achieve this goal they will quote higher prices to minorities than to other buyers. This would be:
choices: illegal for the broker and the salesperson.
not illegal for the broker or salesperson.
acceptable practice for all parties involved as this behavior is in the best interest of both the seller and buyers.
questions.explanation: This is discrimination. The broker and salesperson are behaving illegally. The question does not indicate the seller knew of the broker's plans, so choice A is the best choice.

questions.prompt: To enforce and administer the Map Act, the local planning commission would be interested in:
questions.explanation: The Subdivision Map Act gives the local authorities control over the physical aspects of the subdivision. The objectives of the Act are to coordinate subdivision design, including streets and utilities with the General Plan.

questions.prompt: Recommendations made by the city planning commission are:
questions.explanation: Recommendations made by the Planning Commission are binding rulings mandated in the general plan.

questions.prompt: A flood hazard exists when an area floods:
choices: More than twice in ten years
More than three times in ten years
questions.explanation: A flood hazard is an area which floods more than twice in ten years.

questions.prompt: A seller lists a property with an agent. The agent shows the property to a white prospect at one price, and the agent's broker shows the property to a minority couple at a higher price. The seller then sells the property to a neighbor because the neighbor does not want minorities next door. Who has NOT broken the law?
questions.explanation: The broker and anyone associated with him/her have broken the law by representing the property at a higher price to the minority couple. The white prospect is the only one who has not broken the law.

questions.prompt: The Subdivision Lands Law is administered by:
questions.explanation: The Subdivided Lands Law is directly administered by the Real Estate Commissioner. Its objective is to protect purchasers of property in new subdivisions from fraud, misrepresentation, or deceit in the marketing of subdivided lots, parcels, units and undivided interests in California.

questions.prompt: A real estate licensee who accepts funds from others in connection with any transaction for which a license is required must place them in:
choices: The hands of the offeree or owner
A trust account maintained by the licensee
questions.explanation:
A real estate licensee who accepts funds from others in connection with any transaction for which a license is required must place them in:

a neutral escrow depository,

in the hands of the offeree or owner, or

in a trust account maintained by the licensee.

questions.prompt: The Subdivided Lands Law controls the sale or leasing of new subdivisions to California residents:
choices: only if the property is located in California.
only if the property is unimproved.
regardless of the location of the property.
only if the property is unimproved and located outside of California.
questions.explanation: Subdivisions offered for sale to Californians that are either in state or out-of-state are still under the control of the Subdivision Lands Act.

questions.prompt: A retired farmer decides to subdivide the 1,000 acres he owns into five 200 acre parcels to be leased for agricultural purposes. These parcels would be exempt from the requirements of the Subdivision Map Act if they contain:
questions.explanation: Land leased for agricultural purposes is exempt from the Map Act regardless of size.

questions.prompt: Who is required to provide the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement to the buyer?
questions.explanation: The responsibility to provide the Natural Hazard Disclosure Statement to the buyer lies with the seller (or seller's agent).

questions.prompt: A buyer makes an offer on a property but does not have available cash for the down payment. He executes a promissory note in the amount of $1,000 at 12% interest to be repaid in 10 days. The broker:
choices: may accept it as long as the broker guarantees its repayment.
may only accept cash or personal check.
may accept it but must disclose this fact to the seller before the offer is accepted.
this method of deposit is immaterial.
questions.explanation: A down payment or deposit may be cash or non-cash. It may be cash, check, personal note made payable to the seller, or even a pink slip to a car. If it is in the form of a promissory note, the broker must disclose this fact to the seller before the offer is accepted.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum square feet for a master bedroom?
questions.explanation: Master bedrooms are typically a minimum of 120 square feet (10 x 12), without taking into account closet space or a bathroom.

questions.prompt: Broker Jones receives a 3% deposit from a buyer for the purchase of a house. He also receives appraisal and credit report fees for another client. In addition, he receives rent money on an apartment building which he manages for a client. With regard to these funds:
choices: he can put everything in one trust account.
he must have a separate trust account for the 3% deposit.
he must have a separate trust account for each client.
he must have three accounts - one for sales, one for rentals, and one for loans.
questions.explanation: It is legal for a broker to operate a property management company, a real estate sales office, and/or mortgage loan brokerage office. It is legal for him to place all trust funds received into one trust account as long as he keeps accurate records of beneficiary transactions.

questions.prompt: The installation of curbs, gutters, streets, and utilities in a new subdivision is the responsibility of:
questions.explanation: As a condition of approval, developers must provide plans for installation and/or improvement of curbs, gutters, streets, and utilities.

questions.prompt: It is important for a landlord to obtain all of the information on a rental application in order for the landlord to make a decision about renting to a particular person or to more than one person. A landlord thinks it is important to know whether or not a couple is married. Is it legal for the landlord to inquire whether or not a couple is married on the rental application?
choices: Yes, as it may affect the couple's ability to pay rent.
Yes, because this is a moral issue.
It is legal, but might be considered unethical.
No, this would be considered discrimination.
questions.explanation: It is considered discrimination to require disclosure of marital status on a rental application.

questions.prompt: A real estate broker can store records electronically as long as:
choices: electronic records are backed up on a monthly basis.
the broker is able to provide a paper copy of any document or record requested by the DRE.
the electronic image storage media is an erasable, "read-write" file that allow changes to the stored document or record.
records copied and stored in electronic format are retained for one year.
questions.explanation:
Copies of real estate documents, such as all listings, real estate purchase agreements, trust fund records, and any other type of real estate related documents can be stored on electronic image storage media if the following requirements of Regulation 2729(a) are satisfied:

1. The electronic image storage shall be nonerasable "write once, read many," that DOES NOT allow changes to the stored document or record.
2. Records copied and stored in electronic format shall be retained for three years.
3. Electronic records should be backed up daily.
4. The broker shall provide, at his or her expense, a paper copy of any document or record requested by the DRE.

**Look out for another question relating to what storage formats are allowed. A broker may store records on paper, electronic, or microfiche.

questions.prompt: Seller Jones hired broker Smith to list his property. Seller Jones excluded his washer and dryer. Buyer Dana makes an offer on the property and includes the washer and dryer in the offer. After reviewing the offer, seller Jones was still not willing to sell the appliances. Buyer Dana was out of town and unreachable. Broker Smith said he was sure that buyer Dana would not want to lose the house so he crossed out the appliances on the offer and initialed the change himself. To further induce seller Jones to accept the offer, broker Smith said he would find seller Jones another house immediately, which he never did. Which of the following is TRUE regarding broker Smith's actions?
choices: His behavior would subject him to criminal action.
questions.explanation: Making an addition to or modification of the terms of an instrument previously signed or initialed by a party to a transaction without the knowledge and consent of the party is illegal. In most cases, actions that are considered illegal would also be considered unethical.

questions.prompt: Commingling is one of the greatest single causes for loss of license. Which of the following would NOT be considered commingling?
choices: Holding an uncashed deposit check after acceptance of an offer when directed to do so by the seller.
Cashing a deposit check and placing the money in the broker's safe, properly identified as being the deposit received from the buyer.
Depositing either cash or a check received as a deposit in the broker's personal account to be held until called for by the escrow officer.
Depositing money received by his/her client in the broker's personal account to pay miscellaneous expenses.
questions.explanation:
An exception to this rule is when a check is received from an offeror (seller) in connection with an offer to purchase or lease. In this case, the deposit check may be held uncashed by the broker until acceptance of the offer if the following conditions are met:

The check by its terms expressly provides that it is not to be negotiated by the broker or if the offeror has given written instructions to the broker that the check shall not be deposited or cashed until acceptance of the offer, and

The offeree is informed, before or at the time the offer is presented for acceptance that the check is being so held.

questions.prompt: Complaints involving violations of discrimination should be reported to the:
choices: Department of Fair Employment and Housing.
Department of Housing and Community Development.
questions.explanation: Complaints involving violations of the Fair Housing laws are submitted to the Department of Fair Employment and Housing.

questions.prompt: Each city or county appoints a Planning Commission because:
choices: they must do so to appropriate funds.
the board of supervisors orders it.
questions.explanation: The formation of a Planning Commission is required by state law.

questions.prompt: A buyer wants to know why the demographics have changed in an area causing home prices to decline. The buyer wants to know if it is due to a certain race moving in. What is the best way to answer?
choices: Disclose whatever other information you have about the area.
Tell the buyer to go online and do their own research.
Tell the buyer you will get back to them with the information.
Tell the buyer you don't know anything about this area.
questions.explanation: It is a violation of federal Fair Housing laws to discuss changing demographics related to a certain race moving into the area. The licensee can disclose any other relevant information about the area.

questions.prompt: When a broker has a trust account, the name on the account must:
choices: Name each person who has money in the account as trustee
Name the broker's accountant as trustee
questions.explanation: A trust account must: 1) Designate the account as a trust account; 2) Name the broker as the trustee for the account; the broker may never delegate his/her accountability for the trust account.

questions.prompt: A landlord is trying to evict a tenant and serves an eviction notice. Under what circumstances could a tenant remain in the property?
choices: The tenant has not had hot water for months.
The lessor failed to repair a weak staircase.
questions.explanation: These are all examples of constructive eviction. When the landlord (lessor) engages in constructive eviction the tenant may move without giving the thirty day notice or may correct the situation by paying for the repair and deducting the bill from the rent. This is called "rental offset" and the tenant may do this twice in one 12 month period. The lessor may not evict a tenant if the problem is the lessor's fault.

questions.prompt: What is the Latin word for "buyer beware?"
questions.explanation: Caveat emptor is the Latin term that means "let the buyer beware."

questions.prompt: A hidden defect in the premises unknown to the landlord caused an injury to the tenant. Which of the following is CORRECT?
choices: Landlords are liable for injury caused by concealed and dangerous conditions that the landlord knows, or should know about.
Landlords are NOT responsible for unknown defects and thus cannot be held liable for injury or loss caused by such a defect.
Landlords are liable for defects they “should know” about but cannot be held liable for loss or damages.
As long as the tenant has renter’s insurance, the landlord is not liable for injury or loss due to unknown property defects.
questions.explanation: A landlord leasing dwellings and residential premises to tenants is strictly liable for injuries resulting from latent defects in the premises that exist at the time a lease is executed. Latent defects are concealed and dangerous conditions that a landlord knows, or should know, about. The Landlord is also liable for loss or damage suffered from a defect/disrepair if the Landlord knew or should have known about the defect/disrepair.

questions.prompt: A broker is representing a developer who has completed his project in a subdivision called "Ridgeway." The broker's advertisement states that people have "already won a free gift," but in reality, they must attend a sales seminar to receive the gift. This type of advertising is:
choices: Legal without disclosure of the sales seminar attendance requirement.
Legal, because all the "winners" purchased units anyway.
Legal, if the ad states they must sit through a sales seminar in order to collect the gift.
questions.explanation: When offering prizes or gifts, all requirements to be eligible to win must be stated in the advertisement.

questions.prompt: An advertisement is placed in a newspaper. According to the guidelines establised by the Department of Housing and Urban Development, which of the following phrases would be considered discriminatory?
questions.explanation: Ads may not be written which are aimed at only a certain group of persons. "Retiree's dream house" implies that only retired persons would be welcome and is considered discriminatory.

questions.prompt: A subdivider sold five 1-acre lots to Mr. Dalton and optioned five lots to Mr. Bernstein. What course of action does the subdivider have to take as a result of this action?
choices: Notify the Real Estate Commissioner of a material change
Nothing, but Mr. Dalton and Mr. Bernstein need to contact the Commissioner.
Notify the Commissioner of an intent to subdivide
Report the sale now and report the option when it is exercised by Mr. Bernstein.
questions.explanation: The Commissioner's Regulations state that if the owner of any subdivision options or sells five or more parcels to another, such option or sale constitutes a material change and the owner or original subdivider must immediately notify the Commissioner.

questions.prompt: If a business is sold without complying with the Bulk Sales Act:
choices: the assets still belong to the vendor as far as creditors are concerned.
the transfer is unenforceable by all parties.
questions.explanation: If the Bulk Sales Law is not complied with, creditors still have a claim on the assets of the vendor (seller) purchased by the vendee (buyer). This is why it is very important for the vendee (buyer) to see that the Bulk Sales Law is complied with.

questions.prompt: A subdivider may use the public report in their advertising as long as:
choices: they only use a picture of the report and not its verbiage.
they only reference certain applicable parts of the report.
they use the report in its entirety.
they receive permission to use specific parts of the report.
questions.explanation: A subdivider may use a public report in their advertising as long as they use it in full.

questions.prompt: A statement issued by the authorizing government agency that there will be no impact on the environment significant enough to warrant preparation of an EIR is called a:
questions.explanation: The authorizing government agency is authorized to issue a negative declaration if it determines that there will be no impact on the environment significant enough to warrant preparation of an EIR. Be careful, this one is easy to get backwards. Study Aid: Negative declaration = No impact.

questions.prompt: The transfer of privately owned land to the public under approval of the Map Act is called:
questions.explanation: Dedication is the transfer of privately owned land to the public with the intent that the land will be accepted and used for public use.

questions.prompt: A broker is handling the sale of a house for a seller. The broker gave the buyer the required disclosures. The disclosures failed to disclose something which was recorded with the county recorder. What kind of notice did the buyer receive?
questions.explanation: Recording a document gives constructive notice.

questions.prompt: With regard to the public report, which of the following would be considered a material change in a subdivision?
questions.explanation: Examples of material changes include physical changes, changes in contracts, or changes in deed restrictions. New ownership of the subdivison would also constitute a material change.

questions.prompt: As to running a business, which of the following is FALSE?
questions.explanation: Statement of fact. Remember, you are looking for the incorrect choice.

questions.prompt: When the real estate commissioner stops a real estate licensee from performing any act in real estate which requires a license, he would issue a(n):
questions.explanation: A Bar Order issued by the Real Estate Commissioner prohibits (debars) licensed or unlicensed persons from engaging in specified real estate related activities for a maximum period of 36 months.

questions.prompt: The most common violation of the Commissioner's Regulations concern:
questions.explanation: The DRE's Enforcement Section receives and processes a large number of complaints each year that are investigated and referred to the Department's Legal Section for disciplinary action. Trust fund handling and record keeping violations is the most common problem area. We see case after case in which brokers handle trust monies on behalf of others and either convert the monies to their own use, or do not have the expertise to maintain proper accounting records and end up with shortages in their trust accounts. To avoid problems in this area, all real estate brokers should be familiar with the laws and regulations that govern the handling of trust funds by real estate brokers.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT considered an operating expense?
questions.explanation:
Operating expenses are the costs of running and maintaining the property. Examples include:

- accounting and legal services
- advertising
- insurance premiums
- maintenance
- management fees
- property taxes
- repairs
- reserves and replacement
- supplies
- utilities

questions.prompt: When is the subdivider required to give the public report to prospective purchasers?
choices: prior to the sale of the last lot in a subdivision.
prior to the sale of the first lot in a subdivision.
prior to advertising the lots for sale.
prior to approval of the tentative map.
questions.explanation: No sales can be closed or transactions completed until the final public report is received by the prospective purchasers. All persons who make an offer to purchase based on a final public report must indicate in writing that they have received and read the applicable report.

questions.prompt: What percent of home buyers search online before contacting a real estate agent?
questions.explanation: According to a recent NAR survey, 90% of buyers used the internet as their first stop in house hunting.

questions.prompt: In the event the commissioner has conducted an audit which reflects commingling or conversion of trust funds in excess of $10,000, the court may:
choices: imprison the licensee for not more than thirty (30) days.
automatically revoke the violator's license without a formal hearing.
restrain the licensee from doing business pending a formal hearing.
confiscate any and all commissions earned by that licensee during the preceding calendar year.
questions.explanation: In the event the commissioner has conducted an audit which reflects commingling or conversion of trust funds in excess of ten thousand dollars ($10,000), the court may enter an order restraining the licensee from doing any act or acts in furtherance thereof, and from further exercising the privileges of his/her license pending further order of the court, provided that a hearing shall be held on the order within five days after the date thereof.

questions.prompt: All materials used in obtaining advance fee agreements must be submitted to the Real Estate Commissioner at least ____________ before they are used.
questions.explanation: The Real Estate Commissioner requires that any or all materials used in obtaining advance fee agreements, including but not limited to the contract forms, letters or cards used to solicit prospective sellers, and radio and television advertising be submitted to him or her at least 10 calendar days before they are used (B&P Code 10085).

questions.prompt: To comply with the Bulk Sales Act, publications of the sale must be made at least _________ prior to the sale in a paper of general circulation where the property is located.
questions.explanation: To comply with the Bulk Sales Act, a notice of sale must be published in a newspaper of general circulation within the judicial district on which the property is located at least 12 business days before the sale is consummated.

questions.prompt: When is it permissible for an unlicensed assistant to prepare a Comparative Market Analysis (CMA)?
choices: When an agent asks the assistant.
Subject to the approval of, and for use by, the licensee.
When the client needs it in a hurry and the agent is unavailable.
questions.explanation: According to the 2018 updated publication "Guidelines for Unlicensed Assistants who Work in the Real Estate Industry," an unlicensed assistants may make, conduct or prepare a comparative market analysis subject to the approval of, and for use by, the licensee. An unlicensed assistant cannot discuss the content, relevance, or significance of the CMA with the principal or any party to the transaction.

questions.prompt: A prospective real estate licensee passes the state exam and applies for a license, but the DRE does a background check and finds out that he is delinquent on his child support payments. Which of the following is CORRECT?
choices: His license will be granted even if he is in arrears with his child support.
He will be given a temporary 150-day license until a release is furnished to DRE from the District Attorney showing that he has met his child support obligation in full.
His license will be denied and he will never be able to obtain a license even if he pays his child support obligation in full.
His license will be denied and the DRE will turn his file over to the District Attorney.
questions.explanation:
In accordance with Section 17520 of the Family Code, DRE is precluded from issuing or renewing a full-term license if the applicant is on a list of persons (obligors) who have not complied with a court order to provide child support payments. The Department of Child Support Services compiles the list from information provided by the District Attorney of each county in California.

DRE will issue a 150-day license to an otherwise qualified applicant who is on the list of child support obligors. DRE will advise the applicant that the license applied for cannot be issued unless a release is furnished to DRE from the District Attorney's office during the 150 days.

DRE also receives a supplemental list of obligors who are over four months delinquent in child support payments. DRE compares this list to the total real estate licensee population. If there is a match of an existing licensee and the license is not due for renewal for at least six months, the licensee will be advised that the license will be suspended if the delinquency is not cleared within 150 days. The suspension will remain in effect until the delinquency is cleared.

questions.prompt: The real estate commissioner's authority to administer and enforce the real estate law is called:
questions.explanation: The real estate commissioner issues regulations (Commissioner's Regulations) to aid in the administration and enforcement of the real estate law.

questions.prompt: The seller is required to deliver the "Homeowner's Guide to Earthquake Safety" to the buyer of any one-to-four unit property built prior to:
questions.explanation: In addition to the earthquake disclosure requirements contained in Civil Code Section 1102 since 1991, sellers of one-to-four unit homes built before 1960 must deliver to the buyer, "as soon as practicable before the transfer", a copy of The Homeowner's Guide to Earthquake Safety and disclose certain earthquake deficiencies. The booklet contains a reporting form that may be used for this disclosure. The seller's real estate agent is to provide the seller of such a home with a copy of the booklet for delivery to the buyer.

questions.prompt: A Brownfield property that has been left vacant or is underutilized is most likely:
choices: depleted for crop use from overuse.
questions.explanation: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines a Brownfield as "real property, the expansion, redevelopment, or reuse of which may be complicated by the presence or potential presence of a hazardous substance, pollutant, or contaminant." Brownfields are often abandoned, closed or under-used industrial or commercial facilities, such as an abandoned factory in a town's former industrial section or a closed commercial building or warehouse in a suburban setting. Brownfields, however, can be located anywhere and can be quite small.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must be kept on file by the broker for three years?
choices: receipt for copy of public report
questions.explanation: The broker/subdivider must keep the receipt and make it available for inspection by the Commissioner for three years from the date it is signed. Do not confuse the public report (which is good for five years) with the receipt.

questions.prompt: Which of the following deals with public access to buildings?
questions.explanation: The American With Disabilities Act (ADA) deals with public access to buildings to make sure they are readily accessible to disabled individuals.

questions.prompt: A landlord and a tenant entered into a two year lease on commercial retail space. Three months into the lease, the tenant realizes he is unable to continue paying the rent and asks the landlord to release him from the lease. The landlord agrees. This would be considered a(n):
questions.explanation: Surrender occurs when both the landlord and tenant agree to allow a termination of the lease. There is no financial liability on either the landlord or the tenant.

questions.prompt: A deed has a provision regarding racial and religious discrimination. The deed may be changed:
choices: if the restrictions are discriminatory or offensive.
if a title company agrees the wording is discriminatory or offensive.
questions.explanation: Effective January 2000, a county recorder, title insurance company, escrow company, or real estate licensee who provide a declaration, governing documents, or deed to any person must provide a specified statement about the illegality of discriminatory restrictions and the right of the homeowners to have such language removed. The statement must be contained in either a cover page placed over the document or a stamp on the first page of the document.

questions.prompt: A real estate salesperson can sell:
choices: all mobile homes using a deed.
questions.explanation: Mobile homes that are registered with the Department of Motor Vehicles can be sold by a real estate licensee.

questions.prompt: When selling a business, real estate brokers need to know that the term successor's liability involves certain obligations to the:
questions.explanation: The term successor's liability refers to the purchaser's liability for the sales tax collected by the previous owner but not remitted to the state.

questions.prompt: The Subdivision Map Act requires:
questions.explanation: The Subdivision Map Act requires the subdivider to prepare and file a tentative map with the local planning commission.

questions.prompt: The Financial Discrimination Act of 1977, also known as the Holden Act, has to do with which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Holden Act prohibits state financial institutions from engaging in the practice of redlining. It is also known as the Housing Financial Discrimination Act of 1977.

questions.prompt: When budgeting for a real estate office, the phrase "company dollar" means:
choices: the money required to establish an office and run it for a given period of time.
the income of an office after all expenses are subtracted.
the income of an office after all commissions are subtracted.
questions.explanation: The term "company dollar" is the amount leftover after all commissions have been paid out.

questions.prompt: A material fact that must be disclosed to a purchaser would include all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: the racial composition of the neighborhood.
questions.explanation: The racial composition of a neighborhood is not considered a material fact. Discussing this with the purchaser may be considered a violation of fair housing laws.

questions.prompt: Sellers of target housing must disclose to potential purchasers the presence of any known lead-based paint hazards that affect homes built prior to:
questions.explanation: Sellers of homes built before 1978, and their agents, must disclose to potential purchasers the presence of any known lead-based paint hazards that affect the property. This law also applies to residential landlords and their tenants. "Target housing" means any housing constructed prior to 1978, except housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities (unless any child who is less than 6 years of age resides or is expected to reside in such housing) or any 0-bedroom dwelling. Also know that lead based paint laws went into effect in 1996.

questions.prompt: A broker takes a deposit check from a buyer and deposits it in his trust account. After the offer was accepted, the broker wrote a check from the trust account in the amount of the deposit and brought it to escrow. With regard to the broker's duty to maintain proper trust account records, the records must be retained for:
choices: three years from the date the broker deposited the buyer's check in the trust account.
three years from the the date escrow closes.
three years from the date escrow opened.
three years from the date of the offer to purchase.
questions.explanation: B&P Code Section 10148: Retention of Documents; (a) A licensed real estate broker shall retain for three years copies of all listings, deposit receipts, cancelled checks, trust records, and other documents executed by him/her or obtained in connection with any transactions for which a real estate broker license is required. The retention period shall run from the date of the closing of the transaction or from the date of the listing if the transaction is not consummated.

questions.prompt: An advance fee is:
choices: a bonus paid to the seller by an agent to obtain a listing.
a prepaid fee to cover advertising and promotional costs.
a gift to the listing broker.
questions.explanation: An "advance fee" is any fee paid before any services are rendered. Specifically, it is a practice of some brokers to obtain a nonrefundable fee from the seller in advance to cover advertising of properties or businesses for sale while giving no guarantee that a buyer will be found. Such agreements must be submitted and approved by the Real Estate Commissioner at least 10 calendar days prior to use.

questions.prompt: Mr. Wiseguy salesperson introduces himself to the seller as being employed by a large, successful real estate company because he knew that the seller would only list with a licensee who is employed by a "large company." If Mr. Wiseguy does not work for a large company, but he said it just to be able to sell the property, his conduct would be considered:
questions.explanation: Since many buyers and sellers associate "bigness with safety," it is considered unethical to represent one's self as being protected by a large corporation franchise when such is not true.

questions.prompt: When enforcing the Subdivision Lands Law, the Real Estate Commissioner is protecting purchasers from:
choices: the design of entrance and exit driveways.
energy consumption discrepancies that may cause outages.
fraud and misrepresentation in the marketing and financing of subdivisions.
questions.explanation: The Subdivision Lands Law (found in the Business and Professions Code) regulates the marketing and financing of the subdivision to protect prospective purchasers.

questions.prompt: A seller asks a broker about the race of an offeror. Which of the following is true?
choices: The broker may not answer the question.
The broker may answer the question, but must advise the seller that he is not allowed to discriminate based on that information.
The broker should suggest that the seller not use the services of a broker.
The broker must answer the question because he is an employee of the seller.
questions.explanation: The broker is not allowed to answer the question. The race of a buyer is not a material fact.

questions.prompt: If one uses the words "of definite duration" to describe a lease, it is most likely a(n):
questions.explanation: An estate for years always will have a definite termination date.

questions.prompt: One party sells property to another, and within the contract, the legal description is incorrect because of a simple typographical error. This can be corrected through a legal action called:
questions.explanation: Reformation is legal action necessary to correct or modify a contract or deed that has not accurately reflected the intentions of the parties, due to some mechanical error, such as a typographical error in the legal description or a misstated property value.

questions.prompt: A family rents a house from January 1st to June 30th. This is considered a(n):
questions.explanation: An estate for years is a leasehold created by landlord and tenant for a particular period of time. The period of time could be a fixed number of years, months, weeks, or even days. An estate for years always will have a definite termination date.

questions.prompt: What form is sent when a short sale is completed?
questions.explanation: The Short Sale Addendum (SSA) is a document specifically designed to deal with the unique circumstances that a short sale creates. The basic premise of the Short Sale Addendum is to set a deadline for the acceptance of the short sale by the lender and to delay the start of certain Contingency Periods within the Residential Purchase Agreement (RPA).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a "bona fide" purchaser?
choices: A person who inherits a parcel of property as a gift.
A buyer who innocently purchases a property, without having any prior knowledge that someone else may be able to claim the title to the property.
A buyer who purchases a property knowing full well that he/she cannot qualify for the necessary financing.
A buyer who induces a sale through fraudulent representations.
questions.explanation: The term "bona fide" means honest; genuine; actual; authentic; acting without the intention of defrauding. For example, a bona fide purchaser is one who purchases property for a valuable consideration that is inducement for entering into a contract and without suspicion of being defrauded or deceived by the seller. He or she has no notice of any defects of the title. A bona fide purchaser pays in good faith, full value for the property and, without any fraud or misrepresentation.

questions.prompt: A 17-year-old girl inherits a parcel of vacant land from her uncle. While still a minor, she deeds the land to her church which promptly builds on it. When she turns 18, she decides she wants the land back. In this case she:
choices: cannot get it back under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Most contracts, except those for necessities such as food and clothing, entered into by a minor are generally voidable at the minor's option. The minor must disaffirm the contract within a reasonable time after attaining legal age. If the minor does not disaffirm the contract within a reasonable time, it becomes fully enforceable. A minor may receive realty by gift or inheritance.

questions.prompt: When a lessee transfers all of his/her interest in the property, it is called a(n):
questions.explanation: An assignment of a lease is the transfer of all title, right, and interest that a lessee possesses in a certain property.

questions.prompt: A Bill of Sale is required to transfer personal property if the property sold for more than:
questions.explanation: A California Bill of Sale is a written record that documents the change in legal ownership of an item. A Bill of Sale is used only if an item is sold for more than $500.

questions.prompt: In which of the following ways is fraud different from misrepresentation?
choices: A misrepresentation is a deliberate attempt to deceive while fraud is not.
Fraud is a deliberate attempt to deceive while a misrepresentation is not.
There is no difference between fraud and misrepresentation.
A misrepresentation cannot result in discipline, and fraud will always involve discipline.
questions.explanation: Fraud involves a deliberate attempt to deceive, misrepresentation does not. A licensee may be disciplined for either fraud or misrepresentation.

questions.prompt: A net leasing agreement would require the lessee to pay his share of all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: With a net lease, the lessee (tenant) not only pays the rent for occupancy but also pays maintenance and operating expenses such as taxes, insurance, utilities, maintenance, and repairs. The lessor (owner) would pay the leasing commission. In a true net lease, the tenant is responsible for expenses relating to the premises exactly as if the tenant were the owner. The rent paid is "net" to the lessor. This kind of lease is popular with investors who want to obtain a steady stream of income without having to handle the problems associated with management and maintenance. Commercial or industrial leases, ground leases, and long-term leases are typically net leases.

questions.prompt: Most real estate contracts contain preprinted clauses or spaces for information to be added in writing. In the interpretation of such contracts:
choices: Printed parts take precedence over the written parts.
The written parts and the printed parts are given equal consideration.
The written parts take precedence over the printed parts.
No changes or amendments to the printed clauses are permitted by law.
questions.explanation: Written parts always take precedence over the preprinted parts.

questions.prompt: A recorded legal document that gives constructive notice that an action affecting a particular piece of property has been filed in a state or federal court is called a(n):
questions.explanation: A lis pendens is a recorded legal document that gives constructive notice (in other words, a warning) to potential purchasers of a property that an action affecting a particular piece of property has been filed in a state or federal court. Lis pendens is Latin for "action pending." If they choose to purchase it, they are buying it subject to the outcome of that lawsuit. The lis pendens is also a form of protection to the person or entity that files it. It means that even if the property is sold, they do not automatically lose their claim to title. The lawsuit still must be resolved, and the new owner is subject to the results of that suit every bit as much as the person who sold it would have been.

questions.prompt: A listing agreement is:
questions.explanation: A listing agreement is an employment agreement between an owner of property and the real estate broker authorizing the broker to find a buyer for the property. They are also bilateral contracts in that the seller promises to pay the broker a commission when the property sells and the broker promises to make reasonable efforts to obtain a purchaser.

questions.prompt: Net listings are illegal in many states. Which of the following states allows net listings?
questions.explanation: A Net Listing is a listing based on the net price the seller will receive if the property is sold. Under a net listing the broker can offer the property for sale at the highest price obtainable to increase the commission. This type of listing is legal in California but considered unethical and thus illegal in most states.

questions.prompt: An agent acquired a listing for a house and orally promised to hold an open house every week until the house was sold. The agent failed to hold them as promised. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Constructive fraud is a breach of duty as by a person in a fiduciary capacity, without an actual fraudulent intent. Actual fraud is an act intended to deceive another; e.g., making a false statement or false promise without intending to perform it.

questions.prompt: The broker's promise to use diligence in finding a buyer:
choices: makes the listing a unilateral contract.
makes the listing voidable by the owner.
makes the listing a bilateral contract.
questions.explanation: A bilateral contract is a contract in which each party promises to perform an act in exchange for the other party's promise to perform. An exclusive listing is an example of a bilateral contract with the broker agreeing to use his/her best efforts (diligence) to locate a ready, willing and able buyer, and the seller promising to pay the broker a commission if the property is sold.

questions.prompt: All of the following listings require that the broker be the "procuring cause" of the sale if he/she is to be entitled to a commission, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Under an Exclusive Authorization and Right to Sell Listing, the listing broker is entitled to a commission if the property sells through the efforts of the broker or any other person. The broker is not required to produce a buyer or be the procuring cause to be entitled to a commission.

questions.prompt: Where does information governing the use of electronic signatures (eSigning) NOT exist?
choices: Federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (“ESIGN Act”)
questions.explanation: The Federal Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act (“ESIGN Act”) generally provides that electronic records and signatures have the same validity and effect as original signatures with regard to transactions in or affecting interstate commerce. Many states, including California, have adopted a parallel law, the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (“UETA”), which authorizes electronic records and signatures as a matter of state law. Article 8 and 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code (“UCC”) both permit the use of electronic records and signatures for most purposes.

questions.prompt: A listing with an effective date of March 12th and expiring on April 12th is for:
questions.explanation: You must include all the days in this count. If this doesn't make sense, count the days on a calendar.

questions.prompt: Broker Jones takes an exclusive listing on a property owned by three different people. Broker Jones takes the listing contract to each of their places of business to get it signed. Broker Jones must:
choices: give a copy to the first owner who signs only.
give a copy to each owner when he/she signs.
give one copy to any of the three owners.
get them together in one place to sign at the same time.
questions.explanation: When there are multiple owners, the broker is required to provide a copy of the listing contract to each owner when they sign.

questions.prompt: The Statute of Frauds, outlines what contracts must be in writing to be enforceable through court action. Which of the following contracts would be enforceable?
choices: A verbal lease for one year or less
A verbal listing to secure a loan of $1,500
An exclusive listing taken orally by a broker to sell a single-family residence
An oral agreement to pay a broker a commission for the negotiation of an exchange of two businesses
questions.explanation: The Statute of Frauds is state law that requires certain contracts to be in writing and signed by the party to be charged (or held) to the agreement in order to be legally enforceable. The Statute of Frauds generally requires that all contracts for the sale of land or any interest herein be in writing. Oral leases for a period not exceeding one year, however are generally valid and enforceable.

questions.prompt: A lease contains an assignment clause requiring the consent of the landlord. If the lessee assigns the lease without approval, the assignment is:
